# sheetpane — the full public contract

> Everything llms.txt links to, inlined: the package READMEs, the docs, the laws and the component records. Version 0.3.0; links pinned to v0.3.0.

### Open, edit and review `.xlsx` and `.csv` files inside your web app.<br>Nothing is uploaded. Download gives back the original file, with only your edits patched in.

---

## Three lines of HTML

```html
<script type="module">import '@sheetpane/grid';</script>

<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" src="holdings.xlsx" mode="edit" rules-src="rules.json"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3"></sheetpane-errors>
```

**That is the whole integration.** A spreadsheet, an error list, kept in sync by
the shared `pane` id — put them side by side, in tabs, or in a dialog.

---

## Why sheetpane

|  |  |
|---|---|
| 🔒 **Private by construction** | The file is read, edited and checked in the browser tab. sheetpane sends nothing to any server — no file, cell, edit or telemetry ([law L11](records/0013_LAW-11-workbook-stays-in-the-browser.md), checked by a test). |
| 📄 **The file survives the round trip** | Untouched → back **byte for byte**. Edited → the original with only the changed cells patched in. |
| ✅ **Review built in** | Errors are flagged on the cell *and* listed beside the sheet — from a JSON rules file, your own column rules, or the workbook's own validation. |
| ⚡ **Big files stay smooth** | A 250,000-row CSV scrolls with **0 dropped frames** (measured in headless Chromium on a MacBook — not a promise for your hardware). |
| 🧩 **Pay for what you use** | Formulas, styles, charts, images and more are opt-in plugins — you ship only what you import. |
| 🎨 **Looks like your app** | No font of its own — it inherits yours. Light, dark or auto. |

---

## Fix it in place

Edit a flagged cell and its error resolves in the panel — every change held in
memory until you download.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/readme/demo.gif" alt="Typing a missing advisor, a positive unit count and an approved fee rate; each error in the panel turns green as resolved" width="100%">
</p>

The rules behind it are [this JSON file](docs/readme/holdings.rules.json), with a [schema](packages/grid/README.md#rules-file) your editor completes:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "sheets": { "Holdings": { "headerRow": 2, "columns": {
    "Advisor":  { "required": true },
    "Units":    { "type": "integer", "min": 0 },
    "Fee rate": { "oneOf": ["0.40%", "0.75%", "0.85%"] },
    "As of":    { "type": "date", "min": "2026-09-01", "max": "2026-09-30", "severity": "warning" }
  } } }
}
```

## Get started

> [!NOTE]
> **`0.1.0` is about to ship.** Until it is on npm, the install commands and the
> playground links will not work yet.

```sh
npm install @sheetpane/grid
```

Then follow the [`@sheetpane/grid` guide](packages/grid/README.md). Or try it
first: the [playground](https://arpitarya.github.io/sheetpane/), its
[React version](https://arpitarya.github.io/sheetpane/react/), or a
[starter in StackBlitz](examples/starters/README.md).

---

## Works where you work

The elements are standard web components, so they render in any framework — or
none. **No wrapper packages**; one `import type` line gives typed tags, props
and events.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Plain HTML** | `import '@sheetpane/grid'` — no build step needed |
| **React 19 / 18** | typed JSX, plus [copy-in hooks](packages/grid/README.md#react-hooks-recipes) (`useSelection`, `useErrors`, `useChanges`…) |
| **Vue · Svelte · Solid · Angular** | [one line of setup each](packages/grid/README.md#vue-svelte-solid-angular) |
| **Your tests** | [`@sheetpane/testing`](packages/testing/README.md) — locators and actions for Playwright and Vitest |
| **Your AI agent** | [skills](packages/skills/README.md) for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex · a read-only [MCP server](packages/mcp/README.md) · [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) |

---

## Plugins

**Opt-in, one import each.** Ship only what your users need.

| plugin | adds |
|---|---|
| [`numfmt`](packages/numfmt/README.md) | every Excel number format, with locales |
| [`formulas`](packages/formulas/README.md) | recalculation as you edit — IronCalc, WebAssembly, lazy-loaded |
| [`styles`](packages/styles/README.md) | fills, fonts, borders, alignment, merges |
| [`condfmt`](packages/condfmt/README.md) | conditional formatting, colour scales, data bars |
| [`validation`](packages/validation/README.md) | the workbook's own data-validation rules |
| [`charts`](packages/charts/README.md) | bar, column, line, pie, doughnut and scatter |
| [`images`](packages/images/README.md) | pictures anchored in the sheet |
| [`comments`](packages/comments/README.md) | notes and threaded comments, read and written |
| [`visibility`](packages/visibility/README.md) | hide, unhide and group rows, columns and sheets |
| [`tables`](packages/tables/README.md) | Excel tables drawn in their style — header, bands, totals |
| [`compare`](packages/compare/README.md) | what changed since a base version — tinted, summed up, stepped through; `diffWorkbooks` headless |
| [`review`](packages/review/README.md) | the review as a sheet in the download, flagged cells filled |

```html
<script type="module">import '@sheetpane/grid'; import '@sheetpane/formulas/ui';</script>
<sheetpane-excel src="model.xlsx" plugins="formulas"></sheetpane-excel>
```

---

## The editing basics, included

Typing and paste · undo/redo · range selection with Count · Sum · Average ·
find · zoom · freeze panes · resize rows and columns · hidden rows, columns and
sheets · a pop-up mode · keyboard and touch.

---

## What it deliberately does not do

**XLSX and CSV only** ([law L3](records/0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md)).
Anything else is refused with a clear message — never half-read.

| not supported | what happens |
|---|---|
| `.xls`, `.xlsm`, `.xlsb`, `.ods`, `.numbers` | refused, with the reason |
| macros, password-protected files | detected and refused |
| sending your file anywhere | never — sheetpane makes no upload, beacon or telemetry call ([law L11](records/0013_LAW-11-workbook-stays-in-the-browser.md)); its only requests are the GETs for the `src` and `rules-src` you set |
| real-time collaboration, storage | the workbook lives in memory; saving it is your app's job |
| pivot tables | shown as their values, with a badge — not recalculated |

---

## How far it is proven

**Every feature has tests**, in Node and a real browser: Chromium on every
change; Chromium, Firefox and WebKit nightly. Both demos are driven end to end —
also from the packed tarballs npm would publish.

<details>
<summary><b>The honest gaps</b> — tracked in <a href="work/OPEN-WORK.md"><code>OPEN-WORK</code></a></summary>

<br>

- **Files saved by real apps.** The reader is tested on generated and
  library-written files; not yet on files saved by Excel, Google Sheets,
  LibreOffice and Numbers (W-30).
- **The round trip in desktop Excel.** Exports are read back by independent
  libraries in CI; opening them in Excel is still a manual check.
- **Phones.** Touch selection and download are built, not yet checked on a real
  iPhone.

Until 1.0 the API may change between minor versions — the
[CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) says when.

</details>

**Found a file that opens wrongly?** [Open an issue](https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/issues/new)
with the file (or a minimal copy) attached — it is the most useful thing you can send.

---

## Packages

**One version for all**, ESM with types.

| package | what it is |
|---|---|
| [`@sheetpane/grid`](packages/grid/README.md) | the two web components, the pane's workbook, the plugin host |
| [`@sheetpane/import`](packages/import/README.md) | `.xlsx` / `.csv` in, a plain JavaScript workbook out |
| [`@sheetpane/export`](packages/export/README.md) | a workbook in, `.xlsx` / `.csv` out — build, patch the original, `download()` |
| [`@sheetpane/testing`](packages/testing/README.md) | locators and actions for Playwright and Vitest browser mode |
| [`@sheetpane/fixtures`](packages/fixtures/README.md) | known workbooks for your tests |
| [`@sheetpane/skills`](packages/skills/README.md) | agent skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex |
| [`@sheetpane/mcp`](packages/mcp/README.md) | a read-only MCP server: the API, and workbook inspection |

**Dependencies:** none at runtime outside the project, except the engines two
plugins use — [`numfmt`](https://github.com/borgar/numfmt) and
[IronCalc](https://github.com/ironcalc/IronCalc). Every dependency is free and
open source ([law L2](records/0004_LAW-2-foss-dependencies.md)).

---

## Contributing

**Welcome — especially failing files and bug reports.** You need **Node 22+**,
**pnpm 10** and [**just**](https://just.systems).

```sh
just install     # pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
just check       # type-check, test (Node + Chromium) and build
just demo-html   # the plain HTML demo at http://127.0.0.1:5173
```

<details>
<summary><b>Every command</b></summary>

<br>

| command | does |
|---|---|
| `just test-pkg <name>` | one package's tests, e.g. `just test-pkg grid` |
| `just test-browsers` | the browser suites in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit |
| `just demo-react` | the React 19 demo at http://127.0.0.1:5174 |
| `just demo-check` | both demos driven end to end in Chromium |
| `just pack-check` | every package packed as npm would publish it, and checked |
| `just release <version>` | bump every package together, check, push; a GitHub Release publishes ([RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md)) |

</details>

**How the project is run.** Every rule lives in one record under
[`records/`](records/README.md); the live queue is
[`work/OPEN-WORK.md`](work/OPEN-WORK.md); the map is
[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Much of the code was written by
AI coding agents working under those records — **the tests, not the prose, are
the evidence**. Start at [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) if you are one.

<!-- source: packages/grid/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/grid/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/grid

**View and edit `.xlsx` and `.csv` files inside any web page, and review them.**
Two web components, always in sync through one in-memory workbook:

- `<sheetpane-excel>` — the sheet. View or Edit; every change stays in memory;
  **Download** hands back the file — as opened when nothing changed, else a
  copy of the uploaded file with the changes in it.
- `<sheetpane-errors>` — the errors flagged on the sheet: what's wrong, what it
  should be. Put it anywhere — beside the sheet, in a side column, in another tab.

Nothing is uploaded: the file is read in the browser tab. No framework inside
or outside; no font of its own — yours is used.

```sh
pnpm add @sheetpane/grid      # or npm / yarn
```

Try it first in the [live playground](https://arpitarya.github.io/sheetpane/) or
open a [starter in StackBlitz](https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/main/examples/starters/README.md)
(from the first published release).

## Plain HTML

```html
<script type="module">import '@sheetpane/grid';</script>

<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" src="/files/holdings.xlsx" mode="edit" author="Arpit" style="height:640px"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3" author="Arpit" style="height:640px"></sheetpane-errors>
```

The same `pane` id links them. Mount order does not matter, and they may sit
in different containers, tabs or dialogs.

## React 19

React 19 sets properties and listens to custom events on custom elements
natively:

```tsx
import '@sheetpane/grid';

export function Review({ file }: { file: File }) {
  return (
    <>
      <sheetpane-excel pane="q3" mode="edit" file={file} onsheetpane-change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} />
      <sheetpane-errors pane="q3" onsheetpane-errors={(e) => save(e.detail.errors)} />
    </>
  );
}
```

**Typed JSX:** add `import type {} from '@sheetpane/grid/jsx';` once — e.g. in
a `sheetpane.d.ts` beside your sources — and both tags, their attributes,
properties and `onsheetpane-…` props are typed, payloads included
(`e.detail.ref`). See [Typings and editor support](#typings-and-editor-support).

**React 18** sets attributes only: use a `ref` for properties and events.

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLElement & { file?: File }>(null);
useEffect(() => {
  const el = ref.current!;
  el.file = file;
  const on = (e: Event) => save((e as CustomEvent).detail.errors);
  el.addEventListener('sheetpane-errors', on);
  return () => el.removeEventListener('sheetpane-errors', on);
}, [file]);
return <sheetpane-excel ref={ref} pane="q3" />;
```

### React hooks (recipes)

Not a package (SR-LAW-4: no framework wrappers in v1) — copy
[`examples/react/src/sheetpane-hooks.ts`](../../examples/react/src/sheetpane-hooks.ts)
into your app. Each hook takes a `ref` to `<sheetpane-excel>`, is built on
`useSyncExternalStore` with a stable selector (a component re-renders only
when what it reads changes), removes its listeners on unmount, and is safe
under StrictMode. React 19 and 18.

```tsx
const sheet = useRef<SheetpaneExcel>(null);
const sel = useSelection(sheet);         // { sheet, ref, range, column: { index, letter, header }, value, text }
const edit = useCellEdit(sheet);         // { editing, ref, column, draft } while the user types
const { count, canUndo } = useChanges(sheet);
const { errors, open } = useErrors(sheet);
const wb = useWorkbook(sheet);           // the pane's store
const rules = useColumnRules(sheet, { Age: { type: 'integer', min: 18 } }); // { checking, done, total }
useSheetpaneEvent(sheet, 'sheetpane-beforechange', (e) => { if (Number(e.detail.now) < 0) e.preventDefault(); });
return <sheetpane-excel ref={sheet} pane="r1" mode="edit" src="people.xlsx" />;
```

The primitive under all of them, for a hook of your own:

```ts
const units = useSheetpane(sheet, (store) => store.value('Holdings', 'F3'), null);
```

## Vue, Svelte, Solid, Angular

The elements are standard custom elements, so every framework renders them
once `import '@sheetpane/grid'` has run in the browser. No wrapper package;
an `import type` line types them.

**Vue 3** — tell the compiler the tags are custom elements, then bind
properties with `.prop` and listen with `@`:

```js
// vite.config.js
vue({ template: { compilerOptions: { isCustomElement: (tag) => tag.startsWith('sheetpane-') } } })
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import '@sheetpane/grid';
import type {} from '@sheetpane/grid/vue';   // GlobalComponents: props and @sheetpane-… typed
</script>
<template>
  <sheetpane-excel pane="q3" mode="edit" :file.prop="file" @sheetpane-change="(e) => log(e.detail.ref)" />
  <sheetpane-errors pane="q3" @sheetpane-errors="(e) => save(e.detail.errors)" />
</template>
```

**Svelte** — `import type {} from '@sheetpane/grid/svelte';` once (e.g. in
`src/app.d.ts`); Svelte 5 listens with `onsheetpane-change={…}`, Svelte 4 with
`on:sheetpane-change={…}`; both set properties when the element has one.

```svelte
<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" mode="edit" file={file} onsheetpane-change={(e) => log(e.detail.ref)}></sheetpane-excel>
```

**Solid** — `import type {} from '@sheetpane/grid/solid';` once. Solid sets a
custom element's props as properties, so write an attribute that has no
property with `attr:`, and listen with `on:`:

```tsx
<sheetpane-excel attr:pane="q3" attr:header-row="2" mode="edit" prop:file={file()} on:sheetpane-change={(e) => log(e.detail.ref)} />
```

**Angular** — no package and no typings to import: add
`CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA` to the component that renders the tags, bind
properties with `[…]` and events with `(…)`:

```ts
import { Component, CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA } from '@angular/core';
import '@sheetpane/grid';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-review',
  standalone: true,
  schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA],
  template: `
    <sheetpane-excel pane="q3" mode="edit" [file]="file" (sheetpane-change)="onChange($event)"></sheetpane-excel>
    <sheetpane-errors pane="q3" (sheetpane-errors)="save($event.detail.errors)"></sheetpane-errors>`,
})
export class ReviewComponent { file: File | null = null; onChange(e: Event) { console.log((e as CustomEvent).detail); } save(errors: unknown[]) {} }
```

**Next.js and other SSR** — the import is safe on the server (the elements
just do not register); render the tags in a client component.

## Typings and editor support

| file | for |
|---|---|
| `@sheetpane/grid/custom-elements.json` | the [Custom Elements Manifest](https://github.com/webcomponents/custom-elements-manifest) (schema 2.1.0): every attribute, property, method, event (with its payload type), slot, CSS part and `--sp-*` property; `package.json`'s `customElements` points at it |
| `@sheetpane/grid/jsx` | React 19 — `React.JSX.IntrinsicElements` |
| `@sheetpane/grid/vue` | Vue 3 — `GlobalComponents` (Volar / vue-tsc) |
| `@sheetpane/grid/svelte` | Svelte 4 and 5 — `SvelteHTMLElements` |
| `@sheetpane/grid/solid` | Solid — `JSX.IntrinsicElements` |
| `@sheetpane/grid/vscode.html-custom-data.json` | VS Code: tags, attributes and their values in `.html` |
| `@sheetpane/grid/vscode.css-custom-data.json` | VS Code: the `--sp-*` properties in `.css` |
| `@sheetpane/grid/web-types.json` | JetBrains IDEs (WebStorm, IntelliJ) — read automatically through `package.json`'s `web-types` |

Each typing entry is types only (`import type {} from '…'`); the framework is
never a dependency. Each also exports the element types it builds on —
`SheetpaneExcelEventMap`, `SheetpaneExcelAttributes`,
`SheetpaneExcelProperties` and the same for `SheetpaneErrors` — for typing
your own wrappers.

**VS Code** — point the workspace settings at the editor data:

```json
// .vscode/settings.json
{
  "html.customData": ["./node_modules/@sheetpane/grid/dist/vscode.html-custom-data.json"],
  "css.customData": ["./node_modules/@sheetpane/grid/dist/vscode.css-custom-data.json"]
}
```

All of it is generated from the element sources and their TSDoc
(`scripts/build-manifest.mjs`, run by the build); a test fails when the
committed manifest drifts from the elements.

## `<sheetpane-excel>`

| kind | name | what |
|---|---|---|
| attribute | `pane` | the shared id; the same on both elements |
| attribute | `src` | a URL (read with a GET), a `data:` URL or base64 |
| attribute | `mode` | `view` (default) or `edit` |
| attribute | `display` | `tab` (default; fills its container) or `popup` (a modal dialog; `open` shows it) |
| attribute | `open` | shows the pop-up |
| attribute | `author` | written on errors flagged here |
| attribute | `plugins` | the enabled plugin ids, e.g. `numfmt formulas` |
| attribute | `header-row` | the row holding column titles (default `1`) — every event names the column by it, and column rules match by it |
| attribute | `theme` | `light` (default), `dark` or `auto` (follows the page's `prefers-color-scheme`) |
| attribute / property | `ref` | the cell or range selected once a file is read, scrolled into view: `B4`, `Data!B4`, `'Q3 data'!B4:D8` — see [Opening at a cell](#opening-at-a-cell-and-links) |
| attribute / property | `link` | `none` (default) or `hash`: the selection kept in the URL fragment, and *Copy link* in the cell menu |
| attribute / property | `on-invalid` / `onInvalid` | what a failing column rule does by default: `flag` (default) or `block` |
| attribute / property | `rules-src` / `rules` | a rules file by URL, or as an object — see [Rules file](#rules-file) |
| attribute / property | `flagging` | `on` (default) or `off`: no Flag issue, no composer, no pop-up card — errors are read in `<sheetpane-errors>` |
| attribute / property | `results` | `summary` (default), `marks` or `off` — how passed and not-checked cells show, pane-wide; see [Results](#results-passed-and-not-checked) |
| attribute / property | `protection` | `honour` (default) or `ignore` — whether a protected sheet's locked cells refuse edits, pane-wide; see [Protected sheets](#protected-sheets) |
| property | `columns`, `validate` | column rules by title, and a check function — see [Column rules](#column-rules) |
| property | `file` | a `File`, `Blob`, `ArrayBuffer` or `Uint8Array` to read |
| property | `workbook` | the pane's store (get, or set your own from `createWorkbook()`) |
| property | `errors`, `errorTypes` | the review; the error-type catalog |
| property | `renderDetail` | your extra detail in the error card (W-68, under *Saving and restoring a review*) |
| attribute / property | `layers` | the review layers shown, space-separated — the pane's, shared with `<sheetpane-errors>`; none shows every layer (W-51, under *Saving and restoring a review*) |
| method | `load(src, name?)` | read a file (any of the above) |
| method | `export(options?, { format? })` | `Promise<Blob>` — the upload with every change; `format: 'csv'` from an `.xlsx` is the current sheet, `'xlsx'` from a `.csv` one sheet |
| method | `select(sheet, ref)`, `getErrors({ layer? })`, `setErrors(list or envelope, { layer? })`, `undo()`, `redo()` | |
| method | `highlight(ranges, { tone, label, sheet, pinned, reveal }?)`, `clearHighlight()` | outline cells without selecting them — and `sheetpane-hover` — see *Pointing at cells* under [Following an edit](#following-an-edit) |
| event | `sheetpane-load` (`{ status: 'ready', name, kind, sheets, readMs, sha256 }`), `sheetpane-errors {v, errors, plugins, layers, changed}`, `sheetpane-layers {visible, layers}`, `sheetpane-mode {mode}`, `sheetpane-history`, `sheetpane-export {blob, kind, name, format, converted, sha256, original?}` (cancelable — prevent it to save the file yourself; `original: true` when Download hands back the untouched file, `converted` when ▾ chose the other format), `sheetpane-close` — `sha256` is the SHA-256 of the file opened / the blob handed back, `undefined` without Web Crypto (SP-1009) | bubbling, composed |

### Following an edit

Every edit fires these, in this order, on the element where it happened;
every payload names the column `{ index, letter, header }` (the title from
`header-row`):

| event | fires | detail | cancel it to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sheetpane-select` | the selected cell moves | `{sheet, ref, column, value}` | — |
| `sheetpane-editstart` | the cell bar opens on a cell | `{sheet, ref, column, value, richText?}` — `richText: true` on a rich-text cell, whose edit saves plain text | keep the cell read-only |
| `sheetpane-input` | each keystroke, before saving | `{sheet, ref, column, draft, was}` | — |
| `sheetpane-beforechange` | Enter, Tab, blur, Delete, or each cell of a paste | `{sheet, ref, column, was, now}` | refuse the value |
| `sheetpane-change` | after saving | `{sheet, ref, kind, was, now}` (an insert or delete: `kind: 'structure'`, `op`, `at`, `count`) | — |
| `sheetpane-editcancel` | Esc, a column rule set to `block` refused the value, or the cell is locked on a protected sheet | `{sheet, ref}` (refused: `{sheet, ref, reason: 'blocked', code: 'SP-6003', message}`; locked: `{sheet, ref, reason: 'locked', code: 'SP-3026', message: 'Locked in the file'}`) | — |
| `sheetpane-sheet` | the sheet tab changes | `{sheet}` | — |

A refused value never reaches the change map, undo or a plugin.

```js
excel.addEventListener('sheetpane-beforechange', (e) => {
  if (e.detail.column.header === 'Units' && Number(e.detail.now) < 0) e.preventDefault();
});
```

**Keys:** arrows, Shift+arrows, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End, PageUp/PageDown;
Enter or F2 edits; typing replaces; Delete clears; Ctrl/⌘+V pastes tab-separated cells; **F flags an issue**;
**right-click, Shift+F10 or the Menu key** opens the selection actions (Flag issue, Copy ref, Copy link with
`link="hash"`, Copy value and plugin actions) under the cell — the same actions sit at the right end of the cell bar, never over the cells; Esc
cancels or closes the pop-up; Ctrl/⌘+Z undo, Ctrl+Y / ⌘+Shift+Z redo. The `?`
button lists them, plugins' shortcuts included.

**Selecting a range:** drag (the grid scrolls when the pointer reaches an edge), Shift+click, or click a
column header, row header or the corner — drag or Shift+click headers for several. Ctrl/⌘+arrow jumps to
the edge of the data (with Shift: selects to it); Ctrl+Space selects the column, Shift+Space the row,
Ctrl/⌘+A the data and then the sheet; Shift+Backspace goes back to the active cell; Enter and Tab move
inside a range. On a range, Ctrl/⌘+C copies it so Excel and Google Sheets paste a grid, Delete clears it
(Edit, one undo step), one pasted value fills it, and the status line shows **Count · Sum · Average**.
`sheetpane-select` carries `range` (`B3:D8`) and fires once a drag is released. On a touch screen a finger
scrolls, a tap selects, and a range shows two handles to extend it.

**Resizing:** drag a column header's right edge or a row header's bottom edge; double-click it to fit the
text; with several whole columns or rows selected, one drag or fit sizes them all. Right-click a header (or
Shift+F10 with a whole column or row selected) for *Fit to data*, *Column width…* and *Reset*. Rows keep the
file's heights. Sizes are a view setting, like zoom — not a change, not in the download; save and restore
them with the `sizes` property and the `sheetpane-resize` event:

```js
excel.addEventListener('sheetpane-resize', () => localStorage.setItem('sizes', JSON.stringify(excel.sizes)));
excel.sizes = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('sizes') ?? '{}'); // { Sheet1: { cols: { B: 120 }, rows: { 4: 40 } } }
```

**Inserting and deleting rows and columns (Edit):** the cell menu and the ⋯ menu offer *Insert row above /
below*, *Insert column left / right*, *Delete row* and *Delete column* (with counts for a range); a header
menu offers its axis's three. Ctrl/⌘+Shift+= inserts rows above (columns left when whole columns are
selected); Ctrl/⌘+− deletes whole rows or columns. Everything that points at a cell moves — values, edits,
errors, formulas on every sheet (`#REF!` for a deleted target), merges, validations, conditional formats,
notes, pictures and charts, hidden and grouped rows, freeze, sizes — and the download carries it. Each is one
undo step and one `sheetpane-change` with `kind: 'structure'`, `op`, `at` (0-based) and `count`. What Excel
refuses is refused, greyed with its reason: the file's protection — a protected structure, or a protected
sheet without *Insert rows* / *Delete rows* / *Insert columns* / *Delete columns* (`SP-3026`) — a delete that
splits a merged range (`SP-3022`), anything that
would move a pivot table or its source (`SP-3023`), cells pushed off the sheet (`SP-3024`), a table cut
(`SP-3025`). A host drives the same through the store:

```js
const book = excel.workbook;
if (!book.structureRefusal({ sheet: 'Spec', op: 'insertRows', at: 4, count: 1 })) book.insertRows('Spec', 4); // above row 5
book.deleteCols('Spec', 2, 2); // C and D
```

**Pointing at cells from outside (W-56):** `sheetpane-hover` names the cell under a mouse or pen pointer —
`{sheet, ref, column}`, a merge by its top-left, at most once per frame and only when the cell changes —
and `null` when the pointer leaves the cells; a finger never hovers. `highlight(ranges, options?)` outlines
cells without selecting them: `B3`, `B3:D8`, `Data!B3` or `{ ref, sheet?, tone? }`, in `tone` `info`
(default), `pass` or `fail`. The outline lets the pointer through; it is not a change, not undone, not in the
download. Each call replaces the last; a sheet switch clears it unless `pinned: true`, and so does a new
file; `reveal: true` scrolls the first range into view; a `label` is shown in the status line and said once
by screen readers. It returns how many ranges it outlined (a bad ref or a missing sheet is skipped);
`clearHighlight()` removes it. Together they make "hover a box, its cell lights up — hover a cell, its box
does":

```js
excel.addEventListener('sheetpane-hover', (e) => pdf.outline(e.detail && boxFor(e.detail.ref))); // null: none
pdf.onHover = (box) => (box ? excel.highlight(box.cell, { tone: box.ok ? 'pass' : 'fail', label: box.name }) : excel.clearHighlight());
```

### Opening at a cell, and links

`ref` opens the file at a cell — the selection once it is read, scrolled into view; set later, it selects
then. A cell or range, with or without its sheet (`B4`, `Data!B4`, `'Q3 data'!B4:D8`). One that names no
cell warns `SP-3019` in the console and the sheet opens at A1.

```html
<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" src="/files/q3.xlsx" ref="Data!F9"></sheetpane-excel>
```

`link="hash"` keeps the selection in the URL, so a reload or a shared link opens at the same cell, and adds
*Copy link* to the cell menu. It is off by default. Only one parameter of the fragment is sheetpane's —
`sheetpane=<pane>:<Sheet>!<ref>` — and the rest is left as it was: after a hash router's path it goes with
`?` (`#/reports/12?sheetpane=q3:Data!F9`), after an anchor or your own parameters with `&`. It is written
with `history.replaceState` once the selection settles — no history entry, no `hashchange` for your router
— and read when a file is read and on back and forward. A link wins over `ref`. Give each sheet its own
`pane` when a page has two. The fragment never leaves the browser: it is not part of any request.

**React, Vue and Solid** keep `ref` for their own refs, so their typings leave it out. Set it from a ref
callback, or call `select()` once the file is read:

```jsx
<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" src={url} ref={(el) => el?.setAttribute('ref', 'Data!F9')} />
<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" src={url} onsheetpane-load={(e) => e.detail.status === 'ready' && e.currentTarget.select('Data', 'F9')} />
```

## Column rules

Check what a user types, by column title. Rules are plain JSON — save and load
them as a file if you like — and failures go into the one error list as
`author: "host"` errors that resolve themselves when the cell passes.

```js
excel.columns = {
  Name:   { required: true },
  Email:  { pattern: '^[^@\\s]+@[^@\\s]+\\.[a-z]{2,}$', unique: true },
  Age:    { type: 'integer', min: 18, max: 99, onInvalid: 'block' },
  Status: { oneOf: ['Active', 'Inactive'], severity: 'warning' },
};
excel.validate = async (ctx, signal) =>
  ctx.column.header === 'Email' && ctx.phase !== 'input' && (await api.taken(ctx.value, { signal }))
    ? { severity: 'error', message: 'Email already used' }
    : null;
```

| rule | passes when |
|---|---|
| `required` | the cell is not blank (every other rule skips a blank cell) |
| `type` | `text` · `number` · `integer` · `date` · `boolean` |
| `min`, `max` | a number in range; for `type: 'date'`, an ISO date or a serial |
| `minLength`, `maxLength` | the text's length |
| `pattern` | the text matches (values over 10,000 characters are not tested — **avoid patterns that backtrack catastrophically**: they run on the page) |
| `oneOf` | the value is one of the list (trimmed, case-insensitive) |
| `unique` | no other row of the column holds it |
| `message`, `severity`, `onInvalid` | replace the generated message; `error` (default) · `warning` · `note`; `flag` (default) · `block` |

- **Titles** match trimmed and case-insensitive (an exact title wins). A
  title the file lacks is one `note` error; a duplicated title checks the
  first column and adds one `note`. The file always loads.
- **`validate(ctx, signal)`** runs for every cell of a titled column, sync or
  async. `ctx` is `{phase, sheet, ref, row, column, value, was, original,
  rowValues}`, `rowValues` keyed by title, so a rule can read the row; editing
  any cell asks the row again. A newer edit to a cell aborts the older check
  (`signal`) and its result is dropped. Return `null` or `{severity, message,
  expected?}`.
- **Phases:** `input` — 150 ms after typing stops, an outline and a message
  at the cell bar, nothing stored; `commit` — on save, `flag` stores the value
  and adds an error, `block` refuses it (only a JSON rule or a synchronous
  result can block; an async result flags); `load` — every row, in slices,
  with the progress in the status line.
- Setting `columns`, `validate` or `onInvalid` again re-checks every row;
  host errors no longer produced are removed. People's errors are never
  touched, and a rule never edits a cell.
- Rules belong to the pane: `workbook.setColumnRules({ columns, validate,
  onInvalid, headerRow })` does the same without an element.

## Rules file

Ship the rules next to your code as JSON and point the sheet at them; every
cell they cover is checked on load and the failures are listed in
`<sheetpane-errors>`. With `flagging="off"` the sheet shows no Flag issue and
opens no pop-up — the errors panel is the one place errors are read.

```html
<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" src="./q3.xlsx" rules-src="./sheetpane.rules.json" flagging="off"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3"></sheetpane-errors>
```

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://unpkg.com/@sheetpane/grid/rules.schema.json",
  "version": 1,
  "sheets": {
    "*": {
      "columns": { "Email": { "pattern": "^[^@\\s]+@[^@\\s]+\\.[a-z]{2,}$", "unique": true } }
    },
    "Accounts": {
      "headerRow": 2,
      "columns": {
        "Account ID": { "required": true, "pattern": "^AC-\\d{5}$", "message": "Account IDs are AC- and five digits" },
        "Units":      { "type": "integer", "min": 0 },
        "Status":     { "oneOf": ["Active", "Inactive"], "noneOf": ["TBD", "N/A"], "severity": "warning" }
      },
      "cells": {
        "B1":     { "equals": "Q3 review", "note": "the title cell the export pipeline reads" },
        "H3:H40": { "type": "number", "min": 0, "max": 1 }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- **`sheets`** by name; `"*"` applies to every sheet and a named sheet's rule
  for the same title wins. Each sheet has `headerRow`, `columns` (by title,
  as [Column rules](#column-rules)) and `cells` (an A1 cell or range).
- **The words** are Column rules' plus `equals` (the one valid value; a blank
  cell fails it), `noneOf` (values never valid) and `note` (for whoever
  maintains the file — never shown as the message).
- **`$schema`** gives your editor autocomplete and red squiggles: the schema
  ships as `@sheetpane/grid/rules.schema.json`.
- **Never silent, never a throw:** an unknown key, word or version, a sheet,
  title or cell the workbook lacks, or a pattern that is not a regular
  expression becomes one `note` in the errors panel; the rest still applies.
- `rules-src` is read with a GET like `src`; `excel.rules = object` does the
  same without a fetch. Setting either checks every row again. The element's
  `columns` and `validate` still work beside it — the file's rule wins for the
  same title, with a note.
- **YAML or TOML:** parse it yourself and pass the object — the package reads
  JSON only, so it carries no parser:

  ```js
  import { parse } from 'yaml';      // or: import { parse } from 'smol-toml';
  excel.rules = parse(await (await fetch('./sheetpane.rules.yaml')).text());
  ```

## The same checks with no page (`@sheetpane/grid/check`)

`check()` runs what the pane runs on load — the rules file, column rules, an
async `validate`, and each plugin's `validate` after a `derive` plugin has
recalculated — in Node, a worker or a page, and returns the errors the pane
would hold. The entry imports no element and touches no DOM.

```js
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { check } from '@sheetpane/grid/check';
import { validation } from '@sheetpane/validation/check';

const errors = await check(await readFile('q3.xlsx'), {
  name: 'q3.xlsx',
  rules: JSON.parse(await readFile('sheetpane.rules.json', 'utf8')),
  plugins: [validation()],          // objects, or ids registered with registerPlugin
});
```

- **Options are the element's:** `rules` (an object, or its JSON text),
  `columns`, `validate(ctx, signal)`, `onInvalid`, `headerRow`, `plugins`, and
  the file's `name` (`.csv` reads CSV; unnamed bytes are sniffed as `load()`
  does).
- **The same errors** as `<sheetpane-excel>` given the same file and settings
  — only `id` and `createdAt` are per run — sorted by sheet, row and column.
  A file that cannot be read throws its reader's code (SP-10xx); anything but
  bytes throws SP-3020.
- The store, the rules checker and the plugin contract are exported here too
  (`createWorkbook`, `checkDocument`, `registerPlugin`, the types), for a
  DOM-free plugin or a host's own pipeline. `loadWorkbook(bytes, options)`
  takes the same options and returns the loaded store, every check finished,
  instead of its errors.

## A range as static HTML (`@sheetpane/grid/static`)

`renderStatic(book, { sheet, range, errors, theme, headers })` returns one
self-contained `<table>` — the text the pane shows (the `format` plugin), the
look it draws (`decorate` plugins, merges, the theme's tokens as inline hex),
hidden rows and columns left out, and the errors marked — for a report or an
email. Made with no DOM, in Node, a worker or a page.

```js
import { readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { loadWorkbook, renderStatic } from '@sheetpane/grid/static';
import { numfmt } from '@sheetpane/numfmt';
import { styles } from '@sheetpane/styles';
import { condfmt } from '@sheetpane/condfmt';
import { validation } from '@sheetpane/validation/check';

const book = await loadWorkbook(await readFile('q3.xlsx'), { name: 'q3.xlsx', rules, plugins: [numfmt(), styles(), condfmt(), validation()] });
await writeFile('report.html', renderStatic(book, { sheet: 'Holdings', range: 'A1:F20' }));
```

- **`book`** is a loaded store: `loadWorkbook()`'s, `createWorkbook()`'s after
  `load()`, or an element's `workbook` — its changes and derived values show.
  `sheet` defaults to the selected one, `range` to the used range (≤ 200,000
  cells), `errors` to the visible layers' (`[]` marks nothing; pass `check()`'s
  or a restored review), `theme` to `light` (`dark` too), `headers` to true.
- **Marks:** a ring and a tint as the grid draws them, and a badge with the
  glyph (✕ ! i ✓, `A` for an accepted deviation) and a number that the footer
  explains — severity, range, type, message, *should be*, the acceptance's
  reason. Never colour alone. Errors about the whole sheet or the workbook
  head the footer and mark no cell. Results (✓ passed, — not checked) show
  as the grid's corner glyph only when the pane's `results` level is
  `marks`. Rich text keeps its runs (italic, bold, colour), never a font.
- **Inert:** no script, no event attribute, no `class`, no stylesheet, no URL
  (a `decorate` value that loads or escapes is dropped), every value escaped,
  no font family — the reader's font is the font.
- **Not drawn:** what an `overlay` plugin draws (pictures, charts) — the
  footer says so and `data-sp-skipped` names the plugins. Interactive cell
  controls (a list arrow) are not drawn either.
- Refusals: SP-3027 when `book` is not a loaded workbook; SP-3028 for an
  unknown sheet, a range that is not A1, or too many cells.

## `<sheetpane-errors>`

| kind | name | what |
|---|---|---|
| attribute | `pane`, `author`, `plugins` | as above |
| attribute | `readonly` | hides the form, Resolve, Accept… and Delete — a sign-off screen |
| attribute / property | `results` | as above; the panel's *On sheet* switch moves the pane between `summary` and `marks` |
| property / method | `errors`, `errorTypes`, `getErrors({ layer? })`, `setErrors(list or envelope, { plugins?, layer? })` | |
| property | `renderDetail` | your extra detail in an open row — see below (W-68) |
| attribute / property | `layers`; `layerNames` | the review layers shown (as on the sheet); what the switch calls each, e.g. `{ pdf: 'PDF check' }` (W-51) |
| event | `sheetpane-errors {v, errors, plugins, layers, changed}`, `sheetpane-layers {visible, layers}`, `sheetpane-reveal {error}` | **Show in sheet**: switch to the sheet's tab or open the pop-up |

## Saving and restoring a review

Errors are plain JSON (`SheetpaneError`, schema `v: 1`). Listen to
`sheetpane-errors`, store its `detail` — the envelope `{ v: 2, errors,
plugins, layers, changed }` — where you like, and give it back after the
file loads:

```js
excel.addEventListener('sheetpane-load', () => errors.setErrors(saved));
```

A review saved before W-51 (`{ errors, plugins }`) restores the same way, into
the `review` layer.

**Review layers** (W-51): several sets of errors in one pane — say a
validation run and a PDF check — each replaced whole without touching the
others. Every error has a `layer` (`review` unless named):

```js
errors.setErrors(validationFindings, { layer: 'validation' });
errors.setErrors(pdfFindings, { layer: 'pdf' }); // validation is kept
errors.layerNames = { pdf: 'PDF check' };
errors.layers = ['pdf']; // or layers="pdf" on either element; null shows all
```

With two or more layers the panel's header shows a switch — **All**, then
each layer with its open count. What is shown is the pane's: the sheet's
pins, marks and counts, the list and the comments an export writes all
follow it (`export({ layers: [...] })` names another set). Replacing a layer
keeps undo; a person's new error goes into the layer they are looking at.
Names are ids: 1–64 characters, no spaces (SP-3021).

An error whose cell no longer shows what was found is tagged *stale*, never
moved.

**An error with no cell** (W-55): `range: ""` is about the whole sheet, and
`sheet: ""` with `range: ""` about the whole workbook — "no Pages List", "a
listed tab has no sheet". Add one with `setErrors()`, `workbook.addError()` or
a `validate` hook (a whole-sheet draft only). The list shows them first — a
*Workbook* group, then each sheet's — above the cell errors; a whole-sheet
error is counted on its tab and **Show in sheet** opens the tab; for a
workbook-level one it is disabled. They are never placed on A1; no pin, no
cell mark, no `found`. `errorScope(e)` says which (`cell` · `sheet` ·
`workbook`). **If your code reads `range` as an A1 reference, handle `""`.**

**Your data on an error, and your detail beside it** (W-68): `meta` holds any
JSON of yours (64 KiB at most, `ERROR_META_MAX`); it is saved and restored
with the error and never written into the file. `renderDetail(error)` — on
`<sheetpane-excel>` for the error card and on `<sheetpane-errors>` for the
open row, each its own — returns a string (shown as text, never HTML), a
Node (yours, placed as it is) or `null`. It is drawn after the message, in
`::part(detail)`, and runs again only when that error changes.

```js
workbook.addError({ sheet: 'Spec', range: 'C7', type: 'out-of-range', severity: 'error', meta: { page: 3, measured: '6.63 in' } });
const detail = (e) => (e.meta?.measured ? `The PDF measures ${e.meta.measured}, outside ± 0.06 in` : null);
excel.renderDetail = detail;
errors.renderDetail = detail;
```

A `meta` that is not JSON or is over the cap is dropped (SP-3016); a hook
that throws shows nothing (SP-3017).

**Accepted deviations** (W-69): a known, approved difference can be accepted
instead of deleted. **Accept…** in an open row of `<sheetpane-errors>` asks
for a reason (required) and records it with who (the element's `author`) and
when: `status: 'accepted'`, `acceptedBy`, `acceptedAt`, `reason`. Accepted
errors stay in the review and the download but are not counted — not in
"n open", the severity chips or the sheet's counts — and the **Accepted n**
chip lists them. Reopen takes an acceptance back; so does undo. From code:

```js
workbook.acceptError(id, 'Approved by the customer on 18 Oct', { by: 'Ravi' });
```

A blank reason is refused (SP-3018). Count open problems with
`status === 'open' && !isResult(e)`. With `@sheetpane/comments`, the export adds a reply
*Accepted: <reason>* to the error's comment thread.

**The Edits view** (W-64): an *Edits n* chip beside *Problems* lists every
change in the pane, newest first — the cell or range and kind, *was → now*,
the time, and the errors that edit cleared or raised (each a link to the
error). Picking a row selects the cell; **Revert** on a row and **Revert
all** are each one undo step. It shows in Edit mode, and in View mode while
there are edits. The store gives the same list to your code:

```js
const edits = workbook.edits(); // [{ key, sheet, ref, kind, was, now, at }], newest first
workbook.editEffects(edits[0].key); // { cleared, raised, matched } — error ids
workbook.revertEdits([edits[0].key]); // omit the keys to revert all
```

## Results: passed and not checked

A host that checks a sheet can report what passed as well as what failed:
an entry with `severity: 'pass'` (✓) or `'skipped'` (— not checked; its
`message` says why). Give them with `setErrors()` or from a plugin's
`validate`. Results stay quiet:

| `results=` | errors panel | sheet |
|---|---|---|
| `off` | results are dropped on arrival | as without results |
| `summary` (default) | one line — *1 problem · ✓ 180 passed · — 28 not checked · On sheet* — and *Passed* / *Not checked* chips; the list opens on *Problems* | nothing marked; the status line says *186 of 214 checked* |
| `marks` (or *On sheet*) | the same, switch on | a 9 px ✓ or — in each result cell's bottom-left corner |

Passes are listed grouped by check (`type` + `message`), not-checked cells
by reason (`message`); a group opens to its cells, and **Show ▸** selects its
range and marks it even at `summary`. Selecting a result cell names its check
in the cell bar. A problem on the same cell always wins. Tab counts, the
toolbar counts, the panel's *n open* and the severity filters count problems
only, and a download leaves results out (`@sheetpane/comments` writes them
only with `export({ includeResults: true })`). A host that switches on
`severity` meets two more values.

```js
errors.setErrors([
  { v: 1, id: 'ERR-0001', sheet: 'Holdings', range: 'H3', type: 'fee-rate', severity: 'pass', message: 'Fee rate 0.00%–2.00%',
    found: '0.35%', expected: '', cellChanged: false, status: 'open', matchesExpected: false, author: 'host', createdAt: new Date().toISOString() },
]);
```

## Protected sheets

What a file protects stays protected in Edit, with no plugin. On a protected
sheet (Excel: Review › Protect Sheet) a locked cell — every cell is locked
until someone unlocks it — shows its value and *🔒 Locked in the file* in the
cell bar; typing, paste and Delete there are refused with
`sheetpane-editcancel` `{ reason: 'locked', code: 'SP-3026' }`, before
`sheetpane-beforechange`. Unlocked cells edit as usual, and a paste or a
range Delete writes those only, saying how many locked cells it left. A
formula marked *Hidden* shows its value, never its formula. A workbook whose
structure is protected keeps its sheets and its rows and columns: Hide and
Unhide sheet, and every insert and delete, are disabled with the reason; a
protected sheet refuses the inserts and deletes it does not allow, as Excel
does (`SP-3026`).

```js
const wb = excel.workbook;
wb.isLocked('Spec', 'A2');        // true: a locked cell on a protected sheet
wb.isFormulaHidden('Spec', 'E2'); // true: shows its value only
wb.structureLocked();             // true: <workbookProtection lockStructure="1">
wb.sheetProtection('Spec');       // { formatCells: true, …, hasPassword: true } — never the password
```

sheetpane never reads, checks or removes a protection password, and the
download carries the file's protection exactly as it was. `protection="ignore"`
sets it aside for the pane — **the host's decision**: a host that lets people
edit what the file locks owns that choice.

## Plugins

Features beyond review — every Excel number format, live formulas, cell
styles, data validation, conditional formatting, pictures, charts, comments —
are separate packages that plug into six hooks and six slots. With none
installed the grid is the plain review tool. **See each one on the same
workbook:** the demos' plugin gallery (`just demo-html` or `just demo-react`)
has a tab per plugin, plus Vanilla and All plugins.

```js
import '@sheetpane/numfmt';     // registers "numfmt"
```

```html
<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" plugins="numfmt"></sheetpane-excel>
```

Or build the store yourself: `el.workbook = createWorkbook({ plugins: [...] })`.

## Styling

Colours, spacing and radii are `--sp-*` custom properties on the elements
(`--sp-accent`, `--sp-ink`, `--sp-line`, …); `@sheetpane/grid/style.css`
lists the defaults, and `theme="dark"` swaps in the dark set. The font is yours: set it on the element or any ancestor.

The specs are the records [SR-GRID](../../records/0105_GRID.md) and
[SR-ERRORS](../../records/0106_ERRORS.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/export/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/export/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/export

**A plain JavaScript object in, an `.xlsx` or `.csv` file out.** No runtime
dependencies. Runs in evergreen browsers and Node 22+. Used by
`@sheetpane/grid`'s Export button; usable on its own.

```sh
pnpm add @sheetpane/export      # or npm / yarn
```

## The object

```ts
type Cell = string | number | boolean | null;
interface Sheet {
  name: string; rows: Cell[][]; merges?: string[]; columnWidths?: number[]; hidden?: boolean;
  freeze?: { rows: number; cols: number };
  dataValidations?: DataValidation[]; conditionalFormats?: ConditionalFormat[];
}
interface Workbook { sheets: Sheet[]; dxfs?: Dxf[] }
interface Change { sheet: string; ref: string; value: Cell }
```

`rows[0][0]` is A1. `merges` are ranges like `'A1:J1'` — the top-left cell is
centred, the one format sheetpane keeps. `columnWidths` are Excel character
widths.

## Build a new `.xlsx`

```ts
import { toXlsx } from '@sheetpane/export';

const bytes = await toXlsx({
  sheets: [{ name: 'Sales', rows: [['Region', 'Total'], ['North', 1200], ['South', 950.5]], columnWidths: [14, 10] }],
});
```

Text is written as inline strings, numbers and booleans typed. `{ compression:
'store' }` gives byte-identical output on every engine (larger; the audit
mode); the default compresses with `CompressionStream` / `zlib`.

## Dropdowns and conditional formats

A sheet's `dataValidations` and `conditionalFormats` are written as Excel's
own rules — the same shapes `@sheetpane/import` reads, so a rule read from a
file can be written back unchanged. A conditional format's `dxfId` picks the
format it applies from the workbook's `dxfs`.

```ts
const bytes = await toXlsx({
  sheets: [
    {
      name: 'Spec', rows: [['Item', 'Unit'], ['Bolt', null]],
      dataValidations: [{
        sqref: ['B2:B200'], type: 'list', formula1: 'Lists!$A$2:$A$9',   // or a literal: '"kg,m,pcs"'
        allowBlank: true, showErrorMessage: true, showDropDown: false,   // false shows the arrow (OOXML's inverted flag)
        prompt: 'Pick a unit', error: 'Not a unit on the Lists sheet',
      }],
      conditionalFormats: [{
        sqref: ['B2:B200'],
        rules: [{ type: 'expression', priority: 1, stopIfTrue: false, formulas: ['AND($A2<>"",$B2="")'], dxfId: 0 }],
      }],
    },
    { name: 'Lists', rows: [['Unit'], ['kg'], ['m'], ['pcs']] },
  ],
  dxfs: [{ font: { color: { rgb: 'FF9C0006' } }, fill: { patternType: 'solid', bgColor: { rgb: 'FFFFC7CE' } } }],  // a dxf's solid fill is bgColor
});
```

A rule Excel would repair — an unknown type, a title over 32 or a message over
255 characters, a typed-out list over 255, a `dxfId` with no format — is
refused with `SP-2015`, naming the sheet and range.

## Patch the uploaded `.xlsx` — keep everything else

```ts
import { patchXlsx } from '@sheetpane/export';

const out = await patchXlsx(originalBytes, [
  { sheet: 'Holdings', ref: 'G6', value: 268.4 },
  { sheet: 'Holdings', ref: 'A7', value: 'AC-10044' },
]);
```

Only the changed cells are rewritten (their style is kept); every other part
of the file — charts, pivot tables, comments, names, styles — is copied byte
for byte. Excel is asked to recalculate formulas on open, and pivot tables
whose source changed to refresh.

Options also rewrite a sheet's frozen pane (`freeze`), its merged ranges
(`merges`), its rules (`dataValidations`, `conditionalFormats`, with new
formats in `dxfs`) and what it hides (`hidden`):

```ts
await patchXlsx(originalBytes, [], {
  hidden: [
    { sheet: 'Holdings', rows: [3, 4, 5], cols: [2], outline: { rows: { 3: 1, 4: 1, 5: 1 } } },
    { sheet: 'Workings', state: 'hidden' },   // 'visible' | 'hidden' | 'veryHidden'
  ],
});
```

Each `hidden` list is the sheet's **whole** set after the edit (0-based): the
listed rows and columns are hidden and every other one is shown. `<col>` spans
are split and merged so widths and styles stay put. When the active sheet is
hidden, the workbook opens on the first visible one. Hiding every sheet is
refused (`SP-2002`).

```ts
const book = await read(originalBytes);                 // @sheetpane/import
await patchXlsx(originalBytes, [], {
  dataValidations: [{ sheet: 'Spec', rules: [...book.sheets[0].dataValidations, unitRule] }],
  dxfs: [{ fill: { patternType: 'solid', bgColor: { rgb: 'FFFFC7CE' } } }],
  conditionalFormats: [{ sheet: 'Spec', formats: [{ sqref: ['B2:B200'], rules: [
    { type: 'containsBlanks', priority: 1, stopIfTrue: false, formulas: ['LEN(TRIM(B2))=0'], dxfId: book.styles.dxfs.length },
  ] }] }],
});
```

Each list is the sheet's **whole** set: `[]` removes the block. `dxfs` are
added after the file's own, so the first new one is `book.styles.dxfs.length`.
An `exportPatch` hook can do the same with `setDataValidations(xml, rules)`
and `setConditionalFormats(xml, formats, dxfCount)`.

## Write CSV

```ts
import { toCsv } from '@sheetpane/export';

const { text, guarded } = toCsv(sheet);                 // comma, CRLF, UTF-8 BOM
const semi = toCsv(sheet, { delimiter: ';', bom: false });
```

**Formula injection guard — on by default.** A text cell that starts with `=`
`+` `-` `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading `'`, so a spreadsheet
shows it instead of running it. Plain numerals such as `-150` are left alone.
**This changes the data**; `guarded` lists the cells it touched (`['A1', …]`)
so your app can say so. Turn it off with `{ guardFormulas: false }`.

`toCsv` writes one sheet; for a multi-sheet workbook, pick the one you mean.

## Table references — `resolveStructuredRef(formula, sheets)`

An Excel table's structured reference as plain cells, from the tables each sheet
carries (`@sheetpane/import` reads them):

```js
resolveStructuredRef('Units[Unit]', book.sheets);
// { sheet: 'Lists', table: 'Units', ref: 'A2:A5', range: { top: 1, left: 0, bottom: 4, right: 0 } }
```

`Table[Column]` and `Table[[#Data],[Column]]` are the column's data rows;
`#Headers`, `#Totals` and `#All` name those rows; `Table[[A]:[B]]` spans columns;
`Table[]` and the bare name are the data body. `[#This Row]` and anything that is
not one range give `undefined`. `patchXlsx` keeps a workbook's table parts as they are.

## Errors

Every refusal is an `ExportError` with a `code` and the `sheet` / `ref` it is
about: a bad sheet name (1–31 characters, none of `[ ] : * ? / \`, unique
ignoring case), more than 1,048,576 rows or 16,384 columns, `NaN` or
`Infinity`, text over 32,767 characters, overlapping merges, a `hidden`
option that would leave no sheet visible, a validation or conditional-format
rule Excel would repair (`SP-2015`).

## Save the file — `download(data, filename, options?)`

One call turns export output into a file the browser saves. `.xlsx` and
`.csv` only; the bytes are never changed. The spec is
[SR-DOWNLOAD](../../records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md).

```ts
import { toXlsx, toCsv, download } from '@sheetpane/export';

download(await toXlsx(book), 'sales.xlsx');                 // 1 · bytes → sales.xlsx
download(toCsv(sheet, { bom: true }).text, 'sales.csv');    // 2 · text, BOM kept: Excel shows "José"
download(new Blob([bytes]), 'report.xlsx');                 // 3 · a Blob you already have
download(await toXlsx(book), 'Q3 report');                  // 4 · → Q3 report.xlsx (text → .csv)
download(bytes, 'FY26: North/South?.xlsx');                 // 5 · → FY26_ North_South_.xlsx
download(text, 'data.csv', { type: 'text/csv;charset=utf-8;header=present' }); // 6 · your own type
```

**7 · Errors are explicit, never silent.** Each names the file:

```ts
download(bytes, 'sales.pdf');            // ✗ "sales.pdf" — sheetpane saves .xlsx or .csv only
download(new Blob([bytes]), 'mystery');  // ✗ "mystery" — add .xlsx or .csv; the type can't be told from this Blob
download('a,b', 'sales.xlsx');           // ✗ "sales.xlsx" — text can't be saved as .xlsx; use .csv
download(bytes, 'sales.xlsx');           // in Node or a worker:
                                         // ✗ download() needs a browser page (no document); write the bytes yourself
```

**8 · After an `await` in a click handler** works — tested in Chromium and WebKit:

```ts
button.addEventListener('click', async () => download(await toXlsx(book), 'sales.xlsx'));
```

**9 · With the grid,** `<sheetpane-excel>`'s Export button calls `download` for you.

**10 · Inside an iframe** the host must allow downloads, or the browser blocks
the save silently:

```html
<iframe src="app.html" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-downloads"></iframe>
```

The spec is the record [SR-EXPORT](../../records/0103_EXPORT.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/import/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/import/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/import

**An `.xlsx` or `.csv` in, a plain JavaScript workbook out** — the same
`Workbook` shape [`@sheetpane/export`](../export/README.md) writes, so a file
round-trips: `toXlsx(await read(file))`. No runtime dependency but
`@sheetpane/export`. `@sheetpane/grid` reads every file through it; a host can
use it on its own.

```ts
import { read } from '@sheetpane/import';

const book = await read(file);            // a File, Blob, ArrayBuffer or Uint8Array
book.sheets[0].rows;                      // raw values: [['Account ID', …], ['AC-10021', 1200, 268.4, …]]
book.sheets[0].text;                      // display text: [['Account ID', …], ['AC-10021', '1,200', '268.40', …]]
```

## What you get

| field | what it is |
|---|---|
| `rows` | the stored values — text, numbers, booleans, `null`. Export writes these back. A formula cell holds its **saved** value. |
| `text` | what a cell shows: numbers through a small number-format subset (dates, times, percent, fixed decimals, thousands); anything outside it shows the raw stored text |
| `merges`, `columnWidths` | as `@sheetpane/export` takes them |
| `state` | `'visible'`, `'hidden'` or `'veryHidden'` (`<sheet state>`); `hidden` is kept as `state !== 'visible'` but is deprecated |
| `hiddenRows`, `hiddenCols` | 0-based, sorted; a zero height or width counts as hidden |
| `rowOutline`, `colOutline`, `outline`, `autoFilter` | outline levels per row and column (sparse `{ level, collapsed? }`), the deepest levels and summary placement, and the filter range |
| `formulas`, `styleIndex`, `freeze`, `rowHeights` | per sheet, for the grid and the plugins |
| `runs` | rich-text cells only, sparse: `{ B4: [{ text: 'Net ' }, { text: 'of tax', i: true, sz: 11 }] }` — each run's text with its `b`, `i`, `u`, `strike`, `color`, `sz`, `vertAlign` (never the font family); phonetic runs left out; `rows` and `text` hold the joined text as before |
| `dataValidations`, `conditionalFormats`, `drawings`, `notes`, `threadedComments`, `pivotTables` | per sheet, parsed, for the plugins; the first two are `@sheetpane/export`'s shapes, so `toXlsx` / `patchXlsx` write them back unchanged |
| `protection`, `rowStyles`, `colStyles` | the sheet's `<sheetProtection>` switches while it is protected (`true` = refused; `hasPassword`, never the password), and the formats an empty cell takes from its row or column — with `cellProtection(sheet, styles, row, col)` for a cell's `{ locked, hidden }` |
| `tables` | the sheet's Excel tables: `name` (as formulas use it), `ref`, header and totals rows, `columns`, `style` — drawn by `@sheetpane/tables` |
| `styles`, `themeColors`, `persons`, `definedNames`, `date1904` | per workbook (each `styles.cellXfs` entry with its `protection?`) |
| `workbookProtection` | `{ lockStructure, lockWindows, hasPassword }` when the file protects its structure or windows |
| `part(path)` | any part of the package (a picture, a chart) without re-reading the ZIP |
| `sha256` | from `read()`: the SHA-256 of the bytes opened, 64 lowercase hex digits — which file this is. Absent on a page without Web Crypto (not `https` or `localhost`), with a console warning `SP-1009`; never a substitute hash. `sha256(bytes)` is exported for hashing anything else |

## CSV

```ts
import { fromCsv } from '@sheetpane/import';
const book = await fromCsv(text, { name: 'sales.csv' });   // delimiter , ; or tab detected; book.delimiter says which
```

UTF-8 with or without a BOM; CRLF, LF or CR; RFC 4180 quotes. Every cell is
text, as stored. The one sheet is named after the file.

## What it refuses

Every refusal is an `ImportError` with a `code`:

| code | when |
|---|---|
| `unsupported-format` | any other extension — `.xls`, `.xlsm`, `.xlsb`, `.ods`, `.numbers`, `.tsv`…; a macro-enabled workbook renamed `.xlsx`; a ZIP named `.csv` |
| `password-or-legacy` | an OLE compound file: a password-protected `.xlsx` or a legacy `.xls` |
| `not-workbook` | a ZIP without `xl/workbook.xml`, or bytes named `.xlsx` that are not a ZIP |
| `too-large` | ZIP64; more than 512 MB inflated in one part or 1 GB in all; past 1,048,576 rows or 16,384 columns |
| `corrupt` | broken DEFLATE, a CRC mismatch, XML that does not parse |

The spec is the record [SR-IMPORT](../../records/0104_IMPORT.md).

<!-- source: packages/numfmt/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/numfmt/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/numfmt

**Excel number formats for sheetpane — currency, dates, fractions, elapsed time, conditional sections, locales — as a plugin on the `format` hook.**

A plugin: it registers against the one in-memory workbook of `@sheetpane/grid`
(`createWorkbook({ plugins: [...] })`, or `plugins="numfmt"` on the element), so
`<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>` both see its effect. Versioned in
lockstep with `@sheetpane/grid`. Without it, the grid shows the small number-format
subset it ships with; with it, every format Excel can store.

- `@sheetpane/numfmt` — the headless plugin. Safe to import in Node (no DOM at import).
- `@sheetpane/numfmt/ui` — the controls it adds to the grid's `format-row`: a number-format dropdown and ± decimals. Opt-in.

Engine: [`numfmt`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/numfmt) 4.0.1 (MIT, zero dependencies), pinned.

## Install

```bash
npm install @sheetpane/grid @sheetpane/numfmt
```

## Use

By attribute — importing the package registers it under the id `numfmt`:

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@sheetpane/grid';
  import '@sheetpane/numfmt/ui'; // the format plugin *and* its controls; import '@sheetpane/numfmt' for the format alone
</script>
<sheetpane-excel plugins="numfmt" mode="edit"></sheetpane-excel>
```

By code:

```ts
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { numfmt } from '@sheetpane/numfmt';
import { ui } from '@sheetpane/numfmt/ui';

const workbook = createWorkbook({ plugins: [numfmt(), ui()] });
element.workbook = workbook;               // the element and <sheetpane-errors> share it
await workbook.load(bytes, 'holdings.xlsx');
workbook.text('Holdings', 'G3');           // '$1,234.50 '
```

`numfmt({ locale })` pins a locale; `ui({ locale, ask })` does the same for the controls and lets a host replace the
`window.prompt` that "Custom…" uses (return the code, or `null` to cancel).

## What it does

- **Display.** Every numeric cell's text comes from the library for every built-in id (0–49) and every custom code in the
  file's `<numFmts>`. `General` follows Excel's rule (11 characters, then scientific). A cell with no `s` uses xf 0.
- **1904.** `<workbookPr date1904>` is honoured: the library has no 1904 mode, so a date format's serial is shifted by 1,462
  days first. Elapsed-time formats (`[h]:mm`) are not dates and are not shifted.
- **Dates out of range** show `########`, as Excel does, not the bare number.
- **Fallback.** If the library rejects a code, the plugin says nothing and the core subset shows its text for that cell.
  `plugin.fallbacks()` lists those cells (`['Sheet1!B4']`).
- **Padding.** Accounting and `?` formats pad with spaces; the plugin also provides `decorate` with `white-space: pre` on
  those cells so HTML does not collapse them. It sets no font (SR-LAW-5).
- **Edits.** A format chosen in the UI is a change of kind `numFmt` (key `sheet!ref`, `now` = the code, `was` = the
  file's code). Choosing the file's own code again removes the change. Undo and redo work.
- **Export.** `exportPatch` appends the new `<numFmt>` entries and `<xf>` rows to `xl/styles.xml` — deduplicated, the base
  xf's font, fill, border and alignment kept — and repoints each changed cell's `s`. An en-US built-in code is written as its id.
  Cells nobody touched keep their `s`. A CSV has no styles; its export carries values only.

## The controls

`format-row`, Edit mode only:

- **Dropdown** — General · Number · Currency · Accounting · Date · Time · Percentage · Fraction · Scientific · Text · Custom…
  Number is `0.00`, Percentage `0.00%`, Fraction `# ?/?`, Scientific `0.00E+00`; Currency, Accounting, Date and Time are the
  locale's (`$#,##0.00_);($#,##0.00)` in English, `#,##0.00 €;-#,##0.00 €` in German).
- **Decrease / Increase decimals** — one `0` fewer or more after the point in every section of the code; on `General` it
  starts from the decimals the value shows. Dates, times, fractions and text are left alone.

A selection range applies to every **numeric** cell in it, within the sheet's data. Blank and text cells are skipped. So are
cells with a pending **value** edit: the grid keeps one change per cell, and a format would replace the edit. At most 10,000
cells are changed in one go (each is one change and one undo step) — the plugin warns when it stops.

The cell bar keeps showing the raw value (`1234.5`) while the cell shows the formatted text.

## Locales

The locale is `numfmt({ locale })`, else the page's `<html lang>`, read when a cell is formatted (a cell's text is cached
until it changes, so set `lang` before loading). An unknown tag means English. Tags may be written `de-DE` or `de_DE`.

- `de-DE`: `1.234.567,89`, `15 März 2023`, `12,3%`, `General` 1234,5; built-in ids 14–22 and 5–8, 41–44 become the locale's
  (id 14 → `15.03.2023`), as they do in Excel.
- `en-IN`: Indian grouping, `12,34,567.89` (any `-IN` territory).
- The library's other locales (about 70) are available by tag.

Note: a format that names its own locale, `[$€-407]#,##0.00`, is formatted with that locale's separators by the library
(`€1.234,50`). Excel may keep the reader's; this is unverified (see the record).

## Tests

`pnpm exec vitest run --project numfmt` — a real browser. The fixture table (`test/fixtures/table.ts`) holds the expected text
for every built-in id and 50 custom codes. **It was written from Excel's documented behaviour, not captured from Excel** —
there is no Excel on the build machine; regenerating the `expected` column with `TEXT()` is owed.

Spec: [`work/open/W-15-numfmt.md`](../../work/open/W-15-numfmt.md).
How plugins plug in: [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../../work/compare/plugins.compare.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/formulas/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/formulas/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/formulas

**Formula recalculation for sheetpane — edit a cell and every dependent formula updates — as a plugin on the `derive` hook, backed by IronCalc (WASM, lazy-loaded).**

A plugin: it registers against the one in-memory workbook of `@sheetpane/grid`
(`createWorkbook({ plugins: [...] })`, or `plugins="formulas"` on the element), so
`<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>` both see its effect. Versioned in
lockstep with `@sheetpane/grid`.

- `@sheetpane/formulas` — the headless plugin (`derive`, `exportPatch`).
- `@sheetpane/formulas/ui` — the controls it adds to the grid's slots; opt-in.

```js
import '@sheetpane/grid';
import '@sheetpane/formulas/ui'; // registers "formulas" with its controls
// <sheetpane-excel plugins="formulas" src="book.xlsx"></sheetpane-excel>

// or, headless / your own store:
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { formulas } from '@sheetpane/formulas';
const store = createWorkbook({ plugins: [formulas({ preload: true })] });
```

## What it does

- **Live recalculation.** Edit B3 and every formula that reads it — on any
  sheet, through defined names — gets its new value. Recalculated cells are
  *derived*: drawn with a mark, never in the change map or the change count.
- **Typed formulas.** With the plugin installed, a value typed starting `=` is a
  change of kind `formula` (SR-GRID 21b); it evaluates, and export writes it as
  a real formula.
- **Errors as Excel shows them.** `#DIV/0!`, `#REF!`, `#N/A`, `#VALUE!` are
  values, never exceptions. A circular reference shows `0`, as Excel does, and
  is listed by `cycles()` (the UI names it in the status line).
- **Honest about gaps.** A formula from the file that IronCalc cannot calculate
  (`#NAME?` for a function it lacks, a parse error, `#SPILL!` over a legacy
  array formula) keeps the value Excel saved and is listed by `unsupported()`
  (the UI marks it `≈`); Excel recalculates it on open.
- **Export.** `exportPatch` writes `<f>` and a cached `<v>` for each typed
  formula, a new `<v>` for each recalculated formula cell (its `<f>` — shared
  or not — is kept as written), and keeps `fullCalcOnLoad="1"` so Excel
  re-verifies every value.

## The engine is a cache (SR-LAW-9)

The JavaScript workbook is the only source of truth. The IronCalc model is built
from it — the file's values and formulas overlaid with the user's changes — and
rebuilt whenever the workbook object changes. On a change the plugin reads the
cell's state from the store and writes it into the model; it never reads state
back out of the model, only computed values.

Only what formulas can reach goes into the model: every formula cell, plus the
cells its references (and the defined names') cover. A formula with `INDIRECT`
or `OFFSET` can reach anywhere, so then every cell goes in. A new formula over
cells not yet in the model feeds them on demand.

## Loading: nothing until a formula needs it

`@ironcalc/wasm` 0.9.0 (MIT / Apache-2.0) is a 2 MB `.wasm`. It is reached only
by a dynamic `import()` on the first `derive` that has a formula to calculate:

- importing the package (in Node too) touches no `WebAssembly`;
- a workbook with no formulas never loads it — until a formula is typed;
- `formulas({ preload: true })` warms it when the plugin is created;
- `formulas({ wasm })` says where the `.wasm` is (a URL, a `Response`, the bytes
  or a compiled module) — for a CDN, a strict CSP, or Node. By default the
  bundler emits it beside `@ironcalc/wasm`'s `wasm.js` (`new URL(…, import.meta.url)`;
  Vite, webpack 5, Rollup and esbuild handle it).

## The plugin's own API

| member | what |
|---|---|
| `ready()` | resolves when every queued recalculation is done and merged |
| `cycles()` | formula cells in a circular reference |
| `unsupported()` | file formula cells IronCalc cannot calculate (saved value kept) |
| `stateOf(sheet, ref)` | `'cycle'`, `'unsupported'` or `undefined` |
| `built()` | whether a model exists for the current workbook |

## The UI (`@sheetpane/formulas/ui`)

| slot | control |
|---|---|
| `cellbar` | View: `fx =B3*C3`, the selected cell's formula as read-only text. Edit: the grid's own cell input holds the formula, editable (retyping the file's formula restores the cell). A formula the file marks *Hidden* on a protected sheet shows neither |
| `status` | `Sum · Avg · Count` of the selection (formatted as the active cell); `⟳ N cells recalculated` (Edit); `Circular reference: B2` |
| `cell` | `⟳` recalculated · `↻` in a cycle · `≈` not calculable |
| `overlay` | in Edit, the ranges the selected formula reads, outlined and labelled in colour (`--sp-ref-1` … `--sp-ref-6`), following the formula as it is typed |

No font family is named anywhere (SR-LAW-5).

## Known limits (IronCalc 0.9.0)

- Values are read back at 15 significant digits (IronCalc has no raw-value
  getter); comparisons with Excel's 17-digit cache use a 1e-14 relative tolerance.
- The function probe in `test/parity.test.ts` lists where IronCalc disagrees
  with Excel: `AGGREGATE` (missing), `XLOOKUP` over array constants, and
  `TEXTJOIN` ignoring an empty *literal*.
- 1904-date workbooks: date functions over serial numbers are off by 1,462 days
  (IronCalc knows only the 1900 system).
- A half-typed formula evaluates to IronCalc's `#ERROR!`; Excel would refuse it.
- Typed formulas are exported as typed: a newer function needs Excel's `_xlfn.`
  prefix, which is not added.

Spec: [`work/open/W-16-formulas.md`](../../work/open/W-16-formulas.md).
How plugins plug in: [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../../work/compare/plugins.compare.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/styles/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/styles/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/styles

**Cell styles for sheetpane — fill, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, colour, size, borders, alignment, wrap — as a plugin on the `decorate` hook. Never a font family (SR-LAW-5): the host's font is the font.**

A plugin: it registers against the one in-memory workbook of `@sheetpane/grid`,
so `<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>` both see its effect. Versioned in
lockstep with `@sheetpane/grid` (a peer). No runtime dependencies.

| entry | what it gives |
|---|---|
| `@sheetpane/styles` | `styles()` — the headless plugin: `decorate` draws each cell as the workbook formats it, plus the reviewer's changes; `exportPatch` writes those changes into the file |
| `@sheetpane/styles/ui` | `ui()` — the format row and selection-bar controls; opt-in, Edit mode only |

```js
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { styles } from '@sheetpane/styles';
import { ui } from '@sheetpane/styles/ui';

el.workbook = createWorkbook({ plugins: [styles(), ui()] });
```

Or by attribute: `import '@sheetpane/styles/ui'` (it registers `styles` with its
controls; `import '@sheetpane/styles'` alone registers the headless plugin), then
`<sheetpane-excel plugins="styles">`.

## What a cell shows

`decorate(cell)` reads `cellXfs[s]` → `fonts`, `fills`, `borders`, `alignment`
and returns only these CSS properties:
`background-color`, `color`, `font-weight`, `font-style`, `font-size`,
`text-decoration`, `text-align`, `vertical-align`, `white-space`,
`border-top` / `-right` / `-bottom` / `-left`. Nothing else, ever.

- **Colours:** `rgb` (ARGB), theme colours with Excel's tint, indexed colours
  (the default 64-colour palette, or the file's `<indexedColors>`), `auto`.
- **The default font's size and colour are the host's**: only a size or colour
  that differs from the workbook's default font is drawn, so a plain cell stays
  plain (and dark themes keep their ink). Size scales the grid's own size by
  `sz / default`.
- A filled cell with automatic text is drawn in the workbook's default ink.
- Patterns blend by density; a gradient shows its midpoint; diagonal borders,
  indent and rotation are not drawn.

**Rich text:** a cell whose string has formatted runs (one italic word) is drawn
as spans through `decorateRuns` — each run's weight, style, decoration, size and
colour against the cell's own font, superscript and subscript at three quarters
of the size; never a font family. An edit writes plain text (the cell bar says
so first); untouched rich cells export byte for byte.

`styles({ fileStyles: false })` draws only the reviewer's own changes (rich text plain).

## The format row (`ui()`)

Groups, in order: **text** (Bold `Mod+B`, Italic `Mod+I`, Underline `Mod+U`,
Strikethrough `Mod+5`) · **colour** · **fill** · **border** (all, outside, one
side, thick or double bottom, none) · **align** (left `Mod+Shift+L`, centre
`Mod+Shift+E`, right `Mod+Shift+R`; top, middle, bottom; Merge / Unmerge) ·
**wrap** · **clear** (`Mod+\`). The selection bar adds Bold, Fill and
Merge / Unmerge. Every control restyles the whole selection as **one** undo step.
Merges are core: the merge control only calls `store.setMerge()`.

`ui({ colours, fills, highlight })` picks the swatch sets (`{ value: 'RRGGBB', label }`).
The default fills each keep the grid's changed-corner mark at 3:1 contrast.

## The change it makes

A change of kind `style` at the key `sheet!#style:A1` (not `sheet!A1`, which a
value change owns). Its `now` is a plain object, `StylePatch`:

```ts
{ clear?: true; b?: boolean; i?: boolean; u?: boolean; strike?: boolean;
  color?: 'RRGGBB' | null; fill?: 'RRGGBB' | null;
  border?: { top?, right?, bottom?, left?: { style, color? } | null };
  align?: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' | null; valign?: 'top' | 'middle' | 'bottom' | null;
  wrap?: boolean }
```

Fields the file already shows are dropped; a cell back to its file look has no
change. `clear` drops the file's font, fill, border and alignment; the number
format stays.

## Export

`exportPatch` appends deduplicated `<font>`, `<fill>`, `<border>` and `<xf>`
entries to `xl/styles.xml` (counts updated, every existing entry and every other
byte kept) and repoints `s` on each style-changed cell — adding `<c r s/>` where
the cell had no element. Untouched cells keep their `s`. A CSV carries no
styles, so a CSV is never restyled.

## For `@sheetpane/condfmt`

Exported for reuse: `resolveColor`, `applyTint`, `paletteOf`, `DEFAULT_THEME`,
`DEFAULT_INDEXED`, `ALLOWED_PROPS`, `allowListed`, `fontCss`, `fillCss`
(`{ dxf: true }` reads a dxf's solid `bgColor`), `borderCss`, `alignmentCss`,
`dxfCss`.

Spec: [`work/open/W-17-styles.md`](../../work/open/W-17-styles.md).
How plugins plug in: [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../../work/compare/plugins.compare.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.
