<!-- source: packages/validation/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/validation/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/validation

**The workbook's own data-validation rules, checked when the file loads and after every edit. Each cell that breaks a rule shows up as a warning in `<sheetpane-errors>`.**

A plugin for `@sheetpane/grid`. It reads the `<dataValidations>` the file's
author saved, including the x14 form Excel uses for lists on another sheet,
and runs them through the `validate` hook. `<sheetpane-excel>` and
`<sheetpane-errors>` on the same pane both see the result. On export it can
also write the host's rules file into the `.xlsx` as Excel's own dropdowns
and checks. No third-party runtime dependencies (`@sheetpane/export` writes
the rules and gives `shiftFormula`); `@sheetpane/grid` is a peer. Versioned in lockstep with it.

- `@sheetpane/validation`: the headless plugin (`validate`, and `exportPatch` for the rules file).
- `@sheetpane/validation/ui`: opt-in. Adds the list arrow and the status-line count.
- `@sheetpane/validation/check`: the same plugin with no registration, no
  element and no Download switch (checking only — `exportPatch` is the page
  entry's), and `check(bytes, options)` — `@sheetpane/grid/check`'s check with
  this plugin on: the workbook's own validation from Node or a worker.

  ```js
  import { check } from '@sheetpane/validation/check';
  const errors = await check(await readFile('budget.xlsx'), { name: 'budget.xlsx', severity: 'error' });
  ```

## Use

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@sheetpane/grid';
  import '@sheetpane/validation/ui'; // registers "validation" = rules + controls
</script>

<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" plugins="validation" src="/files/holdings.xlsx" mode="edit"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3"></sheetpane-errors>
```

Without a page, or without the controls:

```ts
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { validation, skippedRules } from '@sheetpane/validation';

const store = createWorkbook({ plugins: [validation({ severity: 'warning' })] });
await store.load(bytes, 'holdings.xlsx');
store.getErrors();      // one error per failing cell
skippedRules(store);    // { rules, checked, skipped: [{ sheet, sqref, type, reason, detail }] }
```

Importing `@sheetpane/validation` registers `validation` as the rules plugin
alone. Importing `/ui` re-registers it as the rules plus the controls.

## What a broken rule looks like

One error per failing cell. If a cell breaks two rules, the first one counts.

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `validation` |
| `severity` | `warning` (set another with `validation({ severity })`) |
| `author` | `workbook` |
| `range` | the cell, e.g. `B4` |
| `found` | the cell's current display text, or `(blank)` |
| `expected` | the rule in words (table below) |
| `message` | the rule's own `errorTitle: error`, or either one alone; otherwise the rule in words |

A workbook error resolves itself when its cell passes again and reopens if
the cell fails again (it keeps the same id). This is the only automatic
resolve in sheetpane; the store does it. `showErrorMessage="0"` rules are
still checked, because that flag only turns off Excel's popup.

## The rules, and the words a reviewer reads

| rule | passes when | `expected` |
|---|---|---|
| `whole` | the value is an integer and the operator holds | `whole number > 0` |
| `decimal` | the value is a number and the operator holds | `decimal between 0.00% and 2.00%` (operands in the cell's own number format) |
| `date` | the value is a date serial and the operator holds | `date between 01-Jul-2026 and 30-Sep-2026` |
| `time` | the value is a number (a fraction of a day) and the operator holds | `time between 09:00 and 18:00` |
| `textLength` | the length of the text holds against the operator | `text length ≤ 5 characters` |
| `list` | the text matches a choice (case-insensitive; a number also matches its number) | `list — Core, Income, Cap` (the first 8, then `… (n more)`) |
| `custom` | the formula is true at the cell | `custom — =A1>0` |

Operators: `between` (the default), `notBetween`, `equal` (`=`), `notEqual`
(`≠`), `greaterThan` (`>`), `lessThan` (`<`), `greaterThanOrEqual` (`≥`),
`lessThanOrEqual` (`≤`). `between` includes both ends.

What an operand can be:

- a number
- `DATE(y,m,d)` or `TIME(h,m,s)` with number arguments
- a quoted string
- a cell: `$G$1`, `Sheet2!B1`, or a relative `D1`, which shifts with each cell the same way it does in Excel
- a defined name that resolves to one of these
- `INDIRECT(<cell>)`: the cell named by that cell's text (see dependent lists below)

A cell operand is read live, so changing the limit re-checks the rule. An
empty operand cell reads as 0.

A `list` source can be:

- a literal list: `"a,b,c"`
- a range: `$H$1:$H$9`, `Lists!$A$1:$A$9`, `$A:$A`
- a defined name that resolves to a range
- an Excel table's column: `Units[Unit]` or `Units[[#Data],[Unit]]`, directly or
  through a defined name — the column's data rows, as the file stores the table

- `INDIRECT($A2)` — a **dependent list** (W-60): each row reads its parent
  cell's text and lists what it names — a defined name (any case; the sheet's
  own name before a global one), a table or table column (`Units[Unit]`), or
  an A1 range (`Lists!$B$2:$B$5`). `INDIRECT("Turbidity")` (quoted text) and
  `INDIRECT($A2, TRUE)` work too.

A range source is read live from the store, and the arrow's menu re-reads it
each time it opens.

### Dependent lists

Excel's pattern for *Unit depends on Parameter*: one defined name per
parameter (`Turbidity` → `Lists!$B$2:$B$3`) and `=INDIRECT($A2)` as the Unit
column's list source. The parent's text is read per row, live: change the
Parameter and the Unit is checked again in the same edit — a unit the new
parameter does not allow (an orphan) is a warning, and the arrow offers the
new parameter's units.

A parent that names nothing (blank, or text that is no name, such as
`Flow Rate`) gives no list. As in Excel, the child then passes under
`allowBlank` ("Ignore blank") and fails without it (`expected`:
`list — (A7 "Flow Rate" names no list)`). Names cannot hold spaces, so
workbooks wrap the parent in `SUBSTITUTE`; that, `&` and R1C1
(`INDIRECT($A2, FALSE)`) are not emulated — the rule is skipped (`source`).

Blank cells pass when the rule has `allowBlank`. Without it, they fail.
Cells are checked only inside the sheet's used range: its data plus any cell
the user changed. A rule on `B:B` therefore does not produce a million rows.

## What is not checked, and why (`skippedRules`)

| reason | what |
|---|---|
| `custom` | a `custom` rule when no formula plugin offers `evaluate()` (see below) |
| `operand` | an operand the subset above does not cover, e.g. `SUM(...)` or `INDIRECT(SUBSTITUTE(...))` |
| `operator` | an operator outside the eight above |
| `type` | an unknown rule type |
| `source` | a list source that is neither a list, a range, a name nor `INDIRECT` of one cell or quoted text (`OFFSET(...)`, `INDIRECT(SUBSTITUTE(...))`), or that names a missing sheet |

`skippedRules(store)` counts `custom` as checked when the pane has a formula
evaluator. `skippedRules(book)` has only the workbook to go on, so it counts
every `custom` rule as skipped. The status line adds `· n rules not checked`.

### Custom rules need a formula engine

`custom` rules run only when the pane's `derive` plugin (`@sheetpane/formulas`)
also exposes:

```ts
evaluate(formula: string, at: { sheet: string; ref: string }): boolean | number | string | null | undefined
```

The plugin passes the formula with its relative references already shifted to
the cell. `true` or a non-zero number passes. `false` or `0` fails. Anything
else counts as unknown, and the cell is not flagged.

## The rules file as Excel dropdowns (`rulesAsValidation`)

A host that checks its sheets with a rules file (`rules-src`, or
`excel.rules`) can hand the same rules to people who work in Excel. The
Download menu shows **Write rules as Excel dropdowns** while the pane has a
rules file or column rules; turned on, the `.xlsx` carries them as the
workbook's own data validation.

```ts
validation({ rulesAsValidation: true });          // the switch on at first (default: off)
await excel.export({ rulesAsValidation: true });  // or for one export
lastRulesWrite(excel.workbook?.book);             // { written, merged, skipped, conflicts }
rulesAsValidations(store);                        // the plan, without writing
```

| the rule says | Excel gets | skipped (code) |
|---|---|---|
| `oneOf`, `equals` | a dropdown list | a value with a comma, an empty list, over 255 characters (SP-5403) |
| `integer` / `number`, `min` / `max` | whole number / decimal | a bound that is not a number (SP-5404) |
| `date`, `min` / `max` | date | a bound not written `2026-01-31` or as a serial (SP-5404) |
| `minLength` / `maxLength` | text length | (SP-5404) |
| `boolean` | the list TRUE, FALSE | |
| `required` | "ignore blank" off (alone: text length ≥ 1) | |
| `pattern`, `noneOf`, `unique` | — | always (SP-5401) |
| two checks in one rule | — | always (SP-5402) |

A column rule covers its column from the row under the titles to the last
row; a cell rule its range. The rule's `message` is Excel's error text, the
rule in words its input prompt; `onInvalid: 'block'` is Excel's Stop, a
`note` its Information, anything else its Warning.

**The workbook's own rule wins.** Where the file already has a rule, the
written one leaves those cells and the conflict is listed (SP-5406); a rule
that checks the same thing joins the file's own instead of repeating it.
Excel 2010 `x14` rules stay where they are. A rules-file title the workbook
lacks is SP-5405. Every rule not written is a console warning with its code,
and the status line adds `· k rules not written to Excel`. `.xlsx` only.

## The controls (`/ui`)

- **List arrow** (`cell` slot, Edit only): appears in every cell a `list` rule
  covers. It opens the rule's current choices, and picking one sets the cell
  with `store.setCell`, which can be undone.
- **Status** (`status` slot, View and Edit): `3 validation warnings`, plus
  `· 1 rule not checked` when rules were skipped, plus `· 2 rules not written
  to Excel` after an export that wrote the rules file.

`<sheetpane-errors>` lists the rule rows with the reviewer's own errors. Its
author filter (Anyone · People · Workbook rules · File comments) shows only
the rule rows when you need them.

## Known limits

- A list whose source is on another sheet is re-checked when its own sheet
  changes, not when the source sheet changes. The arrow's menu is always
  current.
- A cell holding a formula is checked against its saved value. If the user
  typed the formula, the plugin uses the value the formula plugin derived. The
  check runs on the edit, before the formula plugin has finished deriving.
- `found` is fixed when the error is first made. If an error reopens, it shows
  the first failing value.

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/condfmt/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/condfmt/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/condfmt

**Conditional formatting for sheetpane — the file's own `<conditionalFormatting>` rules drawn as Excel draws them: value and text rules, duplicates, top / bottom, averages, colour scales, data bars and formula rules — as a plugin on the `decorate` hook, after `@sheetpane/styles`. Render only: nothing here writes a rule.**

A plugin: it registers against the one in-memory workbook of `@sheetpane/grid`,
so `<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>` both see its effect. Versioned in
lockstep with `@sheetpane/grid` and `@sheetpane/styles` (peers). No runtime
dependencies.

| entry | what it gives |
|---|---|
| `@sheetpane/condfmt` | `condfmt()` — the headless plugin: `decorate`, ordered after `styles`, draws each cell the rules hold for |
| `@sheetpane/condfmt/ui` | `ui()` — the legend and the count: the rule named on hover and in the cell bar, the rules counted in the status line |

```js
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { styles } from '@sheetpane/styles';
import { condfmt } from '@sheetpane/condfmt';
import { ui } from '@sheetpane/condfmt/ui';

el.workbook = createWorkbook({ plugins: [styles(), condfmt(), ui()] });
```

Or by attribute: `import '@sheetpane/condfmt/ui'` (it registers `condfmt` with
its UI; `import '@sheetpane/condfmt'` alone registers the headless plugin), then
`<sheetpane-excel plugins="styles condfmt">`.

## The rules it draws

| type | holds when |
|---|---|
| `cellIs` | the value compares to its operand(s) — `equal`, `notEqual`, `greaterThan`, `lessThan`, `greaterThanOrEqual`, `lessThanOrEqual`, `between`, `notBetween` (bounds in either order) |
| `containsText` · `notContainsText` · `beginsWith` · `endsWith` | the value as text, without case |
| `containsBlanks` · `notContainsBlanks` · `containsErrors` · `notContainsErrors` | the value is blank (or only spaces) / an error |
| `duplicateValues` · `uniqueValues` | the value appears more than once / once in the rule's range (text without case; blanks never count) |
| `top10` | in the top or bottom *n* (or *n* %) numbers of the range, ties included |
| `aboveAverage` | above (or, with `aboveAverage="0"`, below) the range's average |
| `colorScale` | 2 or 3 colours, interpolated in sRGB between thresholds |
| `dataBar` | a bar sized to the value |
| `expression` | its formula is TRUE or non-zero — with a formula engine only (below) |

Comparisons follow Excel: numbers < text < logicals, text without case, a blank
reads as 0 or empty text. Operands are numbers, `"text"`, `TRUE` / `FALSE`, or a
cell — absolute parts stay, relative parts shift with the cell from the
range's top-left. Any other operand is a formula, read through the engine.

**Priority** is one order per sheet, across every `<conditionalFormatting>`
block. A higher-priority rule wins each property it sets; a lower one fills in
the rest; a matching rule with `stopIfTrue` ends the walk. A rule with several
`sqref` areas is one range.

## What a cell shows

A rule's `dxf` goes through `@sheetpane/styles`' `dxfCss` and its allow-list:
`background-color`, `color`, `font-weight`, `font-style`, `font-size`,
`text-decoration`, the four borders. Because `condfmt` runs **after** `styles`,
the rule wins per property and the static style keeps the rest — a bold cell
with a yellow fill and a rule's red fill is bold and red.

- **Colour scale:** `background-color`. Thresholds: `min`, `max`, `num`,
  `percent` (of the range from min to max), `percentile` (`PERCENTILE.INC`),
  `formula`. Values beyond the end thresholds take the end colours; text and
  blanks take none.
- **Data bar:** `background-image`, a gradient from the bar's colour to a
  lighter tint, `minLength` (default 10 %) … `maxLength` (default 90 %) of the
  cell, linear between the low and high thresholds.
- A rule's fill with no text colour of its own takes the cell's static colour,
  else the workbook's default ink: the file's colours are data, drawn as saved
  in both themes.
- **Edit marks stay on top:** an error's ring is an inset shadow and its tint a
  `::before` overlay above the fill, so a flagged cell keeps its rule's fill.

Statistics a range rule needs (sorted numbers, sum, duplicate counts) are
computed once per range and kept; per-cell results are kept too. A change drops
only what depends on it: the changed cell, every cell of a range whose
statistics hold it, and — for rules that read other cells (a formula, a cell
operand) — their results. `evaluations(store)` counts both, for profiling.

## Formula rules

An `expression` rule — or a `cellIs` operand or a threshold that is a formula —
is read through the `derive` provider's synchronous `evaluate(formula, { sheet,
ref })`, which `@sheetpane/formulas` offers. Without one, the rule is **skipped
and counted**, never guessed. So are icon sets (`iconSet`, out of v1),
`timePeriod` and any other type outside the table above.

`skippedRules(storeOrWorkbook)` → `{ rules, shown, skipped: [{ sheet, sqref,
type, priority, reason, detail }] }`, `reason` one of `iconSet`, `formula`,
`type`, `malformed`.

## The legend and the count (`ui()`)

- **Hover:** a rule-coloured cell shows *Conditional: greater than 1000* and its
  range in a tooltip under the cell (an overlay that lets pointer events through
  to the cells).
- **Cell bar:** the selected cell's rules, in the same words — the legend a
  keyboard or a screen reader reaches.
- **Status:** *4 conditional rules from the file · 1 not shown*.

Colour never carries meaning alone.

## Also exported

`rulesOf(book, sheet)` (compiled, priority order), `ruleWords(rule, row, col)`,
`cellResult(store, sheet, row, col)`, `legendAt(store, sheet, row, col)`,
`shiftFormula`, `parseOperand`, `compareCells`, `percentile`, `scaleColor`,
`lerpColor`, `barLength`, `barImage`, `dxfStyle`.

Spec: [`work/open/W-19-condfmt.md`](../../work/open/W-19-condfmt.md).
How plugins plug in: [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../../work/compare/plugins.compare.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/images/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/images/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/images

**Images for sheetpane — pictures anchored in the sheet drawn in sheet space through the `overlay` hook; view only, kept on export.**

A plugin: it registers against the one in-memory workbook of `@sheetpane/grid`
(`createWorkbook({ plugins: [...] })`, or `plugins="images"` on the element), so
`<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>` both see its effect. Versioned in
lockstep with `@sheetpane/grid`.

```ts
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { images } from '@sheetpane/images';

el.workbook = createWorkbook({ plugins: [images()] });
// or: import '@sheetpane/images'  and  <sheetpane-excel plugins="images">
```

No runtime dependencies. Importing is safe in Node (no DOM until a picture renders).

## What it draws

Every `picture` in a sheet's drawing part, at its anchor, in the overlay layer: it scrolls,
zooms and clips with its cells, under the pins and above the cells. `alt` is the picture's
description (`descr`), else its name.

| format | shown as |
|---|---|
| PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP | an `<img>` over an object URL |
| SVG | an `<img>` too — never inline markup, so no script in the file can run |
| EMF, WMF, TIFF, anything else | a dashed frame the size of the anchor: `logo.emf — preview unavailable` |

The format is told from the bytes' header first and the file name second.

Charts and shapes are not pictures and are skipped (the charts plugin draws charts). The status
bar adds `2 pictures · 1 preview unavailable` for the sheet in view.

**View only.** In Edit a click on a picture selects the cell under the click, so that cell can
still be flagged; pictures cannot be moved, resized, added or deleted.

## Anchors (`src/anchors.ts`, exported)

EMU become pixels at 9,525 EMU per pixel (914,400 per inch, 96 px per inch), then are placed in
the grid's own geometry (`Geometry` — pixels at 100 % zoom from A1's top-left):

| anchor | rectangle |
|---|---|
| `twoCell` | `from` to `to`, each corner plus its offset |
| `oneCell` | `from` plus its offset, sized by `ext` |
| `absolute` | `pos` from the sheet origin, sized by `ext` |

An offset never reaches past its own cell, as in Excel. `anchorRect(anchor, geometry)`,
`pointToPx`, `cellAt`, `emuToPx` and `refOf` are plain functions with no DOM, so
`@sheetpane/charts` reuses them as they are.

**Excel's own row heights and hidden rows or columns are not used.** The grid draws every row at
its fixed height and shows what is stored, hidden or not; a picture anchored C4:F9 covers C4:F9
on screen, whatever size those cells are in Excel. A `oneCell` or `absolute` picture keeps its
`ext` in pixels, so beside tall Excel rows it can look smaller than it did there.

## Memory

Nothing is read from the file's media until a picture comes near the screen (a 20 MB photo costs
nothing until scrolled to). One object URL is made per media part however many pictures show it,
and all are revoked when the pane loads another workbook (or a load fails). A decode that
finishes after the workbook went makes no URL.

## Export

Patch-mode export leaves the drawing and media parts as they were (the fidelity ruling), so a
workbook's pictures survive a round trip. **A deleted row does not re-anchor pictures in v1**:
the file keeps the anchors it had.

## Tests

`pnpm exec vitest run --project images` — anchor arithmetic against geometry, rectangles against
the rendered cells (oneCell, twoCell, absolute, zoom), every format, laziness, object-URL
revocation. Fixtures are hand-written packages and the ExcelJS 2×2 PNG; files saved by Excel and
LibreOffice are owed by W-30.

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/charts/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/charts/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/charts

**Charts for sheetpane — each chart in a workbook shown at its anchor: a frame with its title, type, series count and Show source cells (stage 1), drawn as our own SVG for bar, column, line, pie and scatter (stage 2) — through the `overlay` hook.**

A plugin: it registers against the one in-memory workbook of `@sheetpane/grid`
(`createWorkbook({ plugins: [...] })`, or `plugins="charts"` on the element), so
`<sheetpane-excel>` and `<sheetpane-errors>` both see its effect. Versioned in
lockstep with `@sheetpane/grid`.

```ts
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { charts } from '@sheetpane/charts';
import { ui } from '@sheetpane/charts/ui';

el.workbook = createWorkbook({ plugins: [charts(), ui()] });
// stage 1 only (frames, no plot):  charts({ draw: false })
// or: import '@sheetpane/charts/ui'  and  <sheetpane-excel plugins="charts">
```

- `@sheetpane/charts` — the headless plugin: the `overlay` provider.
- `@sheetpane/charts/ui` — the status line and a keyboard shortcut; opt-in.

No runtime dependencies, no chart library. Importing is safe in Node: nothing touches the DOM
until a chart renders.

## The frame (stage 1)

Every `graphicFrame` in a sheet's drawing that holds a chart (`c:chart r:id` → the chart part)
becomes one overlay item at its anchor, scrolling and zooming with its cells. The frame shows:

- the **title** — `c:title` rich text (runs joined, paragraphs joined by a space), a title
  reference's cached text, the only series' name when the title has no text, else `Chart`;
- the **type and series count** — `column · 2 series`, `stacked bar · 3 series`,
  `100% stacked column`, `line`, `pie`, `doughnut`, `scatter`, `area`, `radar`, `3-D column`,
  `column + line` (a combination) …;
- **Show source cells** — selects the plotted cells (see below), in View and in Edit;
- **data changed — Excel will redraw**, once a user change (`value` or `formula`) lands in a
  cell the chart reads — a series' values, categories or name. Undo takes it away again.

A chart that is not drawn lists `Not drawn here: area chart.` and, per series, the cells it
reads: `Sales — Data!A2:A5, Data!B2:B5`.

**Show source cells** selects the union of the series' `c:f` ranges when they tile one
rectangle (categories in A, values in B and C → `A2:C5`). The grid's selection is one
rectangle, so ranges that do not tile one (categories in E, values in H) select the first
series' values. A chart whose data is literal (`c:numLit`, no `c:f`) has nothing to select and
its button is disabled.

In Edit, a click on the chart away from its button selects the cell under the click, so that
cell can be flagged — as pictures do.

## The drawing (stage 2)

| type | drawn |
|---|---|
| `c:barChart`, `c:barDir="col"` | column — clustered, stacked or 100 % stacked |
| `c:barChart`, `c:barDir="bar"` | bar — the same groupings; the first category at the bottom, as in Excel |
| `c:lineChart` | line — standard, stacked or 100 % stacked; a missing point breaks the line |
| `c:pieChart`, `c:doughnutChart` | pie and doughnut — the first series, clockwise from `c:firstSliceAng` (12 o'clock) |
| `c:scatterChart` | scatter — x from `c:xVal` (text x values plot at 1, 2, 3 … as in Excel); lines when the style and the series' line say so |

Everything else — area, radar, stock, surface, bubble, 3-D, pie-of-pie, combination charts and
pivot charts — stays a stage-1 frame.

The SVG has a title band, a value axis with "nice" ticks (1, 2, 2.5 or 5 × 10ⁿ; zero included
unless the data sit in a narrow band far from it, as Excel does), category labels thinned so
they do not overlap, and a legend where the chart has one (`c:legend`: right, or bottom when
`legendPos` is top or bottom, or the chart is narrow). A negative bar is drawn in the error red
(the design board). Percent axes follow a `%` in the value axis' number format.

**Colours** come from the series' explicit fill (`c:spPr/a:solidFill` — `a:srgbClr`,
`a:schemeClr` through the workbook theme, `a:sysClr`, with `lumMod`, `lumOff`, `tint`,
`shade`), a line chart's line colour, per-point fills (`c:dPt`), else Excel's default style:
the theme's accents 1–6 by series index (`c:idx`) — or by point for `varyColors` pies — then
darker and lighter rounds. A workbook without a theme gets Office's accents.

**Values** are the series' cached points (`c:numCache`, `c:strCache`): what Excel drew when the
file was saved. With a `derive` plugin on the pane (`@sheetpane/formulas`), the chart reads the
live cells instead (`store.value`, `store.text` for labels) and redraws as they change; the SVG
carries `data-values="live"` or `"cache"`. Without one, an edit leaves the drawing as Excel
saved it, and the tag says so.

The SVG uses a `viewBox` the size of the anchor at 100 % and fills the item, so it scales with
zoom exactly as the cells do. Every mark carries what it stands for (`data-series`,
`data-point`, `data-value`; slices `data-start`/`data-end` in degrees), so tests compare the
drawing with the values rather than with pixels. No font is named anywhere (SR-LAW-5): the text
is the host's. Text from the file is escaped; colours from the file are validated `#RRGGBB`.

## Names

The item is `role="img"`; its `aria-label` is the chart's title once the part is read (the
drawing's description or name before that), and the SVG carries the same `role`, `aria-label`
and `<title>`.

## `@sheetpane/charts/ui`

- **Status line:** `Chart source: Data!A2:A5, Data!B2:B5, Data!C2:C5` while the selection lies in
  a chart's plotted cells or under its frame; otherwise `2 charts` on a sheet that has some.
- **Mod+Shift+U** shows the source of the chart over the active cell, or of the sheet's only
  chart — listed in the grid's keyboard help. The frame's own button sits inside the grid's
  `role="img"` overlay wrapper, where assistive technology does not reach it; the shortcut is the
  accessible route to the same action.

There is no `selbar` button: a selbar control has no "applies here" test, so it would show on
every selection, chart or not.

## Export

Nothing. Patch-mode export copies the chart parts byte for byte, so Excel redraws each chart
from the (possibly changed) cells when the file is opened.

## Limits

- **Placement uses the grid's geometry** (28 px rows, every row and column shown), as pictures
  do — not Excel's row heights. Past the last column the grid draws, columns count 64 px each.
- One rectangle per selection (above). Data labels, trendlines, error bars, axis titles,
  secondary axes, log scales and date axes are not drawn.
- Only charts on worksheets; chartsheets hold no cells and are not read.
- No chart is ever edited: no type switcher, no series editor, no resize.

## Dependencies

Anchors are placed with `@sheetpane/images`' `anchorRect` and `cellAt` (SR-IMAGES decision 3); `@sheetpane/images` is a peer.

Spec: [`work/open/W-21-charts.md`](../../work/open/W-21-charts.md).
How plugins plug in: [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../../work/compare/plugins.compare.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/comments/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/comments/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/comments

**Excel's comments and sheetpane's errors, in both directions. When a file loads, its notes and threaded comments show up in `<sheetpane-errors>`. When you export, every error in the review goes into the file as an Excel threaded comment on its cell.**

A plugin for `@sheetpane/grid`. It works through the `validate` and
`exportPatch` hooks of the one in-memory workbook, so `<sheetpane-excel>` and
`<sheetpane-errors>` on the same pane both see it. No runtime dependencies;
`@sheetpane/grid` is a peer. Versioned in lockstep with it. There is no
`/ui` entry, because the plugin adds no controls.

## Use

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@sheetpane/grid';
  import '@sheetpane/comments'; // registers "comments"
</script>

<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" plugins="comments" src="/files/holdings.xlsx" mode="edit" author="Arpit"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3"></sheetpane-errors>
```

Without a page:

```ts
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { comments } from '@sheetpane/comments';

const plugin = comments();                  // comments({ write: false }) reads only
const store = createWorkbook({ plugins: [plugin] });
await store.load(bytes, 'holdings.xlsx');
store.getErrors();                          // the file's notes and threads, as `file` notes
const { blob } = await store.exportFile();  // the review written in as threaded comments
plugin.lastExport;                          // { written: [ids], skipped: [{ id, reason }] }
```

## What is read

The plugin reads every legacy note (`xl/comments*.xml`) and every threaded
comment (`xl/threadedComments/*`). Each commented cell becomes one entry in
the error list:

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `comment` (shown as "Comment") |
| `severity` | `note` |
| `author` | `file`. The pane filters these as "File comments". |
| `range` | the cell |
| `found` | the cell's display text from the upload, or `(blank)` |
| `expected` | `''` |
| `message` | the note, or the whole thread: the first comment, then each reply in order, one per line, each starting with its author's name (`R. Mehta: …`). Thread names come from the file's person list; note names come from its authors list. |
| `status` | `open` |

File notes are read-only in both elements: they show **Show in sheet** but no
Resolve or Delete. They never resolve themselves.

For each thread, Excel also writes a legacy note with the author `tc={id}`.
That note is not listed a second time.

## What is written

On export, every error that did **not** come from the file is written:
people's errors, workbook-rule errors and host-rule errors. Each one is
anchored at the top-left cell of its range. Results — `pass` and `skipped`
(not checked) entries — are left out, so a downloaded review stays a list of
problems; `export({ includeResults: true })` writes them too, headed
`Passed` or `Not checked`.

- **The thread.** The first comment holds a header line (`ERR-0003 · Error · Wrong value · Found: 7.5%`) followed by the `message`. If the error has an `expected`, it follows as a reply (`Should be: 0.75%`). The thread is marked `done="1"` when the error is resolved.
- **One comment per cell.** If several errors share a cell, they form one thread: the first error opens it and the rest follow as replies. It is marked done only when all of them are resolved.
- **A cell that already holds someone's thread.** The errors are added to that thread as replies.
- **A cell that already holds a legacy note.** Nothing is written there, because a cell holds one comment and the note stays untouched. The error appears in `plugin.lastExport.skipped` with the reason `note-at-cell`.

Each sheet with errors gets four parts:

| part | what |
|---|---|
| `xl/threadedComments/threadedCommentN.xml` | the threads (Excel 365) |
| `xl/commentsN.xml` | a legacy comment per thread (author `tc={thread id}`). Its text is Excel's `[Threaded comment]` placeholder, followed by the comment and its replies, so Excel 2019 and older can show something. |
| `xl/drawings/vmlDrawingN.vml` | the hidden note shape Excel needs before it shows any comment, plus `<legacyDrawing>` in the sheet |
| `xl/persons/person.xml` | one person per author, for the whole workbook |

The plugin also adds the four relationships and content types. **A part the
file already has is extended, never replaced:** its notes, threads, shapes,
persons and anything else it holds are kept. If a part cannot be read, that
sheet's parts are left exactly as they were and its errors are reported as
`unreadable-part`.

No font is written. The legacy comment text is a plain `<t>`, and the VML
shape copies the one Excel writes, which names no font (SR-LAW-5).

### Ids: export twice, get one thread

Each thread entry's `id` is a version-5 UUID made from the error's `id` and
`createdAt`. Here is how that plays out:

1. You export a review.
2. You load the exported file and restore the same review with `setErrors(saved)`.
3. You export again.

The second export **replaces** the review's own threads instead of adding
copies. Replies that someone added in Excel stay attached to the thread.
After the review is restored, its own threads are no longer listed as file
notes. Without the restore, the threads come back as `file` notes, which is
how a reviewer sees an earlier review. `createdAt` is part of the name
because error ids restart at `ERR-0001` every session.

### Author names go into the file

Each error's `author` is written into the file as a person's `displayName`
and `userId`, with `providerId="None"`. An empty author is written as
**"Reviewer"**. The `author` attribute is the only source. If the names are
personal data the file should not carry, either set `author` to something
neutral or switch writing off.

## Switching writing off

- `comments({ write: false })`: never write. Notes and threads are still read.
- `export({ comments: false })` on `<sheetpane-excel>` (or `store.exportFile({ options: { comments: false } })`): skip the parts for that one export.
- **Review layers** (W-51): an export writes the errors of the layers shown — what the layers switch or the `layers` attribute chose. `export({ layers: ['validation', 'pdf'] })` writes the layers named instead, whatever is shown; `layers: []` writes none.

There is no menu item for this. The host decides, and a host that wants an
end-user toggle can put one in its own `format-row` slot.

## Not yet checked

Whether **Excel 365, Excel 2019 and LibreOffice** open an exported file and
show every error at its cell is checked by the decider, on fixtures saved
from Excel (W-30). The parts follow the shapes Excel writes, but these tests
check the parts sheetpane writes and reads, not Excel itself.

Spec: [`work/open/W-22-comments.md`](../../work/open/W-22-comments.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/visibility/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/visibility/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/visibility

**Hide and unhide rows, columns and sheets in `<sheetpane-excel>` — as changes, written into the download.**

The grid already honours what a file hides, marks it (◂▸ / ▴▾ on the headers, a double line, a
*⊘ n hidden* button for sheets) and lets anyone show it for viewing. This plugin adds editing, in
Edit:

```js
import '@sheetpane/visibility/ui';
excel.setAttribute('plugins', 'visibility');
```

| action | where | Windows / Linux | Mac |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hide rows / columns | the selection bar, the cell and header menus | Ctrl+Alt+9 / Ctrl+Alt+0 | ⌘⌥9 / ⌘⌥0 |
| Unhide rows / columns (select across the gap) | the same, and a click on a marker | Ctrl+Shift+9 / Ctrl+Shift+0 | ⌘⇧9 / ⌘⇧0 |
| Group / Ungroup (outline) | the selection bar, the header menu | Alt+Shift+→ / Alt+Shift+← | ⌥⇧→ / ⌥⇧← |
| Hide sheet | right-click a tab (or Shift+F10 on it) | — | — |
| Unhide sheet | the banner on a hidden sheet opened from *⊘ n hidden* | — | — |

Excel's own Ctrl+9 / Ctrl+0 belong to the browser, so the keys are Google Sheets'. On Windows,
Ctrl+Shift+0 is often taken by the input-language hotkey — the header menu always works.

- **Changes:** hiding is counted once per sheet and axis, undoable, and the download carries it
  (`patchXlsx`'s `hidden` option). Revealing for viewing never is.
- **Rules:** the last visible sheet cannot be hidden ("A workbook needs one visible sheet"); a CSV
  stores no hidden state, so the controls are disabled there; a workbook whose structure the file
  protects keeps its sheets — Hide sheet (and the banner's Unhide) is disabled with the reason
  until the host sets `protection="ignore"`.
- **Headless:** `visibility()` from `@sheetpane/visibility`, and the actions `setSpanHidden`,
  `setSheetHidden`, `hiddenIn`, `canHideSheet`, `spanOf`, `sheetBlockedReason`.

Spec: [SR-VISIBILITY](../../records/0121_VISIBILITY.md). MIT.

<!-- source: packages/tables/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/tables/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/tables

**Excel tables in `<sheetpane-excel>`, drawn as their style draws them — header row, banded rows and columns, totals row.**

A table (a ListObject — *Insert › Table* in Excel) is read by `@sheetpane/import` whether or not
this plugin is on: every sheet carries its `tables` (name, range, header and totals rows, columns,
style). This plugin only draws them:

```js
import '@sheetpane/grid';
import '@sheetpane/tables'; // registers `tables`
excel.setAttribute('plugins', 'tables styles');
```

or `createWorkbook({ plugins: [tables()] })`.

| a table's | drawn |
|---|---|
| header row | bold; filled in the style's colour with light text (Medium), or a line under it (Light) |
| banded rows / columns | every other data row or column filled in a light tint of the style's colour |
| first / last column | bold, when the table turns it on |
| totals row | bold, under a double line |
| lines | Light: over and under the table; Medium: under every row |

- **Styles:** `TableStyleLight1`–`7` and `TableStyleMedium1`–`7`, in the workbook's theme colours
  (style 1 in the dark text colour, 2–7 in accents 1–6) — `TABLE_STYLES`. Any other style (Light
  8–21, Medium 8–28, Dark, a custom style) draws a bold header row only; a table with no style
  draws nothing, as Excel's *None*.
- **Order:** a cell's own format (`@sheetpane/styles`) and a conditional format
  (`@sheetpane/condfmt`) draw over the table's style, as in Excel, whatever order `plugins` lists
  them in.
- **Draw-only:** no control, no change, nothing written — a download keeps the file's table parts
  as they were.
- **Headless helpers:** `tableAt(sheet, row, col)`, `findTable(book, name)`, `tableCss(table, row,
  col, theme)`, `paletteOf(style, theme)`.

**Structured references** — `Units[Name]`, `Units[[#Data],[Name]]` — are resolved by
`@sheetpane/export`'s `resolveStructuredRef`, which `@sheetpane/validation` uses for list sources:
a dropdown over a table column reads the table's cells, with or without this plugin.

Spec: [SR-TABLES](../../records/0122_TABLES.md). MIT.

<!-- source: packages/compare/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/compare/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/compare

**What changed between two versions of a workbook — on the sheet in `<sheetpane-excel>`, or as data in Node.**

Pick the base version (the last approved one) and the pane shows what changed since: changed
cells amber, added rows green, moved rows blue, a red line where rows were removed. The status line
sums it up — *Compared with spec-v1.xlsx: 2 sheets · 5 rows · 3 cells changed* — and every change is
an entry in the errors list. Both files are read in the page; nothing is sent anywhere.

```js
import '@sheetpane/compare/ui';
excel.setAttribute('plugins', 'compare');   // Compare… in the cell bar picks the base file

// or the host hands it the base (bytes, a File, or a workbook already read)
import { compareWith } from '@sheetpane/compare/ui';
await compareWith(excel.workbook, baseBytes, { name: 'spec-v1.xlsx', key: 'Account' });
```

| control | where | keys |
|---|---|---|
| Compare… / Compare with another file… | the cell bar (View and Edit) | — |
| Previous change · Next change (wraps) | the cell bar | Alt+Shift+F5 · Alt+F5 |
| Stop comparing | the cell bar | — |
| the summary | the status line | — |

## Headless

```js
import { read } from '@sheetpane/import';
import { diffWorkbooks, summaryText, applyDiff } from '@sheetpane/compare';

const d = diffWorkbooks(await read(was), await read(now), { key: 'Account' });
summaryText(d.summary);    // "2 sheets · 5 rows · 3 cells changed"
d.sheets[0].rows;          // { op: 'added' | 'removed' | 'changed' | 'moved', a?, b?, … }
d.sheets[0].cells;         // { ref: 'D4', was: { value, text, formula? }, now: { … }, what: ['value', 'text'] }
```

- **Sheets** match by name; an unmatched sheet whose rows are mostly another's is *renamed*
  (`renameThreshold`, default 0.5); the rest are added or removed.
- **Columns** match by header title when both header rows hold distinct titles (a renamed title
  pairs with the one column left over), otherwise by position.
- **Rows** match by `key` columns (titles or letters, for every sheet or `{ Sheet: 'ID', '*': … }`)
  — then a row that changed place is *moved*. Without a key, rows are aligned (patience anchors and
  Myers' diff, alike rows paired as *changed*) and a row that changed place is removed and added:
  *moved* is said only when it is certain.
- **Cells** differ by value, display text (a number format) or formula — compared relative to the
  cell, so a formula that only shifted with its row is not a change.
- Also: merges, rows and columns newly hidden or shown, the sheet's state, and the counts of
  data-validation and conditional-format rules.
- `applyDiff(a, d)` rebuilds the newer version's values from the older one — the property the tests
  check on random workbooks. 50,000 rows diff in about 0.1 s (the budget is 0.5 s).

**Agents:** `@sheetpane/mcp`'s `diff_workbooks` tool runs the same function on two paths.

## Notes

- The comparison is the file **as loaded** against the base; edits made in the pane since are not
  part of it. Loading another file into the pane compares it with the same base.
- The changes are listed as the `compare` review layer (`COMPARE_LAYER`): the review is left as
  it is and undo is kept; the errors panel's layer switch shows them apart. `@sheetpane/comments`
  writes them into a download only when `export({ layers: [..., 'compare'] })` names the layer.
- The tints are `--sp-compare-added`, `--sp-compare-changed`, `--sp-compare-moved` and
  `--sp-compare-removed`; set them to restyle.

Spec: [SR-COMPARE](../../records/0124_COMPARE.md). MIT.


---

<!-- source: packages/review/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/review/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/review

**The review written into the download as a sheet of its own. Every error is listed on a *Review* sheet with a link to its cell. Optionally, each flagged cell is filled by severity, so a reviewer can work the list in Excel, fix the file and upload it again.**

A plugin for `@sheetpane/grid`. It uses one hook, `exportPatch`, on the
in-memory workbook, so it works for `<sheetpane-excel>` and for a store with
no page. `@sheetpane/grid` is a peer and `@sheetpane/export` is a dependency.
Versioned in lockstep with them. There is no `/ui` entry: the plugin adds two
items to the Download menu and nothing else. Everything is written into the
bytes the browser saves. Nothing is sent anywhere (SR-LAW-11).

## Use

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@sheetpane/grid';
  import '@sheetpane/review'; // registers "review"
</script>

<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" plugins="review" src="/files/holdings.xlsx" mode="edit" author="Arpit"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3"></sheetpane-errors>
```

The Download menu gains **Add a Review sheet** (on by default) and **Colour
flagged cells** (off by default). Each one applies to the next download.

Without a page:

```ts
import { createWorkbook } from '@sheetpane/grid';
import { review } from '@sheetpane/review';

const plugin = review({ fill: true });           // colour flagged cells by default
const store = createWorkbook({ plugins: [plugin] });
await store.load(bytes, 'holdings.xlsx');
const { blob } = await store.exportFile();        // the file, plus a Review sheet
plugin.lastExport;                                // { sheet, listed, counts, filled, skipped }
```

## Options

| option | default | what |
|---|---|---|
| `sheet` | `true` | Add the Review sheet. `export({ review: false })` leaves it out of one export. |
| `fill` | `false` | Colour each flagged cell. `export({ reviewFills: true })` colours one export. |
| `sheetName` | `'Review'` | The sheet's name. Characters Excel forbids are dropped, and the name is cut to 31 characters. |
| `severities` | `['error', 'warning', 'note']` | The severities listed and coloured. Results such as `pass` and `skipped` are written only when you name them. `export({ reviewSeverities })` overrides it for one export. |
| `layers` | every layer | The layers listed and coloured. An error with no `layer` belongs to `review`. `export({ reviewLayers })` overrides it for one export. |
| `fills` | pale red, yellow, blue | A fill per severity, as `#RRGGBB`, `RRGGBB` or ARGB. `null` turns a severity's fill off. A value that is not a colour throws SP-5005. |

## The Review sheet

One row per error, below a header row that stays frozen. The workbook's own
errors come first. Then, for each sheet in the file's order, its whole-sheet
errors, then its cells from top to bottom and left to right.

| column | value |
|---|---|
| ID | `ERR-0003` |
| Sheet | the sheet's name; empty for an error about the workbook |
| Cell | `I6` or `A14:J14`, as a link that opens the cell in Excel. A whole-sheet error reads *Whole sheet* and links to its A1. A workbook error reads *Whole workbook* and has no link. |
| Severity · Type | `Error` · `Wrong value` |
| Found · Expected · Message · Author | as in the review |
| Status | `Open`, `Resolved` or `Accepted` |
| Accepted · Accepted by · Accepted at | for an accepted error: *Accepted: \<reason\>*, who accepted it and when (UTC) |

- **A user's own sheet is never overwritten.** If the file already has a
  sheet called *Review* (in any case), the new one is *Review (2)*.
- **The file's own comments are not listed.** These are errors with `author:
  'file'`, which came from the file in the first place.
- **Every cell is an inline string.** `sharedStrings.xml` is never touched,
  and the links are internal hyperlinks, which need no relationship.
- **No font is written** (SR-LAW-5). The header row is marked with a grey
  fill instead of bold text.

## Uploading an annotated file again

A hidden, workbook-scoped defined name, `_sheetpane_review`, marks the sheet.
`reviewSheetOf(book)` reads that name, so a host can leave the sheet out:

```ts
import { read } from '@sheetpane/import';
import { reviewSheetOf } from '@sheetpane/review';

const book = await read(bytes, { name: 'holdings.xlsx' });
const skip = reviewSheetOf(book);                  // 'Review', or undefined
const data = book.sheets.filter((s) => s.name !== skip);
```

When a file that already has a Review sheet is exported again, the plugin
rewrites that sheet in place rather than adding a second one. There is one
exception: if someone gave the sheet parts of its own in Excel, such as
comments or a drawing, it is left alone and a new sheet is added.

## Colouring flagged cells

Each **open** error at a cell has its cells filled by severity. **Accepted**
and **resolved** errors are not problems, so they are never filled.
Whole-sheet and workbook errors are listed but not coloured. They appear in
`lastExport.skipped` as `no-cell`.

- **The cell's own format stays.** Its `xf` is cloned with a solid fill and
  the cell points at the clone, so the number format, font, borders and
  alignment are kept. One clone is made per format and colour. Existing
  formats and fills are never edited, only added to.
- **Nothing else changes.** Only the `s` of a flagged cell is written. Every
  other row and cell keeps its exact bytes. A flagged cell the file does not
  have is added empty, styled from its row or column.
- **Two errors on one cell:** the worse severity's fill wins.
- **A range over 10,000 cells** colours only the cells the file already has
  in it (`range-capped`, SP-5003).
- **No styles part:** nothing is coloured (`no-styles`, SP-5004), and the
  sheet is still written.

## What it does not do

- It writes into an `.xlsx` download of an `.xlsx`. A CSV, or a CSV converted
  to `.xlsx`, carries no plugin parts.
- An empty review writes nothing.
- Whether Excel opens the file without a repair prompt and follows each link
  to its cell is checked by the decider on real Excel (W-30). These tests
  check the parts sheetpane writes and reads, not Excel itself.

Spec: [SR-REVIEW](../../records/0123_REVIEW.md). MIT.

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/fixtures/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/fixtures/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/fixtures

**Known workbooks for testing a sheetpane host — and a manifest that says what is in each.**

```js
import { bytes, url, path, info, MANIFEST } from '@sheetpane/fixtures';

excel.file = new Blob([await bytes('showcase.xlsx')]);     // browser or Node
excel.src = url('showcase.xlsx').href;                     // a URL your bundler copies
fs.readFileSync(path('csv/semicolon.csv'));                // Node
info('showcase.rules.json').errors;                        // the cells the rules sample fails
```

| file | what it holds |
|---|---|
| `showcase.xlsx` | one sheet per plugin: Numbers, Styles, Formulas, Validation, CondFmt, Images, Charts, Comments |
| `showcase.rules.json` | a rules file (SR-GRID 22d) that fails six cells of the showcase |
| `dependent-lists.xlsx` | dependent dropdowns: a Unit list `=INDIRECT($A2)` over one defined name per parameter; one stale unit (`Readings!C6`) |
| `protected.xlsx` | sheet protection (password `sheetpane`): Spec's Value, Unit and Description open, Parameter locked, Limit a hidden formula; Lists locked; Notes open; the structure locked, Archive hidden |
| `edge/*.xlsx` | an empty sheet, a hidden sheet, non-ASCII names, a merged range, the 1904 date system, cached formula errors |
| `edge/legacy.xls`, `edge/not-a-zip.xlsx` | files sheetpane refuses (SR-LAW-3) |
| `csv/*.csv` | comma, semicolon, tab, BOM, quoted fields with newlines, cells the formula guard escapes |

`hugeCsv(rows)` makes the 250,000-row case on demand — it is a generator, not a file.

Every file is **hand-built** by `scripts/make.mjs` (parts written as XML and
zipped by `@sheetpane/export`'s `writeZip`; `just fixtures` rewrites them,
byte for byte the same). Hand-built files prove behaviour, not Excel
compatibility: files saved by Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice and Numbers
join with the app named in `appSaved` (W-30). No dependencies.

The spec is the record [SR-FIXTURES](../../records/0115_FIXTURES.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

# @sheetpane/testing

**Test helpers for apps that embed sheetpane — Playwright and Vitest browser mode, one API.**

```ts
// Playwright
import { sheetpane } from '@sheetpane/testing/playwright';
import { matchers } from '@sheetpane/testing';
expect.extend(matchers);

test('a reviewer edits and downloads', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/review');
  const sp = sheetpane(page);                       // the first <sheetpane-excel>, or { excel: 'css' }
  await sp.waitForLoad();
  await sp.edit({ column: 'Units', row: 4 }, '42');  // by title and row, or 'Sheet1!B4'
  await sp.flag('B5', { expected: '101.20', message: 'Stale price' });
  expect(await sp.errors()).toHaveError({ ref: 'B5', status: 'open' });
  expect(await sp.readDownload()).toHaveCell('Sheet1!F4', 42);
});
```

```ts
// Vitest browser mode: the same API on the element
import { sheetpane } from '@sheetpane/testing/dom';
const sp = sheetpane(document.querySelector('sheetpane-excel')!);
```

| helper | does |
|---|---|
| `waitForLoad()` | until `sheetpane-load` (ready) and the rule checks have finished |
| `ref(at)`, `select(at)`, `value(at)`, `text(at)` | a cell by `B3`, `Sheet1!B3` or `{ column, row }` (the title from `header-row`) |
| `edit(at, text)`, `paste(at, rows)`, `undo()`, `switchSheet(name)` | as a person would: the cell bar, a paste, the toolbar, the tabs |
| `flag(at, { type, severity, message, expected })`, `resolve(at \| index)` | the form in `<sheetpane-errors>` (or inline when none is connected) |
| `download()`, `readDownload()` | presses Download; the file, or its values |
| `readFile(bytes, name)`, `changesBetween(a, b)`, `valueAt(book, 'Sheet1!B2')` | `.xlsx` / `.csv` as values — in Node too (no DOM needed) |
| `matchers.toHaveCell`, `matchers.toHaveError` | for `expect.extend` (Vitest and Playwright) |

The helpers find things only by roles, labels and the grid's committed
`data-sp-*` hooks (SR-GRID decision 9a), never CSS classes — so a host's tests
survive restyling. Known files to test with: `@sheetpane/fixtures`.

The spec is the record [SR-TESTING](../../records/0118_TESTING.md).

**Using an AI coding agent?** `npx sheetpane-skills install` puts sheetpane's skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex into your repository.

<!-- source: packages/skills/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/skills/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/skills

**sheetpane's agent skills for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex — and the installer that puts them in your repository.**

```sh
npx sheetpane-skills install            # for every tool whose folder already exists here
npx sheetpane-skills install --all      # .claude/, .kiro/ and .agents/
npx sheetpane-skills uninstall          # removes exactly what install wrote
npx sheetpane-skills check-rules q3.rules.json   # a rules file checked as <sheetpane-excel> will
```

Every `@sheetpane/*` package depends on this one, and `@sheetpane/grid` exposes
the same `sheetpane-skills` command, so it is there once sheetpane is.

| what | where it lands |
|---|---|
| 25 skills — embed, react, load-export, errors, events, column-rules, rules-file, plugins, theming, testing, troubleshoot, … and the `sheetpane` router | `.claude/skills/`, `.kiro/skills/`, `.agents/skills/` |
| three of them run as commands with an argument: `/sheetpane-embed [framework]`, `/sheetpane-rules [workbook or rules file]`, `/sheetpane-test [workbook]` (in Codex `$sheetpane-embed …`) | the same skill folders |
| a hook that runs `check-rules` after the agent writes a `*.rules.json` and hands the `SP-60xx` problems back | a `PostToolUse` group in `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json`; `.kiro/hooks/sheetpane-rules.json` (`PostFileSave`) |
| the `@sheetpane/mcp` server | the `sheetpane` key of `.mcp.json` / `.kiro/settings/mcp.json`; a block in `.codex/config.toml` |
| a short block saying what sheetpane is and which skill to start with | between `<!-- sheetpane:start -->` and `<!-- sheetpane:end -->` in `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` — nothing outside it is touched |
| a Kiro steering file and a `sheetpane-integrator` agent for Claude and Kiro | `.kiro/steering/`, `.claude/agents/`, `.kiro/agents/` |

- Nothing is written on `npm install` (no `postinstall`); only when you run it.
- A file you changed since it was installed is never overwritten without
  `--force`; `--dry-run` lists every path first. What was written is listed in
  `.sheetpane-skills.json`.
- `--skip contributor` leaves out the two skills for contributing to sheetpane
  itself; `--only`, `--skills-only`, `--no-mcp`, `--no-hooks` narrow further.
- In JSON configs the hook is found by its exact command, the MCP server by
  its `sheetpane` key; every other key stays, and `uninstall` puts the file
  back as it was. Codex runs a project hook only once you trust it in `/hooks`.
- Re-run it after upgrading `@sheetpane/*` so the skills match the version.

## check-rules

```sh
npx sheetpane-skills check-rules sheetpane.rules.json other.rules.json
```

One line per problem, `SP-60xx: message (file)` — the same checks and codes
`<sheetpane-excel>` applies when it loads the file (SP-6010 to SP-6021; a
sheet, title or cell the workbook lacks shows only once a workbook is loaded).
Exit 0 clean, 1 a problem, 2 a usage or read error. As a hook,
`--hook claude|codex|kiro` reads the edited path from the agent's hook input,
ignores every other file, and prints problems to stderr with exit 2 so the
agent reads them. It reads the one file, writes nothing, uses no network.

## Claude Code plugin

The same host skills, the `sheetpane-integrator` agent, the hook and the MCP
server, as one plugin from this repository's marketplace:

```text
/plugin marketplace add arpitarya/sheetpane
/plugin install sheetpane@sheetpane
```

Its files under `plugins/sheetpane/` are generated from this package by
`just plugin`; a test fails when they are stale.

Each skill points to the sheetpane record it summarises and never restates a
rule as its own; a test fails if a skill names an attribute, member or event
the elements do not have. The spec is the record
[SR-SKILLS](../../records/0116_SKILLS.md).

<!-- source: packages/mcp/README.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/packages/mcp/README.md) -->

# @sheetpane/mcp

**A Model Context Protocol server for sheetpane: agents ask, it answers from what ships — never a guess.**

```bash
npx -y @sheetpane/mcp        # stdio; any MCP client
npx sheetpane-skills install # registers it for Claude Code, Kiro and Codex (with the skills)
```

| tool | ask | answer, computed from |
|---|---|---|
| `describe_api` | `{ "name": "flagging" }` — an element, attribute, property, method, event, `--sp-*` property, slot, part or plugin | its entry in `custom-elements.json` (with its TSDoc) and the record that specifies it |
| `inspect_workbook` | `{ "path": "data/q3.xlsx" }` | sheets, size, header-row guess, titles, each column's type, blanks and values, merges, and which plugins the file would use — `@sheetpane/import` |
| `draft_rules` | `{ "path": "data/q3.xlsx", "sheet"?: "Sales" }` | a rules file for `<sheetpane-excel rules-src>`: `required`, `type`, `oneOf` per titled column — **a draft to review** |
| `check_rules` | `{ "rules": {…} or "…json…", "path"?: "data/q3.xlsx" }` | the grid's own check, each rule in words; with a workbook, the pane's own `check()` over it — the sheets and titles it lacks, and the cells that fail |
| `explain_code` | `{ "code": "SP-1002" }` | meaning, likely cause, fix and link — [docs/ERRORS.md](../../docs/ERRORS.md) |
| `find_skill` | `{ "task": "validate columns from a JSON file" }` | the skill to read, with its `SKILL.md` path |
| `diff_workbooks` | `{ "base": "spec-v1.xlsx", "path": "spec-v2.xlsx", "key"?: "Account" }` | what changed: sheets added, removed, renamed; rows added, removed, changed, moved; cells was → now — `@sheetpane/compare` |

## Registering it by hand

| tool | file | entry |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `.mcp.json` | `{ "mcpServers": { "sheetpane": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@sheetpane/mcp"] } } }` |
| Kiro | `.kiro/settings/mcp.json` | the same |
| Codex | `.codex/config.toml` (trusted projects) | `[mcp_servers.sheetpane]` · `command = "npx"` · `args = ["-y", "@sheetpane/mcp"]` |

## What it is and is not

- **Protocol:** MCP revision 2026-07-28 — stateless, `server/discover`, the version in each request's `_meta` — and 2025-11-25 / 2025-06-18 clients through `initialize`. JSON-RPC over stdio, one message per line. **Tools only.**
- **Read-only:** paths are only read; `.xlsx` and `.csv` only; 256 MB at most; no network, no writes.
- **Deterministic:** the same input gives the same output (the tests compare against golden files).
- **Errors** are tool results with `isError: true` and an SP code first — `SP-7001`…`SP-7007`, or the reader's own `SP-10xx`.

Spec: [SR-MCP](../../records/0119_MCP.md). MIT.

<!-- source: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) -->

# sheetpane — architecture

**In one sentence:** a host web page installs one npm package, `@sheetpane/grid`,
drops two custom elements anywhere it likes, and both of them read and write a single
JavaScript object — the workbook — which an export package turns back into an
`.xlsx` or `.csv` file. Nothing leaves the browser tab.

**What this document is.** The map. The *rules* are the laws in
[`records/`](../records/README.md); the *decisions* are the four verdicts in
[`work/compare/`](../work/compare/README.md); the *work* is in
[`work/OPEN-WORK.md`](../work/OPEN-WORK.md). This page restates none of them
in full — it shows how they fit and links to each. If this page and a record
disagree, the record wins and this page gets fixed.

## The picture

![sheetpane architecture — host application on top, the sheetpane package with two elements and one in-memory workbook in the middle, the export package and browser APIs below](architecture.svg)

The same picture as a flow:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph host["YOUR APPLICATION — React 19, plain index.html, anything"]
        T["a tab · a pop-up · different tabs"]
        C["your code: listens to events, saves errors, receives files"]
    end
    subgraph pkg["npm package: @sheetpane/grid"]
        X["&lt;sheetpane-excel&gt;<br/>View · Edit<br/>reader · grid · cell bar · Flag issue"]
        W[("in-memory workbook<br/>one per pane<br/>cells · changes · errors · selection · mode")]
        E["&lt;sheetpane-errors&gt;<br/>list · New error form"]
    end
    subgraph exp["npm package: @sheetpane/export"]
        P["toXlsx · patchXlsx · toCsv · download<br/>zip · crc32 · xml · csv"]
    end
    B["built into the browser: DecompressionStream · CompressionStream · DOMParser · customElements · Blob"]
    T -->|places, gives a file| X
    T -->|places| E
    X <-->|read / write| W
    E <-->|read / write| W
    X -->|Export: workbook + every change| P
    P -.->|new file, original untouched| C
    X -.->|sheetpane-* events| C
    E -.->|sheetpane-* events| C
    X --- B
    P --- B
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same picture, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
  YOUR APPLICATION  (React 19 · plain index.html · anything)
  [ a tab ] [ a pop-up ] [ different tabs ]            [ your code: events, saves, files ]
        |                   |                                   ^            ^
        | places it         | places it                 events |            | new file
        v                   v                                   |            |
  +-- npm: @sheetpane/grid ---------------------------------------------------+   |
  |  <sheetpane-excel>  <--->  ( in-memory workbook )  <--->  <sheetpane-errors> |   |
  |  View · Edit                one per pane                   list · form      |   |
  |  reader · grid              cells · changes · errors                        |   |
  |  cell bar · Flag issue      selection · mode                                |   |
  +----------|----------------------------------------------------------------+   |
             | Export: the workbook + every change held in memory                 |
             v                                                                    |
  +-- npm: @sheetpane/export ---------------------------------+                   |
  |  toXlsx · patchXlsx · toCsv · download(data, filename)    |-------------------+
  +-----------------------------------------------------------+
  built into the browser: DecompressionStream · CompressionStream · DOMParser · customElements · Blob
```

</details>

## The pieces

| piece | what it is | where it lives | decided in |
|---|---|---|---|
| **host application** | any web page; installs `@sheetpane/grid` from npm; places the elements; listens to events | the host's codebase; demos in `examples/` (W-09) | [SR-LAW-4](../records/0006_LAW-4-web-component.md), [SR-LAW-8](../records/0010_LAW-8-npm-package.md) |
| **`<sheetpane-excel>`** | the sheet: the **view** component and the **edit** component as two modes of one element; reader, virtualised grid, cell bar with the docked selection actions (Flag issue, ⋯, right-click), pins and callouts, one Download button | `packages/grid/src/excel/` (W-01) | [grid verdict](../work/compare/grid-rendering.compare.md) |
| **`@sheetpane/import`** | the reader: turns an `.xlsx` or `.csv` into the same `Workbook` object export takes in: ZIP walk + inflate + XML, or a CSV state machine; display text through a small number-format subset; usable without the UI | `packages/import/` (W-13) | [reading verdict](../work/compare/xlsx-csv-reading.compare.md), decision 5 overridden by Arpit 2026-10-18 |
| **in-memory workbook** | the one shared object — sheets and cells, cell **changes**, **errors**, selected cell, mode; a store with `subscribe` / `getSnapshot`; one instance per `pane` id | `packages/grid/src/pane/` (W-01) | [contract verdict](../work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md) |
| **check entries** | the same store and checks with no element: `check(bytes, options)` gives the errors a pane holds after load, in Node, a worker or a page | `@sheetpane/grid/check` (`packages/grid/src/check.ts`), `@sheetpane/validation/check` (W-54) | [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22f |
| **static entry** | a range of a sheet as one inert HTML `<table>` — the grid's text, look and error marks, for a report or an email — made from the same store with no element | `@sheetpane/grid/static` (`packages/grid/src/static.ts`, W-67) | [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md) decision 22g |
| **`<sheetpane-errors>`** | the **error** component: the list (filter, resolve, delete) and the New error form; always on the same workbook as the sheet | `packages/grid/src/errors/` (W-02) | [contract verdict](../work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md) |
| **`@sheetpane/export`** | a plain object or the original file plus changes → `.xlsx` or `.csv` bytes; `download()` to save it (W-12, [SR-DOWNLOAD](../records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md)); ZIP read and write, CRC-32, XML, CSV; zero dependencies; also usable without the UI | `packages/export/` (W-03, W-12) | [export verdict](../work/compare/export-shape.compare.md) |
| **plugins** | eight separate packages that register against the one workbook through six hooks (`format`, `decorate`, `derive`, `validate`, `overlay`, `exportPatch`) and add controls to six slots the grid draws; the grid with none installed is unchanged | `packages/numfmt/` `formulas/` `styles/` `validation/` `condfmt/` `images/` `charts/` `comments/` (W-15–W-22); the host in `packages/grid/src/plugins/` (W-14) | [plugins verdict](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) |
| **browser APIs** | `DecompressionStream` / `CompressionStream` (`deflate-raw`), `DOMParser`, `customElements`, `Blob` | the browser; Node 22+ uses `zlib` for export | the reading and export verdicts |

**Dependency direction:** host → plugins → `@sheetpane/grid` → `@sheetpane/import` → `@sheetpane/export` → browser.
Nothing points the other way. `@sheetpane/export` has no runtime dependencies;
`@sheetpane/grid` depends on `import` and `export`; every plugin lists
`@sheetpane/grid` as a peer at the exact version. Two plugins carry the only
third-party runtime dependencies in the project — `numfmt` (MIT) and
`@ironcalc/wasm` (MIT / Apache-2.0), both pinned. Everything is versioned in
lockstep and published together.

## The four flows

**1 · Load.** The host gives the element a file (`src` URL or base64, or the
`file` property). The reader inflates the parts it needs, parses the XML,
resolves shared strings and merges, formats typed cells once, and writes the
sheets into the workbook store. The grid draws the visible window. Anything
that is not `.xlsx` or `.csv` is refused before parsing (L3).

**2 · Edit.** In Edit mode the cell bar is a text box. A new value becomes a
`change` in the store — `sheet!ref → { was, now }` — never a write to the file.
Every element on the same `pane` re-renders from the store: the sheet shows a
corner mark and "Changed · was X"; the error list shows "matches suggestion"
if the new value equals an error's correction. A reload loses unexported
changes (L6, L9), so the sheet warns on `beforeunload` while changes are held.

**3 · Flag and review.** **Flag issue** on a cell sets `composing` on the
store. If a `<sheetpane-errors>` is connected to the pane it shows the form;
otherwise the sheet shows a small inline form. **Add error** writes a
`SheetpaneError` into the store: `found` is frozen as the uploaded value; the
sheet pins the cell; the list gains a row. Resolve, reopen and delete work from
either element. **Show in sheet** dispatches `sheetpane-reveal` so the host can
switch to the tab that holds the sheet.

**4 · Export.** The sheet asks `@sheetpane/export` for the file: for an `.xlsx`
source, `patchXlsx(originalBytes, changes)` rewrites only the changed cells and
copies every other part byte for byte — charts, styles, comments and defined
names survive; for a `.csv` source, `toCsv(activeSheet)` with BOM and the
formula guard. The result is a `Blob`, dispatched as `sheetpane-export` and
returned from `export()`; the Download button hands it to `download()` from the
same package — or, when nothing changed, the original bytes untouched. The
uploaded file is never modified.

## The public contract (working names)

Settled in the [contract verdict](../work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md); W-01's record makes it final.

| kind | names |
|---|---|
| elements | `<sheetpane-excel>`, `<sheetpane-errors>` |
| link | `pane="…"` on both — same id, same workbook; or set the `workbook` property |
| attributes | `src`, `mode` (`view` \| `edit`), `display` (`tab` \| `popup`), `open`, `author`, `readonly` |
| properties | `file`, `workbook`, `errors`, `errorTypes` |
| methods | `load()`, `export()`, `select()`, `getErrors()`, `setErrors()` |
| events | `sheetpane-load` · `-change` · `-errors` · `-select` · `-mode` · `-close` · `-export` · `-reveal` — bubbling, composed |
| styling | `--sp-*` custom properties on the element for colour, spacing, radius; **no font** — the host's font is inherited through the shadow root |

Plain HTML:

```html
<script type="module" src="/node_modules/@sheetpane/grid/dist/index.js"></script>
<sheetpane-excel pane="q3" src="/files/holdings.xlsx" mode="edit"></sheetpane-excel>
<sheetpane-errors pane="q3"></sheetpane-errors>
```

React 19 renders the same tags; React 18 sets properties through a `ref`
(no wrapper ships — ruled in [SR-LAW-4](../records/0006_LAW-4-web-component.md) Consequences).

## Where each law lands

| law | what it fixes | where you see it in the shape |
|---|---|---|
| [L2](../records/0004_LAW-2-foss-dependencies.md) FOSS dependencies | every dependency OSI-licensed; no copyleft at runtime | export, import and grid have **no** third-party runtime dependency; the licence check is B-008 |
| [L3](../records/0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md) XLSX and CSV only | no other parser, reader or writer | the reader refuses by extension and magic bytes; `.csv` dialects (`,` `;` tab) are read; `download()` refuses other extensions |
| [L4](../records/0006_LAW-4-web-component.md) always a web component | DOM-only contract; no framework peer | two custom elements; plain DOM inside; the host's framework is its own business |
| [L5](../records/0007_LAW-5-host-font.md) the host's font | no font ships; every part inherits | shadow root with inherited `font`; `font: inherit` on controls; `--sp-*` tokens carry no font |
| [L6](../records/0008_LAW-6-edits-in-memory-export-with-changes.md) edits in memory, export carries them | memory is the only store; export applies every change; original untouched | the `changes` map; `patchXlsx`; `beforeunload` warning |
| [L7](../records/0009_LAW-7-surfaces-always-in-sync.md) always in sync | one workbook, no private copies | the store registry by `pane`; both elements subscribe; selection syncs |
| [L8](../records/0010_LAW-8-npm-package.md) an npm package | one distribution; safe to import in Node | every package under `packages/`, lockstep versions; elements register only when `customElements` exists; `download()` throws cleanly without a `document` |
| [L9](../records/0011_LAW-9-memory-is-a-javascript-object.md) memory is a JavaScript object | no IndexedDB or storage, for now | the store is objects in the page; IndexedDB waits on B-025 |
| [L10](../records/0012_LAW-10-examples-maintained.md) examples maintained | every package change keeps every example working and current, in the same change | `examples/html`, `examples/react`, `examples/starters`; `just demo-check` on every push; being current is B-035 |

## Package layout

```text
pnpm-workspace.yaml       packages/*  (W-10: pnpm replaces npm workspaces)
justfile                  install · build · test · typecheck · check · release
packages/
  export/                 @sheetpane/export — zero dependencies (SR-EXPORT)
    src/
      zip.ts deflate.ts crc32.ts   read (central directory) + write; CompressionStream / zlib
      xml.ts refs.ts formula.ts    escaping, A1 helpers, shiftFormula
      xlsx.ts patch.ts validate.ts toXlsx (build), patchXlsx (rewrite changed <c> only), input rules
      csv.ts                       toCsv — RFC 4180, BOM, formula guard
      download/                    download(data, filename) — SR-DOWNLOAD
  import/                 @sheetpane/import — depends only on @sheetpane/export (SR-IMPORT)
    src/                  read.ts (detect + refuse), xlsx.ts, csv.ts, numfmt.ts (the subset), styles.ts, dom.ts
  grid/                   @sheetpane/grid — depends on @sheetpane/import and @sheetpane/export (workspace:)
    src/
      pane/               the workbook store, the pane registry, the error schema
      excel/              <sheetpane-excel>: grid (virtualiser), toolbar, cell bar, pins, callout, inline form, popup
      errors/             <sheetpane-errors>: list, filters, New error form
      tokens.css          --sp-* custom properties (no font)
      plugins/            W-14 — hooks, slots, control descriptors, the plugins attribute
      index.ts            registers both elements when customElements exists
      check.ts            @sheetpane/grid/check — check() and the store, no element, no DOM (W-54)
      static.ts           @sheetpane/grid/static — renderStatic(): a range as one HTML <table>, no DOM (W-67)
  numfmt/                 @sheetpane/numfmt — W-15; dep: numfmt 4.0.1
  formulas/               @sheetpane/formulas — W-16; dep: @ironcalc/wasm 0.9.0 (lazy-loaded)
  styles/                 @sheetpane/styles — W-17
  validation/             @sheetpane/validation — W-18
  condfmt/                @sheetpane/condfmt — W-19; peer: @sheetpane/styles
  images/                 @sheetpane/images — W-20
  charts/                 @sheetpane/charts — W-21; peer: @sheetpane/images
  comments/               @sheetpane/comments — W-22
  tables/                 @sheetpane/tables — W-61; Excel tables drawn (read by import, Table[Column] resolved by export)
  review/                 @sheetpane/review — W-59; export-only (the Review sheet, flagged-cell fills)
    (each: package.json · README.md · tsconfig.json · src/index.ts, and src/ui.ts where it adds controls;
     validation also src/plugin.ts — the plugin, unregistered — and src/check.ts, its /check entry)
examples/                 W-09 — html/ (one index.html) and react/ (Vite + React 19)
```

## Build order

```text
W-10 pnpm + just ✓ ──► W-04 build · test · CI ✓ ──► W-03 export ✓ ──► W-13 import ✓ ──► W-01 excel + workbook ──► W-02 errors ──► W-09 demos
                                                     W-12 download ✓ (inside export's package)
```

Then the plugins, in this order (each waits on the plugin host and the reader):

```text
W-14 plugin host ──► W-15 numfmt ──► W-16 formulas ──► W-23 undo ──► W-17 styles ──► W-18 validation ──► W-19 condfmt ──► W-20 images ──► W-21 charts ──► W-22 comments
W-24 freeze panes runs beside W-01 (core, not a plugin)
```

Every research question that gated this order was ruled on 2026-10-18; the
five verdicts and their reopen-triggers are in [`work/compare/`](../work/compare/README.md).
How it is all tested — Vitest, real browsers, fixtures, goldens — is the
[testing verdict](../work/compare/testing.compare.md).

## Still open, on purpose

- **IndexedDB** (B-025) — the decider's deferred request; needs L6 and L9 rewritten.
- **Largest workbook the tab can hold** (B-026) — unmeasured until W-01 lands.
- **The mechanical check still owed:** B-008 (licences over the whole tree). The
  font, framework-peer, publishable, refusal, round-trip and sync checks run
  today ([SR-BUILD](../records/0102_BUILD.md), [SR-GRID](../records/0105_GRID.md)).
- **The workbook never leaves the browser** ([SR-LAW-11](../records/0013_LAW-11-workbook-stays-in-the-browser.md)): the only network calls are the `src` and `rules-src` reads, pinned by `test/packages.test.ts`.
