<!-- source: records/0008_LAW-6-edits-in-memory-export-with-changes.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0008_LAW-6-edits-in-memory-export-with-changes.md) -->

# SR-LAW-6 — L6, every change is held in memory and export carries it

## §1 — For humans

**Nothing is lost while the workbook is open.** From the moment a file is
loaded, every change the user makes is kept in memory.

**Export means "with my changes".** Exporting produces the workbook as it is
now — the original plus every change, none dropped.

**The original file is never touched.** Export always writes a new file.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U["file loaded"] --> M["workbook in memory"]
    E["every change"] --> M
    M --> X["export: original + every change"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   file loaded ---> workbook in memory ---> export: original + every change
                          ^
   every change ----------'
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

An editor that loses a change, or exports the file as it was loaded, is
worse than a viewer. The decider ruled on 2026-10-18 that once a workbook is
loaded, every change is kept in memory and an export carries every change.

### Decision

1. **Every change is held in memory** from load until the workbook is closed
   or replaced — every cell edit and every other change sheetpane allows.
2. **Memory is the store.** sheetpane writes the changes nowhere else — no
   server, no browser storage. What "memory" means is
   [SR-LAW-9](0011_LAW-9-memory-is-a-javascript-object.md)'s.
3. **Export carries every change.** An export is the loaded workbook with
   every change held in memory applied — none dropped, none reordered.
4. **The original file is never modified.** Export produces a new file.
5. **Export formats are L3's** — XLSX or CSV ([SR-LAW-3](0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md)).

### Consequences

- **Reload (ruled 2026-10-18, "resolve all the blockers"):** a page reload or a
  closed tab loses unexported changes, and that stays so until
  [SR-LAW-9](0011_LAW-9-memory-is-a-javascript-object.md) is rewritten for
  IndexedDB (backlog B-025). sheetpane warns on `beforeunload` when changes are
  held.
- **Fidelity (ruled 2026-10-18):** export keeps everything the workbook held
  that sheetpane does not show or edit. For an `.xlsx` source the export
  **patches the original bytes** — only changed cells are rewritten; charts,
  pivot tables, comments, defined names, styles and other parts are copied as
  they were. For a `.csv` source there is nothing beyond the cells to keep.
  Detail: [`work/compare/export-shape.compare.md`](../work/compare/export-shape.compare.md).
- Exporting a multi-sheet workbook to CSV, which holds one sheet, is a
  component decision, owed by the record that owns export.
- **Checked today:** an edited workbook exported and loaded again carries
  every change (SR-GRID round-trip property); the upload's bytes are compared
  unchanged after export. The veto command's `fetch(` hits are the reads
  [SR-LAW-11](0013_LAW-11-workbook-stays-in-the-browser.md) decision 4 allows; that law's test pins them.

### Alternatives considered

- Save changes to browser storage or a server — rejected by the ruling: the
  changes are kept in memory.
- Write changes back into the loaded file — rejected: the original is the
  user's and stays as it was.

### Reference (required)

- The decider's ruling, 2026-10-18 session — `work/WORKLOG.md`, the entry of
  that date titled "laws L6 and L7 filed".

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** an export of an edited workbook, loaded again,
differs from the in-memory workbook in any changed cell — or sheetpane writes
workbook data to storage or the network.

**How to check it:** `grep -rnE "localStorage|sessionStorage|indexedDB|fetch\(|XMLHttpRequest|sendBeacon" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=archive --exclude-dir=records --exclude-dir=work --exclude-dir=docs . || echo clean` (its hits are the reads SR-LAW-11 decision 4 allows) — plus the round-trip test: `just test-pkg grid -t 'round-trips'`.

---

## References

*Every source this record cites, gathered in one place. An archived document
is never listed here.*

**Records** — [SR-LAWS](0001_LAWS.md) · [SR-LAW-0](0002_LAW-0-authority.md) · [SR-LAW-3](0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md) · [SR-LAW-7](0009_LAW-7-surfaces-always-in-sync.md) · [SR-LAW-9](0011_LAW-9-memory-is-a-javascript-object.md) · [SR-LAW-11](0013_LAW-11-workbook-stays-in-the-browser.md)

**Project docs**

- [SR-GRID](0105_GRID.md) · [SR-IMPORT](0104_IMPORT.md) · [SR-ERRORS](0106_ERRORS.md) — the checks
- [`work/WORKLOG.md`](../work/WORKLOG.md)

<!-- source: records/0009_LAW-7-surfaces-always-in-sync.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0009_LAW-7-surfaces-always-in-sync.md) -->

# SR-LAW-7 — L7, the view, edit and error components are always in sync

## §1 — For humans

**Three components, one truth.** The view, the editor and the error component
always show the same workbook.

**A change anywhere shows everywhere, at once.** Edit a cell and the view and
error component show the new value immediately. Flag an error and the view and
editor show it immediately. No refresh, no save, no button.

**No private copies.** All three read the one in-memory workbook of
[L6](0008_LAW-6-edits-in-memory-export-with-changes.md), so they cannot drift.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M["the one in-memory workbook (L6)"]
    V["view"] <--> M
    E["edit"] <--> M
    R["error component"] <--> M
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
                 .--> view
   the one in-memory workbook (L6) <--+--> edit
                 '--> error component
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

Separate components with separate copies of the data drift: an edit that
the error list never sees, an error the grid never marks. The decider ruled on
2026-10-18 that the view, edit and error components are always in sync.

### Decision

1. **The three components** are the view, the edit, and the error component
   (the review surface that marks incorrect data and its correction).
2. **One source.** All three read and write the one in-memory workbook of L6.
   No component keeps a private copy of workbook data or of its errors.
3. **Always in sync.** A change made through any component appears in the
   other two at once, with no user action.
4. **Errors are part of what is synced.** An error, and its correction, shows
   in the view and the editor as well as the error component.
5. **A component added later joins the same rule** — it reads the one
   workbook and stays in sync.

### Consequences

- **Selection (ruled 2026-10-18, "resolve all the blockers"):** the selected
  sheet and cell are part of the shared state and sync; picking an error in the
  error component selects its cell and the grid scrolls it into view. Scroll
  position itself, zoom and find text stay local to each element.
- **Matching edits (ruled 2026-10-18):** an edit that equals an error's
  suggested correction does **not** resolve the error; it marks it
  "matches suggestion". Resolving stays a human act, so a review can be
  audited. The error component shows the new value either way (decision 3).
  Detail: [`work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md`](../work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md).
- **Checked today:** the sync test mounts both elements on one pane, in two
  containers, one inside a `<dialog>`, in both orders, and checks a change, an
  error, a resolve and a selection in each (SR-ERRORS Consequences).

### Alternatives considered

- Each component holds its own copy and syncs by messages — rejected: copies
  drift, and "always" cannot be proved.
- Sync on save or on a refresh — rejected by the ruling: always in sync.

### Reference (required)

- The decider's ruling, 2026-10-18 session — `work/WORKLOG.md`, the entry of
  that date titled "laws L6 and L7 filed".

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a change made through one component is absent
from another after the change completes, or any component holds its own copy
of workbook data.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg grid -t 'always in sync'`

---

is never listed here.*

**Project docs**

- [SR-GRID](0105_GRID.md) · [SR-IMPORT](0104_IMPORT.md) · [SR-ERRORS](0106_ERRORS.md) — the checks

# SR-LAW-8 — L8, sheetpane is consumed as an npm package

## §1 — For humans

**sheetpane is an npm package.** A host application gets it the way it gets
any other JavaScript library: install it from the npm registry, import it.

**Any npm-compatible client works** — npm, yarn, pnpm, bun.

**One distribution.** What is published to npm is sheetpane. Nothing else is
a separate, second way of getting it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S["sheetpane source"] -->|publish| N["npm registry"]
    N -->|npm / yarn / pnpm install| H["host application"]
    H -->|import| E["the sheetpane web component (L4)"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   sheetpane source --publish--> npm registry --install--> host application --import--> web component (L4)
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

sheetpane is a library other applications build on. The decider ruled on
2026-10-18 that it is consumed as an npm (Node) package.

### Decision

1. **sheetpane is distributed as an npm package**, published to the npm
   registry.
2. **Consumers install it with npm or any npm-compatible client** and import
   it as a module.
3. **The published package is the one distribution.** A CDN that serves files
   straight from the npm package (jsDelivr, unpkg) is the same package, not a
   second distribution.
4. **What the package exports is L4's web component**
   ([SR-LAW-4](0006_LAW-4-web-component.md)); its dependencies obey L2
   ([SR-LAW-2](0004_LAW-2-foss-dependencies.md)).

### Consequences

- The package name, module format (ESM, CommonJS), TypeScript types and
  `exports` map are component decisions, owed by the record that owns
  `package.json`.
- **Server-side import (ruled 2026-10-18, "resolve all the blockers"):**
  importing either package in Node without a browser must be safe.
  `@sheetpane/grid` registers its elements only when `customElements` exists;
  `@sheetpane/export` touches the DOM only inside `download()` (which throws a
  clear error without a `document`) and otherwise runs in Node 22+.
- **Publishing (ruled 2026-10-18):** the two packages are versioned in
  lockstep — one version number, released together — so `@sheetpane/grid@x.y.z`
  always pins `@sheetpane/export@x.y.z`. The root `package.json` is the
  private monorepo root (W-04); the packages meant for npm are under
  `packages/`, and the veto command below reads those. Checked by SR-BUILD
  decisions 7 and 10 (publishable, lockstep, packed manifests).

### Alternatives considered

- A downloadable script bundle as a separate distribution — rejected by the
  ruling: npm is the channel.

### Reference (required)

- The decider's ruling, 2026-10-18 session — `work/WORKLOG.md`, the entry of
  that date titled "laws L8 and L9 filed".
- npm, about packages and modules — https://docs.npmjs.com/about-packages-and-modules

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a publishable package's `package.json` is missing
at release, is marked `"private": true`, or the package cannot be installed
from the npm registry.

**How to check it:** `for p in packages/*/; do node -e "const p=require('./$p/package.json');console.log(p.private?'VIOLATION private '+p.name:'publishable '+p.name)"; done`

<!-- source: records/0011_LAW-9-memory-is-a-javascript-object.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0011_LAW-9-memory-is-a-javascript-object.md) -->

# SR-LAW-9 — L9, memory means a JavaScript object, for now

## §1 — For humans

**"Memory" means a JavaScript object.** When a record — L6 first — says the
workbook and its changes are held in memory, they live in JavaScript objects
in the page.

**Nothing else counts as memory.** Not IndexedDB, not localStorage, not a
file, not a server.

**"For now" is the point.** IndexedDB is the named next step (backlog B-025).
It arrives only by the decider rewriting this record.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M["memory"] --> J["JavaScript objects in the page"]
    M -. not now .-> I["IndexedDB · localStorage · server"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   memory ---> JavaScript objects in the page
          ...> (not now) IndexedDB, localStorage, server
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

L6 says every change is held in memory. "Memory" could mean a JavaScript
object, IndexedDB or a server. The decider ruled on 2026-10-18 that, for now,
memory means a JavaScript object.

### Decision

1. **Memory is JavaScript objects** held in the page's JavaScript heap. Every
   record that says "memory" means this.
2. **Not memory:** IndexedDB, localStorage, sessionStorage, the Cache API, the
   file system, a server.
3. **"For now" is entrenched like any law.** Adding a store — IndexedDB first —
   is a ruling by the decider that rewrites decisions 1 and 2.

### Consequences

- Memory lives and dies with the page: a reload loses unexported changes —
  ruled to stay so in [SR-LAW-6](0008_LAW-6-edits-in-memory-export-with-changes.md)
  Consequences until this record is rewritten for IndexedDB (B-025).
- Connecting to IndexedDB is backlog B-025 (`unruled`) — the decider's own
  request, deferred, not dismissed.
- A workbook is bounded by the tab's memory. The largest workbook sheetpane
  can hold is not measured — backlog B-026 (`unmeasured`).
- **Enforced by:** L6's veto command, which already refuses storage and
  network calls.

### Alternatives considered

- IndexedDB from day one — deferred by the ruling: B-025.

### Reference (required)

- The decider's ruling, 2026-10-18 session — `work/WORKLOG.md`, the entry of
  that date titled "laws L8 and L9 filed".
- [SR-LAW-6](0008_LAW-6-edits-in-memory-export-with-changes.md) — the law
  this one defines a word for.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** workbook data is written anywhere other than
JavaScript objects in the page.

**How to check it:** `grep -rnE "indexedDB|localStorage|sessionStorage|caches\.|showSaveFilePicker" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=archive --exclude-dir=records --exclude-dir=work --exclude-dir=docs . || echo clean`

---

is never listed here.*

**Project docs**

- [`work/BACKLOG.md`](../work/BACKLOG.md) — B-025, B-026
- [`work/WORKLOG.md`](../work/WORKLOG.md)

<!-- source: records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0101_DOWNLOAD.md) -->

# SR-DOWNLOAD — download(): export output in, a saved .xlsx or .csv out

## §1 — For humans

**One call saves an export.** `@sheetpane/export` makes the file's contents
(`toXlsx` gives bytes, `toCsv` gives text). `download()` hands them to the
browser as a real file in the Downloads folder. That replaces the Blob, link
and click code every host would otherwise write, and usually get slightly
wrong.

**It is strict on purpose.** It saves only `.xlsx` and `.csv` (L3). It fixes
file names that Windows or macOS would reject. It never changes the bytes it is
given (L6). It throws a clear error instead of failing silently.

**It lives in `@sheetpane/export`**, beside the writers whose output it
saves; `@sheetpane/grid`'s Export button calls the same function.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    D["data: bytes · Blob · text"] --> F["download(data, filename)"]
    N["filename"] --> F
    F --> C{"name and type OK?"}
    C -- no --> E["throws an Error naming the file"]
    C -- yes --> B["Blob → temporary link → click"]
    B --> S["browser saves the file"]
    B --> R["link removed; URL released a moment later"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   data (bytes|Blob|text) --+
                            +--> download(data, filename) --> name & type OK?
   filename ----------------+                                  |no    |yes
                                                               v      v
                                                  throws Error   Blob -> temp link -> click
                                                                        |-> browser saves the file
                                                                        |-> link removed; URL released later
```

</details>

### Examples

**1 · Excel file**
```ts
import { toXlsx, download } from '@sheetpane/export';
download(await toXlsx(book), 'sales.xlsx');
// saves sales.xlsx, type application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet
```

**2 · CSV text**
```ts
download(toCsv(sheet, { bom: true }).text, 'sales.csv');
// saves sales.csv, type text/csv;charset=utf-8; the BOM is kept so Excel shows "José" correctly
```

**3 · A Blob you already have**
```ts
download(new Blob([bytes]), 'report.xlsx');
```

**4 · Missing extension gets added**
```ts
download(await toXlsx(book), 'Q3 report');   // → Q3 report.xlsx  (bytes)
download(toCsv(sheet).text, 'Q3 report');         // → Q3 report.csv   (text)
```

**5 · Unsafe file names get cleaned**
```ts
download(bytes, 'FY26: North/South?.xlsx');  // → FY26_ North_South_.xlsx
```

**6 · Overriding the file type**
```ts
download(text, 'data.csv', { type: 'text/csv;charset=utf-8;header=present' });
```

**7 · Errors are explicit, never silent**
```ts
download(bytes, 'sales.pdf');
// ✗ Error: "sales.pdf" — sheetpane saves .xlsx or .csv only

download(new Blob([bytes]), 'mystery');
// ✗ Error: "mystery" — add .xlsx or .csv; the type can't be told from this Blob

download('a,b\n1,2', 'sales.xlsx');
// ✗ Error: "sales.xlsx" — text can't be saved as .xlsx; use .csv

download(bytes, 'sales.xlsx');   // in Node or a web worker
// ✗ Error: download() needs a browser page (no document); write the bytes yourself
```

**8 · Inside a button click, after the async export**
```ts
button.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  const bytes = await toXlsx(book);
  download(bytes, 'sales.xlsx');
});
```

**9 · With the grid's Export button**: no code needed.
```html
<sheetpane-excel src="sales.xlsx"></sheetpane-excel>
<!-- Export → object built from memory, edits included → toXlsx → download -->
```

**10 · Inside an iframe**: the host must allow downloads.
```html
<iframe src="app.html" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-downloads"></iframe>
```

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

Arpit asked on 2026-10-18 for a downloader (W-12). `toXlsx` and `toCsv` return
data, not files. Saving them in a browser takes a Blob, an object URL, a
temporary `<a download>` and a correctly timed release of the URL. Each host
writing that itself would duplicate it and get the timing wrong.

### Decision

1. **One function:** `download(data: Uint8Array | Blob | string, filename: string, options?: { type?: string }): void`.
   It is synchronous and returns nothing. It has exactly one implementation,
   in **`@sheetpane/export`** (ruled 2026-10-18 — the package a host uses to
   make a file is the package that saves it; `@sheetpane/grid` imports it for
   its Export button); no other package re-implements it.
2. **Input.** `Uint8Array` and `Blob` are saved as given. A `string` is encoded
   as UTF-8, and a leading BOM (U+FEFF) is kept. **The bytes are never
   altered** (L6).
3. **File type.** The MIME type comes from the extension:

   | extension | MIME type |
   |---|---|
   | `.xlsx` | `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet` |
   | `.csv` | `text/csv;charset=utf-8` |

   `options.type` overrides it.
4. **Extensions (L3).** The extension is matched case-insensitively.
   - **What counts as an extension:** the letters and digits after the
     last `.` of the cleaned name (`/\.([A-Za-z0-9]+)$/`); a name like
     `Q3 report` has none.
   - **Other extensions:** anything except `.xlsx` or `.csv` throws.
   - **No extension:** one is added. `Uint8Array` → `.xlsx`, `string` → `.csv`.
     For a `Blob`, its `type` decides when it is one of the two MIME types
     above; otherwise the call throws.
   - **Text as `.xlsx`:** a `string` saved as `.xlsx` throws.
5. **File names.** Each of `\ / : * ? " < > |` is replaced with `_`. Control
   characters (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F) are removed. Leading and trailing spaces
   and trailing dots are trimmed. The name is capped at 200 characters with
   the extension kept. A name left empty by cleaning throws.
6. **Mechanism.** Blob → `URL.createObjectURL` → a hidden `<a download>`
   appended to `document.body`, clicked, and removed at once. The URL is
   revoked on a later task after **30 seconds** (`REVOKE_DELAY_MS`), never in
   the same task as the click. **Measured 2026-10-18** (W-12,
   `download.browser.test.ts`, a 64 MB file): Chromium 156 and WebKit (Safari
   27.2, macOS) save the whole file even when the URL is revoked in the
   click's own task; so does Firefox 157 (Linux, nightly run 39124283729) —
   it could not be launched on the measuring Mac (`work/MACHINE.md`). The
   30-second margin stays until iOS Safari is measured — it costs only the
   Blob's memory for that long.
7. **No page, no download.** Where `document` is undefined (Node, a worker),
   the call throws an `Error` saying a browser page is needed. Never a silent
   no-op.
8. **Errors.** Every throw is an `Error` (a `TypeError` for a wrong argument
   type). The message names the filename as given and the rule it broke.
9. **No runtime dependency** (L2; the zero-dependency default).
10. **Out of scope:**
    - Whether the host can intercept or cancel the Export button's download
      (W-07's events).
    - The iframe `sandbox` attribute (the host's).
    - Any save location or save dialog (decision 6 uses the browser's default).

### Consequences

- **Codes (W-40, SR-CODES):** `download()` refuses with SP-2101 to SP-2107, each error carrying `spCode`.
- **Built and tested:** `packages/export/src/download/index.ts`; Node tests
  for decisions 4, 5, 7, 8 (`download.test.ts`) and real downloads caught by
  Playwright for examples 1–5, 7 and 8 (`download.browser.test.ts`) — Chromium
  on every push, WebKit and Firefox nightly (all three green, run 39124283729).
- **iOS Safari: not tested.** No iOS device or simulator is reachable from the
  build machine; the decider will test it on a phone later (backlog B-031). Desktop WebKit
  passes every example.
- **Hosts in sandboxed iframes** must add `allow-downloads`. The README says so.
- **Easier:** a host saves an export in one line. The grid's Export button
  uses the same call.

### Alternatives considered

- **File System Access API (`showSaveFilePicker`).** Rejected as the default:
  Chromium only, and it adds a dialog. It may come back as an opt-in later.
- **FileSaver.js.** Rejected: a runtime dependency against the
  zero-dependency default, for about 15 lines of code.
- **`data:` URLs.** Rejected: size limits, and the whole file is held twice as
  a string.
- **`window.open`.** Rejected: popup blockers, and it opens a tab instead of
  saving.
- **Leave it to each host.** Rejected: every host repeats the code and the
  revoke timing.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/export/src/download/index.ts`](../packages/export/src/download/index.ts):
  the code this record specifies; `download.test.ts` and
  `download.browser.test.ts` beside it prove decisions 2–8.
- [`work/reference/specs/web/mdn-url-createobjecturl.md`](../work/reference/specs/web/mdn-url-createobjecturl.md)
  · [`mdn-blob.md`](../work/reference/specs/web/mdn-blob.md) — the mechanism
  in decision 6.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:**
- more than one source file under `packages/` creates an object URL for a
  download, or
- `download` accepts an extension other than `.xlsx` or `.csv`.

**How to check it:** `grep -rlE 'createObjectURL' packages/*/src | grep -v 'packages/images/src/media.ts' | wc -l` prints `1` (the pictures' display URLs are not downloads — SR-IMAGES); and `just test-export -t 'file names'` passes.

<!-- source: records/0102_BUILD.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0102_BUILD.md) -->

# SR-BUILD — the monorepo build

## §1 — For humans

**One command per job, from a clean clone.** `just install`, `just typecheck`,
`just test`, `just build`, `just check` (all three). The `justfile` only wraps
the pnpm scripts, so nothing *needs* just.

**Every package is published at the same version.** `just release 1.2.3`
bumps every package under `packages/`, runs the checks and pushes a tag; CI
publishes them together from that tag. A plugin always pins the exact grid it was tested with.

**Tests run where the code runs.** `@sheetpane/export` in Node; every package
that touches the DOM in a real browser (Chromium on every push, Firefox and
WebKit nightly). No simulated DOM.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C["clean clone"] --> I["pnpm install --frozen-lockfile"]
    I --> B["build: tsc → dist/ + .d.ts; grid style.css"]
    B --> T["typecheck: tsc per package, strict"]
    T --> V["test: Vitest — Node + Chromium, coverage"]
    V --> P["pack-check: tarballs as npm sees them"]
    P --> R["release: one version, tag; CI publishes"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   clean clone -> pnpm install --frozen-lockfile -> build (tsc -> dist/, style.css)
     -> typecheck (tsc, strict) -> test (Vitest: Node + Chromium, coverage)
     -> pack-check (tarballs as npm sees them) -> release (one version, tag; CI publishes)
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-04 asked for a repo that builds, tests and type-checks every package from a
clean clone, locally and in CI, before feature code lands. W-10 moved it to
pnpm and a justfile; the testing verdict chose the runner.

### Decision

1. **Package manager:** pnpm, pinned by `packageManager` in the root
   `package.json`; the workspace is `packages/*` (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`).
   Internal dependencies and peers use `workspace:*`; `pnpm publish` rewrites
   them to the exact version.
2. **Commands:** the root `package.json` scripts are the real commands
   (`build`, `test`, `typecheck`); the `justfile` wraps them and adds
   `check`, `test-pkg`, `test-export`, `test-grid`, `test-browsers`,
   `pack-check`, `release`, `clean`.
3. **Build:** plain `tsc` per package (`tsconfig.build.json`, `src/` →
   `dist/`, ESM with `.d.ts` and maps). No bundler: consumers bundle; the
   output is native ESM with `.js` import specifiers, so it also loads from
   plain HTML (SR-LAW-4). `@sheetpane/grid` also writes `dist/style.css` from
   its token module.
4. **Type-check:** `tsc --noEmit` per package over `src/` and `test/`, and
   at the root over `test/` and `vitest.config.ts`; `tsconfig.base.json` is
   strict, with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`.
   The examples are the exception to decision 5: they type-check against the
   built `dist/`, as a host app does, so `just check` builds first (a clean
   clone failed every CI run while it type-checked first).
5. **Source condition:** every `exports` entry carries a `source` condition
   pointing at `src/`, so type-check and tests read sibling packages without a
   build. `publishConfig.exports` drops it from the published manifest. The
   grid's framework typings (W-37) are generated `.d.ts` files
   committed in `src/frameworks/`: `source` points at the `.d.ts`, the build
   copies them into `dist/frameworks/` with an empty `.js` for `import`.
5a. **Entries** (each with its `source` condition, decision 5):

    | entry | what | DOM |
    |---|---|---|
    | `@sheetpane/grid` | the elements, registered on import, and the API | a page (imports anywhere) |
    | `@sheetpane/grid/check` | the pane's checks with no page — `check()`, `loadWorkbook()`, the store, the rules checker (W-54, SR-GRID 22f) | none |
    | `@sheetpane/grid/static` | a range as one static HTML `<table>` — `renderStatic()`, `loadWorkbook()` (W-67, SR-GRID 22g) | none |
    | `@sheetpane/grid/jsx` · `/vue` · `/svelte` · `/solid` | framework typings (W-37) | types only |
    | `@sheetpane/grid/style.css` · `/rules.schema.json` · `/llms.txt` · `/custom-elements.json` · `/vscode.*-custom-data.json` · `/web-types.json` | data | — |
    | `@sheetpane/<plugin>` | the plugin, registered on import | none |
    | `@sheetpane/<plugin>/ui` | its controls (numfmt, formulas, styles, validation, condfmt, charts, visibility) | a page |
    | `@sheetpane/validation/check` | the plugin unregistered (checking only, no export switch), and `check()` with it on (W-54, SR-VALIDATION 11) | none |
    | `@sheetpane/fixtures/files/*` | the fixture files | — |

    A `/check` or `/static` entry's import graph holds no element module and names no
    `customElements`, `document` or `window` (`test/check-entries.test.ts`).
6. **Tests:** Vitest, one root config. Project `repo` and `export` run in
   Node; every other package runs in browser mode on Playwright, and so do
   `@sheetpane/export`'s `*.browser.test.ts` files (project `export-browser`,
   the engine-determinism proof), and so do the React hook recipes'
   tests under `examples/react/test` (project `react-recipes`, against the
   demo's own React). `SP_BROWSERS` selects the engines.
   Browser tests run at a 1280 × 800 viewport. Node projects carry the
   `source` condition in `ssr.resolve` as well, so
   they never read a stale `dist/`. `.xlsx` and `.csv` fixtures load as assets
   (`?inline`). `coverage/` and `.vitest/` are ignored output. Two browser
   commands (`test/commands.ts`), `armDownload` and `takeDownload`, let a test
   catch a real download through Playwright. Dev-only readers
   for read-back tests (ExcelJS, PapaParse, fflate) are dev dependencies of
   the package that uses them; so is any `@sheetpane/*` package a test
   imports (`workspace:*`). Coverage (v8) is reported on every `just test`;
   90 % lines on `packages/export/src/**` fails the run — in CI, the
   `coverage` job runs `@sheetpane/export`'s tests with coverage and holds that
   line, while the sharded test jobs collect none. CI shards (`--shard=k/n`)
   are balanced by measured time, not Vitest's path hash: `vitest.config.ts`'s
   sequencer puts the longest file first, each into the lightest shard, from
   `test/durations.json` (`just test-durations` re-measures it; an unlisted
   file counts 1 s). A wall-clock budget (a frame gap,
   pixels scrolled in 5 s) is asserted on a developer machine and only
   reported on a shared CI runner: `vitest.config.ts` provides
   `timingBudgets` (off when `CI` is set), the grid's test helpers export it
   as `budgets`, and the test logs its numbers either way. Every structural
   assertion in the same test still holds everywhere.
7. **Package checks** (`test/packages.test.ts`): each package is public,
   `@sheetpane/<dir>`, MIT, ESM with types; one version across all (lockstep);
   `workspace:*` for `@sheetpane/*`; no UI framework as a dependency or peer;
   no third-party runtime dependency except `numfmt` and `@ironcalc/wasm`,
   each pinned exactly; no font file, `@font-face`, web-font URL or named
   `font-family` in any package source; no network call in any package's
   shipped code but the three reads [SR-LAW-11](0013_LAW-11-workbook-stays-in-the-browser.md) decision 4 allows. Each package ships `dist` only —
   except `@sheetpane/fixtures`, which ships `files/` too, so that `url()`
   reaches them from `src/` and `dist/` alike (W-42), and `@sheetpane/skills`,
   which ships `skills/`, `entry/` and `bin/`, has no build and is a
   dependency of every other package (W-35, SR-SKILLS). A plugin that writes
   into the package at export depends on `@sheetpane/export` (`workspace:*`):
   `@sheetpane/visibility` (W-49) and `@sheetpane/validation` (W-58) — and
   `@sheetpane/grid`, which ships `custom-elements.json` beside `dist` (W-37).
   **`create-sheetpane`** (W-43, SR-CREATE) is the one unscoped package — `npm
   create sheetpane` resolves that name — with `files: ['bin', 'templates']`,
   a bin, no dependencies and no build; the font scan walks its `bin/` and
   `templates/`.
   Grid's build is `tsc` → `build-grid-css.mjs` → `build-manifest.mjs` (the
   manifest, the editor data, the framework typings; no dependency); grid has
   `@types/react` as a dev dependency so the React augmentation type-checks in
   the workspace. `test/types/` type-checks a usage per framework — React
   against the real `@types/react`, Vue, Svelte and Solid against stubs (none
   is installed in the repo); the root `tsconfig.json` excludes it.
7a. **TSDoc (W-36):** every symbol reachable from a package's `exports`
    carries TSDoc that survives into the built `.d.ts` (`removeComments`
    stays off): a summary; for a function `@param` per top-level parameter
    and `@returns` unless it returns `void`; a custom element class lists its
    Attributes, a `@fires` per event it dispatches, an `@example` and a `@see`
    to its record. `test/tsdoc.test.ts` reads the built declaration files —
    TypeScript 7 has no stable JavaScript compiler API, so `test/tsdoc-walk.ts`
    follows `export … from`, `export *`, aliases, re-exported imports and
    `@sheetpane/<pkg>` re-exports itself — and fails naming each symbol; it
    also type-checks every `@example` code block against the built packages.
8. **CI:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every push to any branch, every
   PR and on demand, every job in parallel and set up by
   `.github/actions/setup` (Node; the pinned pnpm, installed with npm; the
   pnpm store cached by the lockfile; Playwright's Chromium cached by its
   version, without apt dependencies — the Ubuntu image carries them). Jobs:
   `lint` (version parity, build, typecheck — the repo's lint); `test` (the
   whole suite, Node + Chromium, in four balanced shards, decision 6);
   `coverage`; `package` (`pack-check` and `demo-check` in Chromium);
   `portable` (ubuntu, macos and windows × Node 22 and the current LTS:
   version parity, build, typecheck, the Node unit tests, and
   `scripts/smoke-built.mjs`, which installs every package from its packed
   tarball with npm into an empty folder and imports it from plain Node (and
   runs each `/check` entry on a CSV, W-54, and renders one with
   `/static`, W-67), so
   the BUILT package is what is tested); and `create` — a matrix over the six
   `create-sheetpane` templates running `scripts/create-check.mjs`
   (SR-CREATE decision 5). A branch's newer push cancels its older run; on
   `main` every run finishes, since `publish.yml` reads each commit's verdict.
   The target is about two minutes of wall time. Every package's `engines.node` is `>=22` (the
   decider, 2026-10-19; Node 20 is past end of life). Build scripts resolve
   paths with `fileURLToPath`, never `URL.pathname`, so they run on Windows;
   `nightly.yml` runs the browser suites in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit;
   `pages.yml` (W-44) on a release tag builds the live playground — `just
   site` → `site/` (`scripts/build-site.mjs`: the HTML gallery at `/` with
   every file its import map names copied in, the React gallery at `/react/`
   with a relative base, the version in both headers, no third-party script)
   — checks it with `demo-check`, and deploys it to GitHub Pages;
   `publish.yml` publishes the packages when a GitHub Release is published
   (decision 9).
8b. **Starters and links (W-44):** `scripts/build-starters.mjs` (`just
    starters`) scaffolds every `create-sheetpane` template with the CLI itself
    into `examples/starters/<template>` (not workspace members) with an index
    of **Open in StackBlitz** links pinned like `llms.txt` (`v<version>`, `main`
    before the first release); `release.mjs` reruns it; `test/starters.test.ts`
    fails when they are stale and checks each has `dev` and `build`. StackBlitz
    installs from npm, so a starter runs once its version is published — the
    test checks the folders, not StackBlitz. The root README, the grid and
    `create-sheetpane` READMEs, `llms.txt` and the setup skill link the live
    playground (`https://arpitarya.github.io/sheetpane/`, decision 8) and the
    starters.
9. **Release** (`RELEASING.md` is the walkthrough): `just release <version>`
   — clean tree required; every package set to the version
   (`scripts/release.mjs`, which then rebuilds the starters, the Claude Code
   plugin and `llms.txt`); version parity; `just check pack-check`; a commit
   pushed to `main` as `chore(release): v<version>` (commits follow
   Conventional Commits, the decider, 2026-10-19), no tag; it refuses unless
   `CHANGELOG.md` has a `## <version>` section. After `ci.yml` is green on
   that commit, `just publish <version>` publishes the GitHub Release
   `v<version> — <summary>` (the heading's summary) with that section as its
   notes (`scripts/release-notes.mjs`),
   and that alone runs
   `.github/workflows/publish.yml`. Its `build` job refuses unless `ci.yml`
   concluded `success` on the commit on `main`, checks version parity and that
   the tag is the packages' version, builds once and packs every public
   package (`pnpm pack` rewrites `workspace:*`) into one artifact. Its
   `publish-npm` job (environment `npm`) never rebuilds: it checks each
   tarball (README, LICENSE and the build output present; no `src/`, `test/`
   or `workspace:`) and publishes it with npm ≥ 11.5.1, `--provenance`, the
   `next` dist-tag for a version with a `-` and `latest` otherwise; a version
   already on npm is skipped, so a failed run is re-run. **No token** — npm
   trusted publishing (OIDC; the decider's ruling, 2026-10-19: no
   `NPM_TOKEN`). Trusted publishing needs the package to exist: the first
   version is published once by hand, then each package trusts `publish.yml`
   and environment `npm` (npmjs.com, or `scripts/npm-trust.sh`). Neither name
   may change: npmjs.com is bound to both. Never `npm publish` from a package
   folder: npm ships `workspace:*` literally.
9a. **llms.txt (W-38):** `scripts/build-llms.mjs` (`just llms`, no
    dependencies, deterministic) writes `llms.txt` (llmstxt.org: an H1, a
    summary, sections Start · Elements · Plugins · Rules and errors · Testing
    and tooling · Skills · Records of absolute links) and `llms-full.txt` (the
    package READMEs, the docs, the laws and the component records inlined,
    each under its source path — never `work/` or `archive/`) at the repo
    root; the grid build copies both into `dist/` (`@sheetpane/grid/llms.txt`).
    Links are GitHub URLs pinned to `v<version>` (`main` before the first
    release); `release.mjs` rewrites them with the version, and
    `test/llms.test.ts` fails when either is stale (it prints the full file's
    size — over 200 KB is a hint to split per package).
9b. **Version parity:** `scripts/check-version-parity.mjs` (`just
    version-parity`; Node standard library only) fails when any file holding
    the version disagrees: every `packages/*/package.json`, the plugin's
    `plugin.json`, each starter's `@sheetpane/*` pins and `tree/v…` links, and
    `blob/v…` in `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`. It runs in `ci.yml` (every
    job) and in `publish.yml`.
10. **Pack check:** `scripts/pack-check.mjs` packs each package as publish
    would and fails on a surviving `workspace:` or `source` entry or a missing
    exported file (for a subpath pattern such as `./files/*`, its folder).
11. **Demos:** `examples/html` (one `index.html`, an import map onto the
    packages' `dist/`, served by `scripts/serve.mjs`) and `examples/react`
    (Vite + React 19) are workspace members that depend on the packages by
    name and import only their public exports. `scripts/demo-check.mjs` uses
    both in Chromium (flag, resolve, edit + Download read back, font, pop-up,
    CSV, refusal; in React also the hooks strip and the column rules; the
    review steps driven by `@sheetpane/testing`, SR-TESTING) —
    `just demo-check`, on every push; `scripts/demo-packed.mjs`
    installs both from `pnpm pack` tarballs (every package, the eight plugins
    included) outside the workspace and runs the same check — `just
    demo-packed`, nightly. Both share one look (2026-10-19): a host bar
    (Views, Open file…, the CSV sample, the pop-up, Font, and Theme — light ·
    dark · auto, set on every component), the components filling the window,
    and a footer of host events (the `sheetpane-export` line names the file,
    the format and the first 12 hex digits of its SHA-256, W-65);
    `examples/react/src/demo.css` is the
    stylesheet the HTML demo inlines.
11a. **The plugin gallery (W-32):** both demos carry a second tab row —
    Review (the demo above) · Vanilla · Number formats · Styles · Formulas ·
    Validation · Conditional formats · Images · Charts · Comments · All
    plugins · Hide and show (W-49: `@sheetpane/visibility` — hide a row from
    its header menu, the marker unhides it) · Tables (W-61: `tables
    validation` on the showcase's Tables sheet — both tables in their style
    colours, and C9 typed "furlong" fails the list over `Units[Unit]`) · Compare (W-63:
    `@sheetpane/compare` — the fixtures' `compare/now.xlsx` against
    `compare/base.xlsx`, which the host fetches and hands to `compareWith`;
    `demo-check` reads the status line's 4 sheets · 7 rows · 2 cells, the
    amber price, the 7 listed changes and Alt+F5 to D4) · Review sheet (W-59:
    `@sheetpane/review` — the download gains a Review sheet listing the
    review, flagged cells coloured) · Rules file (W-33: the showcase's rules sample — `rules-src` in
    HTML, the `rules` prop in React — with `flagging="off"`). Every gallery
    tab opens one showcase workbook from `@sheetpane/fixtures` (SR-FIXTURES:
    the HTML import path `./node_modules/@sheetpane/fixtures/files/…`, a
    `?url` import in React; W-42) on its
    own `pane`, mounted when the tab first opens and kept after; a plugin's
    peer loads with it (condfmt with styles, charts with images). Both demos
    depend on all eight plugins, and the HTML import map lists them with
    `numfmt` (its ESM build, `dist/index.mjs`) and `@ironcalc/wasm`.
    `demo-check` asserts per tab: Vanilla plain (1.25, no overlay, no errors);
    1 1/4; the yellow fill; B6 recalculated; two rule errors; a data bar; the
    picture; both charts; the note and the thread; all of them together; lazy
    mounting and edits kept; the Rules file tab's six errors with no Flag issue
    and no card on F or a click; the Tables tab's two header fills and C9's
    list.

### Consequences

- **Codes (W-40):** `test/error-codes.test.ts` and its append-only `test/error-codes.lock.json` are SR-CODES' (carved out of `test/`); `test/ssr.test.ts` asserts the SSR refusal's code.
- **Enforced today:** decisions 6, 7 and 10 by `just check` / `just
  pack-check`, locally and in CI.
- **Owed by the decider:** the first publish by hand (any package not yet on
  npm), a trusted publisher per package (`publish.yml`, environment `npm`,
  *Allow npm publish*) and the `npm` environment in GitHub — `RELEASING.md`
  §One time; the `@sheetpane` organisation exists.
- **Still open:** the licence check over the whole lockfile (backlog B-008);
  decision 7 checks only the runtime allow-list.
- **Plugins must keep `@sheetpane/grid` as a dev dependency too** (a peer is
  not installed for the package's own tests).

### Alternatives considered

- A bundler (tsup, Vite library mode) — rejected: `tsc` output is already
  valid ESM; a bundler adds a tool and hides import mistakes.
- Building before type-checking siblings (project references) — rejected for
  the `source` condition: no build step in the edit–test loop.
- jsdom/happy-dom for DOM tests — rejected by the testing verdict.
- Changesets — rejected: lockstep needs one version, not per-package bumps.

### Reference (required)

- [`justfile`](../justfile) · [`vitest.config.ts`](../vitest.config.ts) ·
  [`test/packages.test.ts`](../test/packages.test.ts) ·
  [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml)
- [`work/compare/testing.compare.md`](../work/compare/testing.compare.md) — the runner.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a clean clone cannot run `just check` and
`just pack-check` green, or two packages carry different versions.

**How to check it:** `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && just check pack-check`

<!-- source: records/0103_EXPORT.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0103_EXPORT.md) -->

# SR-EXPORT — @sheetpane/export

## §1 — For humans

**Three writers, no dependencies.** `toXlsx(book)` builds a new `.xlsx` from
a plain object. `patchXlsx(original, changes)` takes the uploaded file and
rewrites only the cells that changed, so charts, styles, comments, names and
everything else survive. `toCsv(sheet)` writes one sheet as CSV that Excel
opens with accents intact and formulas defused.

**The same input gives the same bytes**, on every engine, in `store` mode —
the audit mode. The default compresses with what the platform ships.

**One ZIP and XML implementation for the whole project.** The reader
(`@sheetpane/import`) and the plugins import it from here.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    W["Workbook object"] --> X["toXlsx"] --> B1[".xlsx bytes"]
    O["uploaded .xlsx"] --> P["patchXlsx"]
    C["changes"] --> P --> B2[".xlsx bytes — only changed cells rewritten"]
    S["one Sheet"] --> V["toCsv"] --> T[".csv text + guarded refs"]
    Z["zip · crc32 · xml · refs"] -.-> X & P
    Z -.-> I["@sheetpane/import"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   Workbook object ---------------> toXlsx ----> .xlsx bytes
   uploaded .xlsx + changes ------> patchXlsx -> .xlsx bytes (only changed cells rewritten)
   one Sheet ---------------------> toCsv -----> .csv text + guarded refs
   zip · crc32 · xml · refs  ... used by the writers and by @sheetpane/import
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-03 asked for "a JavaScript object in, an Excel or CSV file out", the
dependency of the Excel component. The export verdict
([`export-shape.compare.md`](../work/compare/export-shape.compare.md)) fixed
the shape; SR-LAW-6 requires export to carry every change and keep everything
else.

### Decision

1. **Input:** `Cell = string | number | boolean | null`;
   `Sheet { name, rows, merges?, columnWidths?, hidden? }`; `SheetState =
   'visible' | 'hidden' | 'veryHidden'` (W-49);
   `Workbook { sheets }`; `Change { sheet, ref, value }`; `Sheet.freeze?:
   { rows, cols }` (W-24). `columnWidths` are
   Excel character units (`<col width>`), index 0 = column A.
   `Sheet.dataValidations?: DataValidation[]`, `Sheet.conditionalFormats?:
   ConditionalFormat[]` and `Workbook.dxfs?: Dxf[]` (W-57) — the shapes
   `@sheetpane/import` reads (`DataValidation`, `ConditionalFormat`,
   `CfRule`, `Cfvo`, `Dxf`, `Font`, `Fill`, `Border`, `BorderSide`,
   `Alignment`, `Color` are defined here and re-exported by import), so a
   rule read is a rule written; a rule's `dxfId` indexes `Workbook.dxfs`.
2. **`toXlsx(book, { compression?, onStripped? }): Promise<Uint8Array>`**
   writes exactly `[Content_Types].xml`, `_rels/.rels`, `xl/workbook.xml`,
   `xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels`, `xl/worksheets/sheetN.xml`, `xl/styles.xml`.
   Text → `t="inlineStr"`; numbers → `<v>`; booleans → `t="b"`; `null` → no
   `<c>`. Style 1 is the only format written: centred, on each merge's
   top-left cell. Hidden sheets get `state="hidden"`; the first visible sheet
   is the active tab. The file's default font in `styles.xml` is Excel's
   (Calibri 11) — a property of the file for Excel, never read for display
   (SR-LAW-5). `toXlsx` writes no formulas and takes no change list, so it
   writes no `<calcPr>`. **Rules (W-57):** each sheet's
   `conditionalFormats` as one `<conditionalFormatting>` per format and its
   `dataValidations` as one `<dataValidations>`, in schema order after
   `<mergeCells>` (`conditionalFormatting` before `dataValidations`);
   `Workbook.dxfs` as `<dxfs>` after `<cellStyles>` in `styles.xml` (a dxf's
   children in CT_Dxf order: font, numFmt, fill, alignment, border). A
   validation with a `prompt` or `promptTitle` gets `showInputMessage="1"`
   (the shape has no flag for it, and Excel shows no prompt without it);
   `type="none"` and false flags are left out; attribute line breaks and tabs,
   and a carriage return in a formula, are written as character references so
   both readers give them back. A workbook with no rules and no dxfs is
   written byte for byte as before.
3. **`patchXlsx(original, changes, { compression?, exportPatch?, onStripped?, maxEntrySize?, maxTotalSize? })`**
   - rewrites only the changed `<c>` elements of the touched sheets, keeping
     each cell's `s` (style); new text goes in as inline strings; shared
     strings stay in place;
   - copies every other ZIP entry's **compressed bytes** unchanged, in the
     original order, directory entries included;
   - writes `<calcPr fullCalcOnLoad="1"/>` (in schema order) whenever any
     cell changed;
   - sets `refreshOnLoad="1"` on every pivot cache whose `worksheetSource`
     meets a changed cell, and on any cache whose source is a name or table;
   - drops `xl/calcChain.xml` (part, relationship, content type) when a
     formula cell became a value — Excel rebuilds it;
   - when the master of a shared formula is overwritten, the first remaining
     dependent becomes the master, its formula shifted (`shiftFormula`);
   - reads rows and cells without `r`, self-closing rows and prefixed
     namespaces; widens `<dimension>` to new values; drops `spans` on touched
     rows;
   - `freeze: [{ sheet, rows, cols }]` rewrites that sheet's first view's
     `<pane>` (with `topLeftCell` and `state="frozen"`; `0, 0` removes it);
     sheets not named keep theirs byte for byte; `toXlsx` writes `<pane>`
     for `Sheet.freeze` (W-24);
   - `merges: [{ sheet, ranges }]` rewrites that sheet's `<mergeCells>` to
     exactly those ranges (in schema position; removed when empty);
   - `dataValidations: [{ sheet, rules }]` and `conditionalFormats: [{ sheet,
     formats }]` (W-57) rewrite that sheet's `<dataValidations>` and every
     top-level `<conditionalFormatting>` to exactly those (the new formats
     where the first old block stood, else in schema position after
     `mergeCells` / `phoneticPr`; `dataValidations` after them; removed when
     empty); Excel 2010's `x14:` rules inside `<extLst>` are left as they are
     (import does not read them). `dxfs: Dxf[]` is appended to the file's
     `<dxfs>` (count updated; created before `tableStyles` / `colors` /
     `extLst` when missing; a package with no style sheet gets sheetpane's,
     with its relationship and content type); a rule's `dxfId` counts the
     file's formats first, then the appended ones. Everything is checked
     before anything is written; sheets not named stay byte for byte.
     `setDataValidations(xml, rules)` and `setConditionalFormats(xml,
     formats, dxfCount)` are exported for an `exportPatch` hook;
   - `hidden: [{ sheet, rows?, cols?, state?, outline?: { rows?, cols? } }]`
     (W-49): each list and outline map is the sheet's whole set after the
     edit (0-based); fields not given are left alone. Rows: the listed rows
     get `hidden="1"` (a missing `<row>` is created empty, `sheetData` kept in
     order), every other row loses `hidden`, and a zero `ht` loses
     `ht`/`customHeight`. Columns: `<col>` spans are split and merged so
     exactly the listed columns carry `hidden="1"`, width, style and
     `customWidth` kept on every piece; a shown zero-width column loses
     `width`; `<cols>` is created before `<sheetData>` and removed when
     empty. Outline: `outlineLevel` (0–7) per row and column, `sheetFormatPr
     outlineLevelRow/Col` the deepest level (`sheetFormatPr` added when
     missing); `collapsed` is never written. Sheets: `state` sets `<sheet
     state>` (`visible` removes it); when the active sheet ends up hidden,
     `activeTab` and `firstSheet` move to the first visible sheet and
     `tabSelected` moves with it, or Excel opens a blank window. Refusals: an
     unknown sheet → `no-sheet`, a bad index → `bad-ref`, a bad level or
     state → `bad-value`, no visible sheet left → `sheet-count`. Sheets not
     named stay byte for byte. Checked through ExcelJS and the import
     package; not yet opened in Excel or LibreOffice (W-30's files);
   - `structure: [{ sheet, op, at, count }]` (W-52) inserts and deletes rows
     and columns in the upload first, in order — decision 11; `changes`,
     `merges`, `freeze` and `hidden` are then given as the sheet stands
     after them;
   - runs each `exportPatch` hook after its own writes, with a
     `PatchContext` (`list`, `has`, `readText`, `readBytes`, `write`,
     `remove`, `workbookPath`, `sheetNames`, `sheetPath`, `relsPathOf`,
     `addRelationship`, `setContentType`, `setDefaultContentType`).
4. **`toCsv(sheet, { delimiter?, bom?, eol?, guardFormulas? }): { text, guarded }`**
   — defaults `,`, CRLF, BOM on, guard on. Fields with the delimiter, `"`, CR
   or LF are quoted, inner quotes doubled; ragged rows are padded to one
   width; the last line ends with the line ending. **The guard** prefixes `'`
   to text starting `=` `+` `-` `@` tab or CR, **unless the text is a plain
   numeral** (`-150`, `+1`, `1,200.50`, `-2e3`) — data, not a formula — and
   returns the guarded refs. Booleans are `TRUE` / `FALSE`.
5. **Strings:** SpreadsheetML's own escape — CR as `_x000D_`, a literal
   `_xHHHH_` protected as `_x005F_xHHHH_`; `xml:space="preserve"` when
   whitespace would be lost. Characters XML forbids are stripped and the
   cells reported through `onStripped`.
6. **Rules** (errors are `ExportError` with a `code` and the `sheet` /
   `ref`): sheet names 1–31 characters, none of `[ ] : * ? / \`, no leading
   or trailing `'`, unique ignoring case; at least one sheet, at least one
   visible; ≤ 1,048,576 rows and ≤ 16,384 columns, naming the first cell
   over; finite numbers; ≤ 32,767 characters of text; merges of two or more
   cells that do not overlap. **Rules** (`bad-rule`, SP-2015, W-57): every
   `sqref` non-empty and each entry a cell or range; a known validation
   `type`, `operator` and `errorStyle`; `errorTitle` / `promptTitle` ≤ 32
   characters, `error` / `prompt` ≤ 255, a quoted list ≤ 255 — Excel's own
   limits, past which it repairs the file; a conditional format with at
   least one rule, a known `type`, `operator` and `timePeriod`, a whole
   `priority`, ≤ 3 formulas, a `dxfId` the workbook has; a colour scale with
   2–3 thresholds and one colour each, a data bar with 2 and a colour, an
   icon set with 2–5 and a known set name; `dxfs` a list of objects.
   Characters XML forbids are dropped from a rule's text.
7. **ZIP:** central-directory walk, sizes from the central directory, ZIP64
   and encrypted entries refused, methods 0 and 8 only, CRC-32 checked on
   every inflate; inflated size capped (512 MB per entry, 1 GB per archive by
   default); new entries get 1980-01-01, no extra fields, UTF-8 names.
8. **Compression:** `deflate` (default) through `zlib.deflateRawSync` in Node
   and `CompressionStream('deflate-raw')` in browsers; `store` is
   byte-identical on every engine. No DOM is touched (SR-LAW-8).
9. **Shared exports** for `@sheetpane/import` and plugins: `readZip`,
   `inflateEntry`, `rawData`, `writeZip`, `isZip`, `crc32`, the XML and
   OOXML-string helpers, `getAttr` / `setAttr` / `parseRels` /
   `resolveTarget` / `relsPathOf`, the A1 helpers, `shiftFormula`,
   `checkSheetName`, `resolveStructuredRef`.
9a. **Structured references (W-61):** `resolveStructuredRef(formula,
    sheets)` turns a table reference into `{ sheet, table, range, ref }`
    from the tables each sheet carries (SR-IMPORT decision 13; any `{ name,
    ref, headerRowCount, totalsRowCount, columns }` fits — `TableShape`):
    `Table[Column]` and `[[#Data],[Column]]` are the column's data rows;
    `#Headers`, `#Totals`, `#All` and touching pairs of them
    (`#Headers,#Data`, `#Data,#Totals`) name the bands; `[[A]:[B]]` a
    column span; `Table[]`, `Table[#Data]` and the bare `Table` the data
    body. Table and column names are case-insensitive; `'` escapes `[ ] #
    '`. `[#This Row]` / `@`, a union of columns, bands that do not touch and
    a band the table does not have resolve to `undefined`. `patchXlsx`
    leaves table parts as they are (a test reads both tables back after an
    edit); moving a table's `ref` when rows are inserted is W-52's.
10. **No runtime dependencies** (SR-LAW-2). `download()` lives in this
    package too — [SR-DOWNLOAD](0101_DOWNLOAD.md).
11. **Rows and columns inserted or deleted (W-52):** one operation is
    `StructureOp { sheet, op: 'insertRows' | 'deleteRows' | 'insertCols' |
    'deleteCols', at (0-based), count }`, and **one implementation** shifts
    for it (`structure.ts`, shared with `@sheetpane/import` and the grid):
    an index moves or is deleted; a span widens on an insert strictly inside
    it and is clipped by a delete, gone when wholly deleted; a leading count
    (a frozen split) grows or shrinks; A1 text keeps its `$` signs (absolute
    references move too, as in Excel); `restructureFormula(f, host, op)`
    moves every reference to the sheet — qualified, or unqualified on the
    host sheet — and writes `#REF!` (`Sheet1!#REF!`) for a deleted target,
    leaving strings, other sheets, external (`[1]Sheet!A1`), 3-D and
    structured references alone. `patchXlsx`'s `structure` option
    (`restructure.ts`) rewrites, per operation: the sheet's rows and cells
    (deleted ones go, `spans` dropped), every sheet's cell formulas (a shared
    group that names the sheet is written out per cell; array and data-table
    ranges move), `<dimension>`, the frozen pane's split and corner, the
    selections, `<cols>` (a span an insert starts inside is split — new
    columns take the default width; neighbours a delete closes up rejoin),
    `<mergeCells>`, the autofilter (filter columns follow their column) and
    sort state, the existing `<dataValidations>` and `<conditionalFormatting>`
    blocks and their x14 twins (a block wholly deleted goes — its own
    function, `restructureRuleBlocks`), hyperlinks,
    protected ranges, ignored errors, cell watches and page breaks; tables
    (range, autofilter, a deleted column's `<tableColumn>`, calculated
    formulas), drawing anchors (a point in a deleted row is pulled to the
    gap), legacy notes and their VML shapes, threaded comments, every chart's
    series (`restructureChartXml`), and the defined names; then drops the
    calculation chain and sets `fullCalcOnLoad`. **Refused, the file left
    as it was** (`bad-structure`, SP-2016): moving a pivot table or its
    worksheet source, cutting an array formula or a data table, and a table
    cut it cannot follow (`tableRefusal`: all of it, its header or totals
    row, every data row, or columns inserted inside it). **Order (W-57):**
    the structure is applied to the upload first; every other option
    (`changes`, `merges`, `dataValidations`, `conditionalFormats`, `dxfs`,
    `freeze`, `hidden`) is then written as given, against the sheet as it
    stands after it — so a sheet's rules given whole land where the caller
    put them and are never moved again, and a block not named is the file's
    own, shifted.

**Codes (W-40):** `@sheetpane/export` owns the code registry (SR-CODES: `CODES`, `spError`, `spMessage`, `codeOf`, `detailOf`, `codeUrl`); `ExportError` gains `spCode` and `spDetail` (`code` unchanged, the message prefixed `SP-2xxx`); `download()` refuses with SP-2101 to SP-2107. W-57 adds SP-2015 (`bad-rule`).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** the Node tests (`just test-export`) and the browser
  tests (`just test-pkg export-browser`, which also catch real downloads —
  SR-DOWNLOAD): independent read-back through ExcelJS,
  PapaParse and fflate; fast-check properties (CSV identity, `toXlsx`
  identity, `patchXlsx` changes exactly the named cells, string escape;
  W-57: `import(toXlsx(x))` and `import(patchXlsx(upload, x))` give the
  validation, conditional-format and dxf tables `x` back, through DOMParser
  and the built-in XML reader — `packages/import/test/rules*.test.ts`);
  the committed golden `sheetpane-sample.store.xlsx` reproduced in Node and
  Chromium; coverage gate 90 % lines.
- **Opened by the decider, 2026-10-18:** `sheetpane-sample.xlsx` and
  `sheetpane-sample.store.xlsx` open in Excel and LibreOffice with no repair
  prompt, and `sheetpane-sample.csv` shows its accents correctly in Excel. "Excel
  opens it" is backed by Excel and LibreOffice as well as three independent
  readers.
- **Rules are checked for structure, not against the schema** (W-57): the
  tests read what is written back through ExcelJS and the import package;
  ECMA-376 schema validation is B-033. Opening a generated file with working
  dropdowns and formats in Excel and LibreOffice is W-30 DoD 3.
- `patchXlsx`'s `dxfs` are appended, never deduplicated or removed: a format
  no rule names any more stays in `styles.xml` (harmless, like orphaned
  shared strings).
- **W-52 (2026-10-19):** `restructure.test.ts` (21; with W-57, rules given whole written
  after the shift, as given, and a block not named shifted) — every part above on a
  hand-written workbook (`test/fixtures/structure.ts`) with ExcelJS read-back,
  the refusals, and the fast-check property that inserting then deleting the
  same span gives back every part byte for byte; `structure.test.ts` (9) for
  the pure shifts; `@sheetpane/import`'s property that the moved workbook
  reads the same as the moved file. Opening a shifted Excel-saved file in
  Excel is the decider's (W-30).
- Shared strings orphaned by a patch stay in the table (harmless; keeps the
  patch small); the table's `count` is not recomputed.

### Alternatives considered

- Patch via `DOMParser` — rejected: Node has no DOM, and this package must
  run in Node 22+.
- Re-compressing untouched parts — rejected: copying the compressed bytes is
  faster and provably byte-identical.
- A shared-string table in `toXlsx` — rejected by the verdict (inline strings
  are simpler and deterministic).

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/export/src/`](../packages/export/src/) — the code;
  [`packages/export/test/`](../packages/export/test/) — the tests.
- [`work/compare/export-shape.compare.md`](../work/compare/export-shape.compare.md) — the verdict.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a fixture fails to read back, the store-mode
golden differs between engines, or the package gains a runtime dependency.

**How to check it:** `just test-export && just test-pkg export-browser && node -e "const p=require('./packages/export/package.json');console.log(Object.keys(p.dependencies||{}).length?'VIOLATION':'zero-dep')"`
