<!-- source: records/0106_ERRORS.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0106_ERRORS.md) -->

# SR-ERRORS — <sheetpane-errors>

## §1 — For humans

**The reviewer's checklist, anywhere on the page.** The host puts
`<sheetpane-errors pane="q3">` beside the sheet, in a side column, in another
tab or inside a pop-up. It lists every error flagged on the workbook — what
was found, what it should be — and holds the form that **Flag issue** opens.

**It is never out of step.** It keeps nothing of its own: an error added,
resolved or deleted here shows in the sheet at once, and the reverse (L7).
There is no "linked" chip and no export footer — it is always linked.

**A known deviation can be accepted.** *Accept…* asks why; the error then
stays in the review and the download with who, when and the reason, but no
longer counts as open (W-69).

**Several reviews can share one pane (W-51).** Errors come in named layers —
say *Validation* and *PDF check* — each replaced whole by the host and kept
whole. With two or more, a switch in the header shows one layer, or all;
the sheet shows the same.

**Every edit is one tab away.** *Edits n* beside *Problems* lists each change
in the pane — the cell, what it was and is now, when, and the errors it
cleared or raised — and each has its own **Revert** (W-64).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S[("the pane's workbook")] --> L["list: filter · pick · Show in sheet · Resolve · Delete"]
    S --> F["New error form (when Flag issue fires)"]
    L -->|"Accept… + a reason"| S
    L --> S
    F -->|Add error| S
    L -->|sheetpane-reveal| H["host switches tab / opens the pop-up"]
    S --> E["Edits: was → now · cleared / raised · Revert"]
    E -->|"Revert / Revert all (one undo step)"| S
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   ( pane's workbook ) --> list (filter, pick, Show in sheet, Resolve, Delete) --> workbook
                       --> New error form (Flag issue) --Add error--> workbook
   list --sheetpane-reveal--> host switches tab / opens the pop-up
   list --Accept… + a reason--> workbook (accepted: kept, not counted)
   ( pane's workbook ) --> Edits (was -> now, cleared / raised) --Revert / Revert all--> workbook
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-02 asked for the error component, always linked to the sheet. The schema,
the store and the contract are the contract verdict's and
[SR-GRID](0105_GRID.md)'s; this record owns the element.

### Decision

1. **The element** registers on import; attributes `pane`, `readonly`,
   `author`, `plugins`, `theme` (SR-GRID decision 15a), `results` (decision 15), `layers` (W-51, decision 16); properties `workbook`, `errors`, `errorTypes`,
   `readOnly`, `theme`, `results`, `renderDetail` (W-68, decision 13), `layers`, `layerNames` (W-51); methods `getErrors({ layer? })`, `setErrors(list | envelope, { plugins?, layer? })`; events
   `sheetpane-errors {v, errors, plugins, layers, changed}` (the v2 envelope, SR-GRID 5d), `sheetpane-layers {visible, layers}`, `sheetpane-change`,
   `sheetpane-select`, `sheetpane-history`, `sheetpane-reveal {error}` —
   bubbling, composed; an action's event fires on the element where it
   happened.
2. **No private copy:** every render reads the store — the errors in the
   visible layers (`visibleErrors`, SR-GRID 5d). Connecting registers the
   element with the store, so Flag issue opens the form here and not in the
   sheet; disconnecting releases it.
3. **The list:** "n open" (problems only — decision 15); severity filter (All · ✕ · ! · i, each with its
   count of problems) and — when errors come from more than people — an author filter
   (People · Workbook rules · Column rules — "Rules file" when the pane has
   a rules file, its rows then grouped by sheet — · File comments); rows open first then resolved,
   by number; each row shows the number (✓ when resolved), the type's name,
   Found → Should be, the range and severity, and tags (cell changed ·
   resolved · matches suggestion · stale · hidden row · hidden column ·
   hidden sheet — W-49: picking such a row shows the place in the sheet,
   SR-GRID 21c). **Errors with no cell come first (W-55, SR-GRID 5a):** a
   *Workbook* group, then one group per sheet for its whole-sheet errors
   (*Holdings · whole sheet*) in the workbook's sheet order, then the cell
   errors under *Cells*. The filters apply within each group, and keyboard
   order follows the groups. Such a row reads *whole sheet* or *workbook* where a
   range would be, and has no Found → Should be line when both are empty.
   Picking a row selects its cell
   (selection syncs) and expands it: the message, author and time, **Show in
   sheet**, Resolve / Reopen, **Accept…** (an open error, decision 14),
   Delete. **Accepted errors are not counted (W-69):** "n open", the severity
   chips and *All* leave them out, and the list hides them until the
   **Accepted n** chip (shown while any exists) is pressed — it then lists
   only them, the other filters still applying.
4. **Show in sheet** selects the cell and dispatches `sheetpane-reveal
   {error}`, so the host can switch tab or open the pop-up. For a whole-sheet
   error it opens the sheet's tab, as a tab click does, and keeps the
   selection if it is already on that sheet. For a workbook-level error it is
   disabled, with *About the whole workbook — no sheet to show* beside it, and
   nothing is dispatched (W-55).
5. **The form** (while the pane is composing, in Edit, and never when the
   pane is `flagging="off"` — SR-GRID 22e): the cell, Found (the
   uploaded text), Column (the header text found above, and the letter), Row
   (number and first value); type chips from `errorTypes` (each with its
   default severity); What’s wrong; What it should be; **Also change the cell
   to this value**; severity Error / Warning / Note with its help line; the
   chosen type's example; Add error (⌘/Ctrl+↵) and Cancel (Esc). A
   `duplicate-row` error covers the whole row.
6. **`errorTypes`** defaults to the seven types and Other from the board
   `Edit-Examples` (`DEFAULT_ERROR_TYPES`, SR-GRID).
7. **`readonly`** hides the form, Resolve, Accept…, Delete, Undo and Redo — a sign-off
   screen. Errors authored `workbook`, `file` or `host` are always read-only
   (SR-GRID decision 19b) and named from `BUILTIN_TYPE_NAMES` when the
   host's `errorTypes` does not name their type.
8. **A saved review** restored with a different plugin set shows the
   "formatted differently" notice (plugins verdict decision 3).
9. **Undo / Redo** buttons and Ctrl/⌘+Z, Ctrl+Y, ⌘+Shift+Z act on the pane's
   one stack (W-23).
10. **Font (L5):** no font family; every control is `font: inherit`.
    Severity is a glyph and a colour, never colour alone.

11. **Codes (W-40, SR-CODES):** `SheetpaneError` gains an optional `code`
    (`SP-xxxx`, additive to v1); a machine-authored note from the rules engine
    always sets it, and the expanded row shows it beside the author and time.

12. **Test hooks (W-41):** rows carry `data-sp-error` and `data-sp-ref`; Resolve `data-sp="resolve"`; the form's Add `data-sp="add-error"` (SR-GRID decision 9a lists them all).

13. **The host's detail (W-68):** `renderDetail(error) → Node | string |
    null | undefined`, a property on this element and on `<sheetpane-excel>`,
    each its own. It is called with a copy of the error (its `meta`, SR-GRID
    5b, included) and its result is drawn in a `part="detail"` region right
    after the message: in the open row here, in the error card in the sheet.
    So the host's focusable controls come after the row's button (the card's
    previous / next) and before Show in sheet, Resolve and Delete. A string
    is text, never parsed as HTML; a Node is trusted host code, placed as it
    is. `null`, `undefined` or `''` leaves the region empty, and an empty
    region takes no room. The hook runs again only when that error changes
    (`meta` included) or the hook is replaced, so a list re-drawn for another
    error keeps the host's node. A throw is logged as SP-3017 and shows
    nothing. Clicks, input and keys inside the region are the host's: the
    element does not act on them. No hook, no region.

14. **Accept… (W-69):** in the open row of an open error a person may
    change (not `readonly`, not machine-authored — as Resolve), **Accept…**
    opens a small form after the row's buttons: *Why is this accepted?*
    (required — **Accept** stays disabled while it is blank), Cancel and
    Accept. Focus goes to the reason; Esc or Cancel closes it and returns
    focus to Accept…; ⌘/Ctrl+↵ accepts. Accepting calls the store's
    `acceptError` (SR-GRID 5c) with this element's `author` as who — one
    undo step, so Ctrl/⌘+Z here or in the sheet takes it back. The row then
    moves under the Accepted chip, which takes focus. An accepted row's badge
    reads **A** and its name ends *, accepted*; open, it shows *Accepted by
    <who> · <when>* and the reason after the message, and Reopen (which drops
    them). The sheet's error card shows the same lines and Reopen (SR-GRID
    13); the form itself is only here. The workbook's own errors (validation,
    file comments) are not accepted here — B-029.

15. **Results (W-50):** `pass` and `skipped` entries (SR-GRID decision 23)
    are listed apart from the problems. The `results` attribute (and
    property) sets the pane's level, as on the sheet. **Summary line** —
    under the header whenever the pane holds results and the level is not
    `off`: "*n* problems · ✓ *n* passed · — *n* not checked" (problems are
    open entries; results are cells) and an **On sheet** `role="switch"`
    that moves the pane between `summary` and `marks` (a view setting: no
    change, no undo step). **Chips** — *Problems n* · *✓ Passed n* · *— Not
    checked n*, the result chips only when such results exist; *Problems* is
    the default and the only view with the severity and author filters.
    **Groups** — *Passed* lists one row per check (`type` + `message`),
    *Not checked* one per reason (`message`, else `type`); each says its
    name (the message, else the type's name), its cell count and where it
    is (one range when its cells fill it, "H6, H31, H44 …" otherwise, "*n*
    sheets" across sheets), largest first, with **Show ▸**: it selects the
    group's bounding range on its first sheet, marks that range's results on
    the sheet even at `summary` (`store.focusResults`) and fires
    `sheetpane-reveal` with the group's first entry. A group opens to its
    entries, **virtualised** — 28 px rows in a box at most 280 px tall, only
    the rows in view (± 4) in the DOM; each row (with `data-sp-error` and
    `data-sp-ref`) is Show in sheet for that entry, and marks its range.
    **Counts that ask for action ignore results:** "n open", the severity
    filters, and the sheet's tab and toolbar counts (SR-GRID decision 23) —
    as they ignore accepted errors (decision 14); the summary line's *n*
    problems and the *Problems n* chip leave both out too. **Problems** is
    the view decision 3 describes — W-55's *Workbook* and whole-sheet groups
    above *Cells*, the severity, **Accepted n** and author filters, the
    expanded row with the host's detail (decision 13) and Accept…; the
    result views have none of these. The form offers the three problem
    severities only.
16. **Layers (W-51, SR-GRID 5d):** with two or more layers in the pane, the
    header shows a switch — `role="group"`, *Review layers* — of toggle
    buttons: **All**, then each layer in the pane's order with its open
    count (*PDF check 2*), each `aria-pressed` while shown. A layer's
    button shows that layer alone; All shows every layer; focus stays on
    the button pressed. The list, "n open", the severity and author filters
    and the Accepted chip — and the summary line, the result chips and groups (decision 15) — read the shown layers only; while more than one
    is shown, each row's tags name its layer. A layer is called by
    `layerNames[id]`, else `review` reads *Review* and any other its id.
    The `layers` attribute or property (on this element or the sheet — the
    pane's one setting) sets what is shown; the switch and the attribute
    fire `sheetpane-layers {visible, layers}` on the element acted on.
    `setErrors(envelope)` reads `plugins` from the envelope for the notice
    (decision 8); `setErrors(list, { layer })` replaces one layer and leaves
    the notice as it was.

17. **Edits (W-64):** an **Edits n** chip after the others in the view
    switch (decision 15) — *n* the change map's size — lists every edit in
    the pane from `store.edits()` (SR-GRID decision 24), newest first. It
    shows in Edit mode, and in View mode only while the pane holds edits; in
    Edit mode with no results the switch is *Problems n · Edits n*. A
    **row** per change-map entry (`data-sp-edit="<key>"`, `data-sp-ref`):
    its place (`Sheet!B3`, `Sheet!A1:J1`, or *Sheet · whole sheet*) and kind
    (*Value*, *Formula*, *Style*, *Number format*, *Merge*, *Freeze panes*,
    *Hidden rows* / *columns*, *Sheet visibility*, *Row* / *Column groups*,
    *Rows and columns* — a sheet's inserts and deletes, W-52, one row per
    sheet; any other kind by its own name), **was → now** (a cell's value as
    the cell shows it, *(blank)* for none; *as read → 2 rows inserted at 3,
    column C deleted* for rows and columns; other kinds in a few words; its
    Revert takes every insert and delete on the sheet back as one undo step,
    SR-GRID 24), the time, and how many
    errors it cleared or raised. Under it, one link per error from
    `store.editEffects(key)` — *✓ Cleared error 3: Out of range*, *✕
    Raised …*, *= Matches the suggestion of …* — which opens that error in
    *Problems* (filters cleared, the row expanded and focused, its cell
    selected); an error in a layer not shown (W-51, decision 16) is named
    but not linked. **Picking** a row selects its cell or range, or opens the
    sheet's tab for a whole-sheet edit. **Revert** (`data-sp="revert-edit"`,
    named *Revert <place>*) on each row and **Revert all**
    (`data-sp="revert-all"`, in a bar above the list with the count) call
    `store.revertEdits` — each one undo step, firing `sheetpane-change` per
    entry here; only in Edit mode and not `readonly`, as Undo. After a
    Revert, focus goes to the next row's Revert, else the previous one's,
    else the Edits chip. **Keys:** ↓ ↑ Home End move between rows; Enter
    or Space picks; Tab reaches the row's Revert, then its links. The view
    draws 100 rows, then **Show 100 more**. No filters (they are
    *Problems*'), no form of its own; the empty view says what will be
    listed.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `packages/grid/test/errors.test.ts` (form, list,
  filters, reveal, readonly, `errorTypes`, events, notice, font, axe; W-55:
  the groups and their order, keyboard order, the tab count, Show in sheet
  for a sheet and disabled for the workbook, restore, axe; W-68: a string as
  text in the card and the row, a Node kept until its error changes, the hook
  replaced, a throw as SP-3017, the region's clicks left to the host, focus
  order, axe; W-69: Accept… with a required reason, who / when / why, the
  counts and the Accepted chip in both elements, the pin and the card, Esc,
  Cancel and ⌘↵, one undo step, Reopen, `readonly` and a rule's row, axe with
  the form open; W-51: no switch with one layer, the switch's buttons and
  counts and `layerNames`, a layer chosen in the list, the sheet's pins,
  marks, toolbar and tab counts, `sheetpane-layers` on the element acted on,
  keyboard, the `layers` attribute and property on either element, a new
  error in the shown layer, the v2 envelope and its `changed`, a restore
  from it with the plugins notice, axe with a layer chosen) and the
  L7 sync test in both mount orders with the errors element inside a
  `<dialog>`; the undo-across-elements test in `plugins.test.ts`;
  `results.test.ts` (W-50: the summary line and chips only with results,
  Problems by default, groups by check and by reason with their counts and
  ranges, Show ▸ marking at `summary`, Show in sheet for all five
  severities, the On sheet switch from here marking the sheet, counts that
  ignore results, axe with a group open, 5,000 passes as two rows and an
  opened group drawing fewer than 20 rows as it scrolls; with W-55 and
  W-69, the Problems view keeping the scope groups and the Accepted chip,
  and every count leaving out results and accepted errors alike);
  `edits.test.ts` (W-64: with W-52, a sheet's inserts and deletes as one
  *Rows and columns* row and its Revert one undo step; `edits()` newest first, one step's edits in map
  order, a sheet's W-52 operations as one entry; `revertEdits` one and all as
  one undo step each, undo bringing the times back; `editEffects` cleared,
  raised and matched, compared with before the cell first changed; with
  W-51, an error in a layer not shown named but not linked; the view
  in Edit mode and only with edits in View; rows, picking a cell, a range
  and a whole-sheet edit; Revert and Revert all with focus, undo, View and
  `readonly`; ↓ ↑ Home End Enter Tab; 250 edits in pages of 100; L7 both
  ways; axe with links and in View).

- **Known gap (found by W-55):** axe's label-in-name rule (WCAG 2.5.3) fails
  on every row and filter in the browser's default font. For example,
  *All 4* is named *All severities: 4*. The host-font axe test passes only
  because of the font, and the W-55 axe test turns that one rule off and
  says why. Not fixed yet.

### Alternatives considered

- A linked / not-linked chip and an export footer — removed by the decider
  (2026-10-18): the element is always linked, and export belongs to the sheet.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/grid/src/errors/element.ts`](../packages/grid/src/errors/element.ts)
- [`work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md`](../work/compare/workbook-and-error-contract.compare.md)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** the errors element is ever seen showing an error
the sheet does not, or the reverse.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg grid -t "always in sync"`

<!-- source: records/0107_IMAGES.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0107_IMAGES.md) -->

# SR-IMAGES — @sheetpane/images

## §1 — For humans

**The pictures in a workbook show where the author put them.** With
`@sheetpane/images` on a pane, every picture a sheet anchors — a logo, a
signature, a photo — is drawn over the grid at its cells, scrolls with them
and sits under the error pins. It is view only: pictures are never changed,
and export keeps them exactly as they were.

**Nothing is decoded until it is needed.** A picture is read from the file
only when it scrolls near the screen; a format the browser cannot show (EMF,
WMF) gets a labelled frame instead.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    I["@sheetpane/import: drawings (anchors + media paths)"] --> P["images(): overlay hook"]
    G["the grid's Geometry"] --> P
    P --> O["OverlayItem: rect + <img> (blob: URL, lazy) or a frame"]
    O --> V["drawn under the pins, in sheet space"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   import: drawings (anchors + media) --+
   the grid's Geometry -----------------+--> images(): overlay --> rect + <img> (lazy blob: URL) or a frame --> under the pins
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-20 asked for the first `overlay` provider; the plugins verdict made
pictures a plugin and view only. The reader exposes drawing anchors and the
media parts (SR-IMPORT decision 2).

### Decision

1. **`images()`** → `{ id: 'images', provides: ['overlay'] }`; importing the
   package registers `images` (`sideEffects` names the entry). No `./ui`
   entry; one `status` control: "N pictures · M preview unavailable".
2. **Items:** each `picture` drawing of the sheet is one `OverlayItem`
   (charts and shapes are skipped; a picture without media or with no area
   is skipped). Ids carry a workbook generation, so a cached element is never
   reused across workbooks. `alt` and the image's `alt` come from `descr`,
   else the name.
3. **Anchors** (`src/anchors.ts`, public, DOM-free — `@sheetpane/charts`
   imports it): 9,525 EMU per pixel; `twoCell` from/to with offsets, `oneCell`
   from + `ext`, `absolute` `pos` + `ext`, placed in the **grid's** `Geometry`
   (28 px rows; hidden rows and columns shown, as the grid shows them), not in
   Excel's row heights. An offset is clamped to its own cell.
4. **Media** (`src/media.ts`, the one file that makes object URLs): read
   through `book.part()` only when the item nears the viewport
   (IntersectionObserver, 300 px margin); the format sniffed from the bytes,
   the extension as fallback; PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP and SVG shown through
   `<img>` (never inline SVG); one URL per part.
5. **No preview:** EMF, WMF, TIFF, bytes that do not decode and a missing part
   show a frame "name — preview unavailable" at the anchor's size, without
   reading the bytes when the extension already says so.
6. **Lifetime:** every URL is revoked, once, when the pane loads another
   workbook or a load fails; a decode still running then makes no URL.
7. **Interaction:** in Edit a click on a picture selects the cell under the
   click; in View it does nothing.
8. **Export:** nothing — patch mode copies drawing and media parts byte for
   byte (SR-EXPORT). Deleting rows does not re-anchor pictures (there is no
   row deletion in v1).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg images` — 29 tests (anchor arithmetic;
  rects against the rendered cells for every anchor type and at 150 % zoom;
  decode of each raster format; the EMF frame; URL revocation; click to
  select), Chromium per push, WebKit locally green.
- **Owed:** pictures from files saved by Excel and LibreOffice, and positions
  compared with Excel's own rendering — W-30 (the decider's files). Because the
  grid's rows are 28 px, a picture in a file with taller or shorter rows sits
  differently than in Excel (decision 3).
- **A store that is dropped without loading another workbook keeps its URLs
  until the page goes** — the plugin contract has no dispose signal.

### Alternatives considered

- Excel's row heights and hidden rows for placement — rejected: the grid does
  not draw them, and a picture must sit on the cells the user sees.
- `data:` URLs — rejected: the bytes would live as strings for the page's life.
- Inline SVG — rejected: file-supplied markup in the page.
- Decoding at load — rejected: a 20 MB photo should cost nothing off screen.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/images/src/`](../packages/images/src/) · [`packages/images/test/`](../packages/images/test/)
- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) — the `overlay` hook.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a picture's frame stops matching the cells its
anchor names in the grid, or a URL outlives its workbook.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg images`

---

is never listed here.*

**Code**

- [`packages/images/src/index.ts`](../packages/images/src/index.ts) · [`anchors.ts`](../packages/images/src/anchors.ts) · [`media.ts`](../packages/images/src/media.ts)

**Project docs**

- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) · [`work/reference/design/boards/Plugin-Images.dc.html`](../work/reference/design/boards/Plugin-Images.dc.html)

<!-- source: records/0108_VALIDATION.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0108_VALIDATION.md) -->

# SR-VALIDATION — @sheetpane/validation

## §1 — For humans

**The file's own rules find the wrong cells before a person does.** A
workbook that says "Units must be a whole number above 0" or "Status is one of
Core, Income, Cap" gets every breaking cell listed in `<sheetpane-errors>` as
a warning from the workbook, on load and after every edit.

**They clear themselves.** Fix the cell and the warning resolves; break it
again and it reopens. They are the workbook's, so a person cannot resolve or
delete them. A list rule gives the cell a ▾ in Edit with the allowed values.

**The host's rules go back out as Excel's own (W-58).** With *Write rules as
Excel dropdowns* on, the download carries the host's rules file as the
workbook's data validation: "Status is one of Active, Inactive" becomes a
dropdown in Excel, "Units is a whole number of at least 1" a check. What
Excel cannot hold — a pattern, "none of", unique — is listed, never dropped
silently, and a rule the workbook already had on those cells wins.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["<dataValidations> (import)"] --> V["validation(): validate hook"]
    S["the pane's cells (live)"] --> V
    V -->|one warning per failing cell, author workbook| E["the error list · ⚠ pins"]
    U["ui(): ▾ list arrow · status count"] --> S
    F["the host's rules file (store.columnRules)"] -->|export, rulesAsValidation| D["<dataValidations> in the download"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   <dataValidations> + live cells --> validation(): validate --> one warning per failing cell (author: workbook)
                                                                  --> error list, ⚠ pins
   ui(): list arrow ▾ (sets the cell), status count
   host rules file --export, rulesAsValidation--> <dataValidations> in the download (what Excel cannot hold: listed)
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-18 asked for the workbook's validation rules to land in the error pane; the
plugins verdict put them on the `validate` hook as workbook-authored errors
(SR-GRID decision 17).

### Decision

1. **`validation({ severity?, rulesAsValidation? })`** → `{ id: 'validation',
   provides: ['validate', 'exportPatch'], exportOptions }`;
   `@sheetpane/validation` registers it, `@sheetpane/validation/ui` registers
   it with `ui()` (`validation-ui`: a `cell` list arrow and a `status` count).
   No third-party runtime dependency; `@sheetpane/export` (a workspace
   package) writes the rules of decision 10 and gives `shiftFormula` and
   `resolveStructuredRef` (decision 4).
2. **One error per failing cell:** `type: 'validation'`, severity `warning`
   (the host may choose another), `author: 'workbook'`, `range` = the cell,
   `found` = its current text (`(blank)` when empty), `expected` = the rule in
   words, `message` = the rule's `errorTitle: error` (either alone), else the
   rule in words. When a cell breaks several rules, the first counts.
3. **Rule types:** `whole`, `decimal`, `date`, `time`, `textLength` with all
   eight operators (default `between`, inclusive); `list` from a literal, a
   range, another sheet's range, a defined name, a table's structured
   reference (`Units[Unit]`, `Units[[#Data],[Unit]]`, directly or through a
   defined name — W-61, resolved by `@sheetpane/export`'s
   `resolveStructuredRef`, re-exported by the grid, to the table's cells as
   the file stores its `ref`; it never shifts per cell), a **dependent list**
   `INDIRECT(<cell>)` (W-60, decision 9), or the x14 form; `custom`
   only through a `derive` provider exposing a synchronous `evaluate(formula,
   { sheet, ref })`, relative references shifted per cell —
   `@sheetpane/formulas` provides it (SR-FORMULAS decision 8).
4. **Operands:** numbers, quoted text, `DATE` / `TIME` with numeric
   arguments, cell references (relative parts shift from the rule's first
   cell, through `@sheetpane/export`'s `shiftFormula` — imported from
   `@sheetpane/export` itself since W-54, so the main entry needs no
   `@sheetpane/grid/check` at run time; the grid re-exports the same
   function), defined names and structured references (`resolveStructuredRef`,
   from `@sheetpane/export` the same way), and `INDIRECT` of one cell
   or of quoted text (`INDIRECT(x, TRUE)` too; decision 9); anything else — a
   table or column that is not there, `[#This Row]`, `INDIRECT` of
   `SUBSTITUTE`, `&` or R1C1 (`FALSE`), `OFFSET` — skips the rule and counts
   it (`source` for a list), never guessed.
5. **Values:** number rules need a number (`whole` an integer); text dates are
   not parsed; `textLength` uses the stored value's length; a list matches
   text ignoring case and a number by value. Blank cells pass with
   `allowBlank`. Only the used range (data plus changed cells) is checked.
   `showErrorMessage="0"` rules still check.
6. **Lifecycle (SR-GRID):** errors appear on load, re-check on every sheet
   after every change and after `derive`, resolve themselves when the cell
   passes and reopen (with `found` refreshed) when it fails again; they are
   read-only, drawn with a square ⚠ pin at the cell's right edge, filterable
   as "Workbook rules", named "Workbook rule".
7. **Skipped rules:** `skippedRules(book | store)` returns what was not
   checked and why (`custom`, `operand`, `operator`, `type`, `source`); the
   status line shows "n validation warnings · k rules not checked" (n counts
   the open ones in the review layers shown — W-51, SR-GRID 5d). It is not
   in `sheetpane-load`'s detail — the plugin contract has no way to add to a
   core event (B-032).
8. **List arrow:** in Edit, on cells a `list` rule covers — even past the data,
   the grid widens to the columns rules name — by mouse or Alt+↓; the choices
   are re-read live; a pick sets the cell (undoable). `showDropDown` (Excel's
   "hide the arrow") is read by the importer and not yet honoured.
9. **Dependent lists (W-60):** `INDIRECT(<cell>)` reads the cell (relative
   parts shifted from the rule's first cell) at each checked cell, live, and
   resolves its text to a defined name (case-insensitive, the rule sheet's
   own name before a global one), a table or table column (W-61) or an A1
   cell or range — always fixed; `INDIRECT("text")` resolves once. Text that
   names nothing (blank, a space, an unknown name) gives no list: the cell
   passes with `allowBlank` and fails without it, as Excel does, `expected`
   saying why (`list — (A7 "Flow Rate" names no list)`). Because `validate`
   re-runs on every sheet after every change (decision 6), a parent edit
   re-checks its children in the same edit: an orphaned child opens a
   warning, an open one follows the new list (SR-GRID decision 19b), and the
   arrow offers the new parent's choices. A number rule's `INDIRECT` operand
   reads the one cell its text names.
10. **The host's rules written as the workbook's own (W-58).** The export
    option `rulesAsValidation` — the Download menu's *Write rules as Excel
    dropdowns*, off unless `validation({ rulesAsValidation: true })`; shown
    only while the pane has a rules file or element `columns` (SR-GRID
    decision 17, `applies`), and then an untouched workbook is exported, not
    handed back — writes the rules the rules engine checks (the element's
    `columns` < the file's `"*"` < the named sheet, by title, from
    `store.columnRules` through the grid's `checkDocument`) into each `.xlsx`
    sheet's `<dataValidations>` (`setDataValidations`, SR-EXPORT decision 3).
    One rule → one Excel rule (`validationOf`); a column rule covers its
    column from the row under `headerRow` to row 1,048,576, a cell rule its
    cell or range. Every Excel rule gets `errorTitle` / `promptTitle` (the
    column title or cell, cut to 32), `error` (the rule's `message`, else the
    rule in words, cut to 255), `prompt` (the rule in words) and `errorStyle`
    (`onInvalid: 'block'` → `stop`; severity `note` → `information`; else
    `warning`). `required` (and `equals`) clear `allowBlank`.

    | rules-file words | Excel rule | not written (listed) |
    |---|---|---|
    | `oneOf`, `equals` | `list`, typed out: `"Active,Inactive"` (booleans `TRUE` / `FALSE`) | a value with a comma, an empty list, over 255 characters — SP-5403 |
    | `type: 'integer'` / `'number'`, or `min` / `max` alone | `whole` / `decimal`: `between`, `≥`, `≤`; no bound: ±9.99E+307 | a bound that is not a number, `min` above `max` — SP-5404 |
    | `type: 'date'` with `min` / `max` | `date`, `DATE(y,m,d)` or a serial; no bound: 1900-01-01 to 9999-12-31 | a bound not `2026-01-31` or a serial — SP-5404 |
    | `minLength` / `maxLength` | `textLength` | not whole numbers from 0, `minLength` above `maxLength` — SP-5404 |
    | `type: 'boolean'` | `list` `"TRUE,FALSE"` | |
    | `required` alone | `textLength ≥ 1`, blank not allowed | |
    | `type: 'text'`, `message`, `note`, `severity`, `onInvalid` | no rule of their own (the text and style above) | |
    | `pattern`, `noneOf`, `unique` | — | always — SP-5401 |
    | two checks (a list with a bound or length; a number or date with a length; `equals` with `oneOf`; list values outside the `type`) | — | always — SP-5402 |
    | a title no sheet has, a sheet the workbook lacks | — | SP-5405 |

    **Merging (one rule per cell in Excel):** the workbook's own rules —
    classic and `x14` — keep their cells; a written rule leaves them (a
    conflict, SP-5406) unless it checks the same thing (type, operator,
    operands, `allowBlank`), when its cells join the workbook's rule instead
    of a second copy (`merged`). A cell rule wins over a column rule and a
    named sheet's over `"*"`'s, the same way. `x14` rules stay in `<extLst>`
    (`mainBlockCount`), never copied into the main block. A sheet whose own
    rules export refuses (SP-2015) keeps its block and none are written to it
    (SP-5407). Each rule not written and each conflict is one console warning
    with its code; `lastRulesWrite(book)` → `{ written, merged, skipped,
    conflicts }`, and the status line adds "k rules not written to Excel"
    (not in `sheetpane-export`'s detail — B-032). `rulesAsValidations(store)`
    gives the plan without writing. `.xlsx` only: a CSV, or a CSV converted
    to `.xlsx`, carries no rules.

    **Parity:** export the fixtures' rules sample (`showcase.xlsx` +
    `showcase.rules.json`) with the rules, open the file again with this
    plugin alone, and it flags exactly the cells the rules engine flags
    except under rules not written. Known differences beyond the skipped
    rules: whitespace-only text is blank to the rules engine but text to
    Excel; text that reads as a number or a date passes the rules engine's
    `number` / `date` but not Excel's; `minLength` counts the shown text,
    Excel the stored value.
11. **With no page (W-54):** `@sheetpane/validation/check` serves the plugin
    from `src/plugin.ts` — `validation`, `validateSheet`, `skippedRules`,
    `lastReport`, `listRuleAt` and the evaluator (`rulesOf`, `ruleWords`,
    `listOptions`, `parseOperand`) — registering nothing and importing only
    `@sheetpane/grid/check` (SR-GRID decision 22f), and `check(bytes, options
    & { severity })`: the grid's `check()` with `validation({ severity })`
    added (an id `"validation"` in `plugins` means the same plugin). The main
    entry re-exports the same module and registers its own `validation()`:
    that one adds decision 10's export switch (`exportPatch`,
    `exportOptions`, `src/write.ts`, which reads the rules file through
    `@sheetpane/grid`), so `/check`'s plugin checks and never writes. The
    one-rule `check(rule, store, row, col)` stays on the main entry only, so
    `check` names one thing per entry.

### Consequences

- **W-52 (2026-10-19):** rows and columns inserted or deleted move
  `dataValidations` in the workbook the plugin reads (SR-IMPORT decision 14);
  `structure.test.ts` checks a rule and its error follow their cells — no
  code here changed.
- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg validation` — 59 tests (every type and
  operator, list sources (a table column by structured reference, W-61), dependent
  `INDIRECT` lists — names per parameter, sheet-scoped first, tables, A1 text, a parent
  that names nothing, the skipped forms, a parent edit and undo, the arrow following
  the parent, `@sheetpane/fixtures`' `dependent-lists.xlsx` (W-60) — x14, relative operands, live limits, resolve /
  reopen / undo, the arrow and its menu, the shared error pane with the
  author filter, a `custom` rule evaluated by IronCalc through
  `@sheetpane/formulas`; W-58's `write.test.ts`: the mapping table row by row,
  placing and merging, `x14` left alone, SP-5407, the option, the console and
  status line, the Download menu, and parity on the showcase), plus SR-GRID's
  core tests for read-only rows, the ⚠ pin and cross-sheet re-validation.
- **Owed:** a fixture with every rule type saved by Excel — W-30; a file
  written with the rules opened in Excel and LibreOffice, the dropdowns and
  checks working, no repair prompt — W-30 DoD 3 (W-58 DoD 3).

### Alternatives considered

- A formula engine of its own for operands — rejected: it would duplicate W-16.
- Flagging blanks under whole-column rules — rejected: a million rows.
- Severity from Excel's `errorStyle` — rejected: the spec fixes `warning`; the
  host chooses.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/validation/src/`](../packages/validation/src/) · [`packages/validation/test/`](../packages/validation/test/)
- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) — `validate`.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a cell that breaks a supported rule is not
listed, or a listed workbook error stays open after the cell passes; or a
rules-file rule the table writes is missing from the download, a written
rule takes cells from the workbook's own, or the re-opened showcase flags a
cell the rules engine does not (or misses one it does) under a written rule.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg validation`

<!-- source: records/0109_NUMFMT.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0109_NUMFMT.md) -->

# SR-NUMFMT — @sheetpane/numfmt

## §1 — For humans

**Numbers look the way Excel shows them.** Without this plugin the grid
formats dates, percentages and fixed decimals and shows anything else as
stored. With it, every format a workbook uses — currency, accounting,
fractions, elapsed time, conditional sections, locales — renders as in Excel.

**And a reviewer can change one.** In Edit a dropdown and ± decimals set a
cell's format; the change is held in memory like any other, undoable, and
export writes it into the file.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C["a numeric cell + its format code"] --> F["numfmt(): format hook → numfmt 4.0.1"]
    F -->|text| G["the grid"]
    F -->|library rejects the code| S["core subset (fallback, counted)"]
    U["ui(): dropdown · ± decimals"] -->|numFmt change| X["exportPatch: <numFmt> + <xf>, cells repointed"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   numeric cell + code --> numfmt(): format --> numfmt 4.0.1 --> text in the grid
                                         \--> rejected code: the core subset (counted)
   ui(): dropdown, ± decimals --> numFmt change --> exportPatch: <numFmt> + <xf>, cells repointed
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-15 asked for the full ECMA-376 format grammar through the
[`numfmt`](https://github.com/borgar/numfmt) library (MIT, zero
dependencies), replacing the core subset (SR-IMPORT decision 4) when
installed — the plugins verdict's `format` hook.

### Decision

1. **`numfmt(options?)`** → `{ id: 'numfmt', provides: ['format',
   'decorate', 'exportPatch'] }`; `ui()` (`numfmt-ui`) carries the controls.
   Importing `@sheetpane/numfmt` registers `numfmt` alone; `@sheetpane/numfmt/ui`
   registers `[numfmt(), ui()]`. The headless entry never imports the UI.
   Runtime: the peer `@sheetpane/grid` and `numfmt@4.0.1`, pinned.
2. **The code** for a cell is the user's `numFmt` change, else its
   `cellXfs[s].numFmtId` — the file's `<numFmts>` entry first, else the
   library's built-in for that id in the locale (so ids 5–8, 14–22, 41–44
   follow it, as in Excel).
3. **Output:** finite numbers only; out-of-range dates show `########`;
   `General` follows Excel's 11-character rule.
4. **1904:** a code that shows a year, month or day gets the serial shifted by
   1,462 days; elapsed `[h]` formats are not shifted.
5. **Locale:** `options.locale`, else `document.documentElement.lang` read
   when formatting (guarded for Node); `-IN` territories group `3,2`.
6. **Fallback:** a code the library rejects returns nothing, so the core
   subset shows the cell; the cell is counted in `plugin.fallbacks()`. The
   count is not in `sheetpane-load`'s detail (backlog B-032).
7. **`decorate`** only sets `white-space: pre` for codes with `_`, `*` or `?`
   padding — never a font.
8. **UI:** a `format-row` dropdown (General · Number · Currency · Accounting ·
   Date · Time · Percentage · Fraction · Scientific · Text · Custom…) and ±
   decimals; a choice applies to the selection's numeric cells as **one undo
   step** (`setChanges`), each a `numFmt` change whose `was` is the file's own
   code; Custom… asks for a code (`ui({ ask })`, default `prompt`) and
   refuses an invalid one. The change lives in the cell's `numFmt` slot
   (`sheet!#numFmt:A1`, SR-GRID decision 3), so a value edit and a format on
   one cell are two changes. The cell bar keeps showing the raw value.
9. **Export:** `exportPatch` appends deduplicated `<numFmt>` (new ids from
   max(163, existing) + 1; a built-in code uses its id) and `<xf>` entries — a
   copy of the cell's old xf with the new `numFmtId` — and repoints each
   changed cell's `s`, inserting a missing `<c>` or `<row>`.

### Consequences

- **Codes (W-40, SR-CODES):** SP-5101 (a selection too large to format, a warning), SP-5102 / SP-5103 (no usable style sheet on export).
- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg numfmt` — 42 tests (every built-in id
  and 50 custom codes through load → text; 1904; fallback; locales `de-DE`,
  `en-IN`; the dropdown, ranges, ± decimals, Custom…; export and read-back;
  package shape and the headless boundary). The table also found five bugs
  in the core subset; two are fixed (month-only codes, serial 0) and three
  are recorded as limits in SR-IMPORT.
- **Owed:** expected values captured from Excel itself (the table follows
  Excel's documented output) — W-30.
- **The reading verdict's "1 in 100" trigger** compares misreads; the one
  fixture cell where the subset and the library differ (`[$€-407]#,##0.00`)
  is a code the subset declines and shows raw, not a misread.

### Alternatives considered

- `addLocale` for `en-IN` — rejected: global state shared by every pane.
- A copy of the core subset for fallback — rejected: returning nothing reuses
  the core's.
- `[Red]` colours through `decorate` — left for a follow-up (dark-theme
  contrast, W-29).

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/numfmt/src/`](../packages/numfmt/src/) · [`packages/numfmt/test/`](../packages/numfmt/test/)
- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) — the `format` hook.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** the library misformats more than 1 in 100
numeric cells across the real-app fixtures (W-30), or a code Excel accepts is
refused.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg numfmt`

**Code**

- [`packages/numfmt/src/index.ts`](../packages/numfmt/src/index.ts) · [`fmt.ts`](../packages/numfmt/src/fmt.ts) · [`patch.ts`](../packages/numfmt/src/patch.ts) · [`ui.ts`](../packages/numfmt/src/ui.ts)

**Project docs**

- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) · [`work/reference/design/boards/Plugin-Numfmt.dc.html`](../work/reference/design/boards/Plugin-Numfmt.dc.html)

<!-- source: records/0110_STYLES.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0110_STYLES.md) -->

# SR-STYLES — @sheetpane/styles

## §1 — For humans

**Cells look the way the file formats them.** Without this plugin the grid
draws every cell plain. With it, fills, bold, italic, underline, colours,
sizes, borders and alignment show as saved — in the host's own font, always.

**And a reviewer can restyle them.** In Edit a format row (and Bold · Fill ·
Merge on the selection bar) restyles the selection; each action is one change
per cell, one undo step, and export writes it into the file.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    X["cellXfs[s] → fonts · fills · borders · alignment"] --> D["styles(): decorate → allow-listed CSS"]
    C["the reviewer's style change (sheet!#style:A1)"] --> D
    D --> G["the grid (file colours kept in both themes)"]
    U["ui(): format row · selbar"] -->|style change, one undo step| C
    C --> E["exportPatch: <font>/<fill>/<border>/<xf> appended, s repointed"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   cellXfs[s] (fonts, fills, borders, alignment) --> styles(): decorate --> allow-listed CSS --> grid
   reviewer's style change (sheet!#style:A1)      --/
   ui(): format row, selbar --style change, one undo step--> change map
   change map --> exportPatch: <font>/<fill>/<border>/<xf> appended, cells' s repointed
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-17 asked for the styles plugin on the plugins verdict's `decorate` hook,
with the format row the Plugin-Styles board draws. Merges are core (SR-GRID);
the number format is SR-NUMFMT's.

### Decision

1. **`styles({ fileStyles? })`** → `{ id: 'styles', provides: ['decorate',
   'exportPatch'], after: ['tables'] }` — a cell's own format draws over its
   Excel table's style (SR-TABLES decision 4); `ui(options?)` (`styles-ui`) carries the controls.
   Importing `@sheetpane/styles` registers `styles` alone;
   `@sheetpane/styles/ui` registers `[styles(), ui()]`. The headless entry
   never imports the UI. No runtime dependency; `@sheetpane/grid` is a peer.
2. **`decorate`** reads `cellXfs[s]` → `fonts`, `fills`, `borders`,
   `alignment` and returns only `background-color`, `color`, `font-weight`,
   `font-style`, `font-size`, `text-decoration`, `text-align`,
   `vertical-align`, `white-space` and `border-top/right/bottom/left` —
   **never `font-family`** (the host refuses one, SR-GRID 17). Colours: ARGB,
   theme with Excel's tint (the file's theme, else Office's), indexed (the
   file's `<indexedColors>`, else the 64-colour default), `auto`.
3. **The default font's size and colour are the host's:** only a size or
   colour that differs from the workbook's default font is drawn (size as
   `sz / default` of the grid's size), so a plain cell stays plain in both
   themes. A filled cell with automatic text gets the workbook's default ink.
   Patterns blend by density; a gradient shows its midpoint; diagonal
   borders, indent and rotation are not drawn.
4. **File colours are data** (SR-GRID 15a): they render as saved in light and
   dark; the grid's state tints sit above them (SR-GRID 15b).
5. **The change** is kind `style` in the cell's style slot
   (`sheet!#style:A1`, SR-GRID 3); `now` is a `StylePatch` (`clear`, `b`,
   `i`, `u`, `strike`, `color`, `fill`, `border`, `align`, `valign`,
   `wrap`). Fields the file already shows are dropped; a cell back to its file
   look has no change; `clear` drops the file's font, fill, border and
   alignment and keeps the number format.
6. **UI:** `format-row` groups text (Bold `Mod+B`, Italic `Mod+I`, Underline
   `Mod+U`, Strikethrough `Mod+5`) · colour · fill · border · align (left,
   centre, right with `Mod+Shift+L/E/R`; top, middle, bottom; Merge/Unmerge)
   · wrap · clear (`Mod+\`); `selbar` (docked in the cell bar and in the right-click menu, SR-GRID 13) adds Bold, Fill and Merge/Unmerge. Every
   action restyles the selection as **one undo step** (`setChanges`). Merge
   calls the core's `setMerge` (kind `merge`), is labelled Merge or Unmerge,
   and is disabled on a CSV or a single unmerged cell. `ui({ colours, fills,
   highlight })` sets the swatches; the default fills keep the changed mark at
   3:1.
7. **Export:** `exportPatch` appends deduplicated `<font>`, `<fill>`,
   `<border>` and `<xf>` entries (counts updated, every other byte kept),
   repoints `s` on each changed cell (adding `<c r s/>` and `<row>` where
   missing), and creates `styles.xml` with its relationship and content type
   when the package has none. Untouched cells keep their `s`; a workbook
   without style changes is left byte for byte. A CSV is never restyled.
8. **For condfmt (W-19):** the colour and CSS helpers (`resolveColor`,
   `applyTint`, `paletteOf`, `fontCss`, `fillCss` with `{ dxf: true }`,
   `borderCss`, `alignmentCss`, `dxfCss`, `ALLOWED_PROPS`, `allowListed`)
   are exported.
9. **Rich text (W-53):** `decorateRuns` (on the `decorate` hook, SR-GRID
   decision 17) draws a rich-text cell's runs (`cell.runs`, SR-IMPORT
   decision 12) as pieces: a run with no formatting takes the cell's look; a
   formatted run states `font-weight` (700 / 400), `font-style` (italic /
   normal) and `text-decoration` (or `none`) outright — an Excel run's
   `<rPr>` is its whole font — and its size (`em` of the cell's own font's
   size) and colour only where they differ from the cell's own font (a cell
   font with no colour is measured against the default font, so default ink
   stays the host's); superscript and subscript are `vertical-align: super` /
   `sub` at 0.75 of the size. Never a font family; allow-listed like
   `decorate`. `fileStyles: false` draws runs plain. Exported:
   `decorateRuns`, `runCss`. A restyle keeps the runs (only the cell's `s`
   changes); a value edit drops them (plain text, SR-GRID). Nothing in
   `exportPatch` touches `sharedStrings.xml`.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg styles` — 56 tests (colours: rgb, theme
  and tint, indexed; decorate from the ExcelJS fixture property by property
  and from hand-made `styles.xml` for every border style, alignment, font and
  fill; the allow-list and the L5 veto over the package; the format row in
  View and Edit, every group, shortcuts, one undo step; merges; the core
  layout showing alignment and wrap with tints above a fill; contrast of the
  changed mark on every default fill; export round-trips, dedup, missing
  `styles.xml`, byte-for-byte when untouched). `runs.test.ts` (W-53, 10):
  every run property against the cell's own font, superscript, the
  allow-list and no family, `fileStyles: false`, the spans drawn, and export —
  an edited rich cell written as a plain inline string while the shared
  strings and every untouched rich cell stay byte for byte, a restyle
  keeping the runs.
- **Owed:** a fixture of every fill, font and border combination **saved by
  Excel**, and a rich-text cell saved by Excel — W-30.

### Alternatives considered

- One change per cell for value and style — replaced by per-kind slots
  (SR-GRID 3): a value edit and a restyle of one cell are two changes.
- Drawing the default font's size and colour — rejected: a dark host would
  get dark-on-dark text in every plain cell.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/styles/src/`](../packages/styles/src/) · [`packages/styles/test/`](../packages/styles/test/)
- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) — the `decorate` hook

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a cell in a real-app fixture (W-30) renders a
fill, font or border property differently from Excel, or any decorate result
names a font family.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg styles`

<!-- source: records/0111_FORMULAS.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0111_FORMULAS.md) -->

# SR-FORMULAS — @sheetpane/formulas

## §1 — For humans

**Edit a number, and the totals follow.** Without this plugin a formula cell
shows the value Excel saved, marked stale once its inputs change. With it,
IronCalc recalculates every formula that depends on the edit; those cells are
marked ⟳ and are never counted as the reviewer's changes.

**A reviewer can type a formula.** In Edit the cell bar holds the cell's
formula; typing `=` makes a formula change that evaluates at once and is
written into the file with its new value.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S["the store (changes + file)"] -->|derive: load / change| F["formulas(): IronCalc model (a cache)"]
    F -->|cells whose value changed| D["derived (⟳, not changes)"]
    D --> G["the grid · validation · status"]
    F -->|exportPatch| X["<f> + new <v>, fullCalcOnLoad=1"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   store (changes + file) --derive--> formulas(): IronCalc model (a cache)
   model --cells whose value changed--> derived (marked, never changes) --> grid, validation, status
   model --exportPatch--> <f> + new <v>, fullCalcOnLoad="1"
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-16 asked for recalculation on the plugins verdict's single-provider
`derive` hook, with IronCalc (MIT/Apache-2.0) as the engine.

### Decision

1. **`formulas({ preload?, wasm? })`** → `{ id: 'formulas', provides:
   ['derive', 'exportPatch'] }` plus `ready()`, `cycles()`, `unsupported()`,
   `stateOf()`, `built()`; `ui(engine?)` (`formulas-ui`) carries the overlay
   and the controls. Importing `@sheetpane/formulas` registers `formulas`;
   `@sheetpane/formulas/ui` registers `[formulas(), ui()]`. Runtime: the peer
   `@sheetpane/grid` and `@ironcalc/wasm@0.9.0`, pinned.
2. **Lazy:** IronCalc is loaded by a dynamic `import()` on the first `derive`
   with a formula to calculate — a workbook with none never loads it until one
   is typed; `preload: true` warms it; `wasm` names its bytes or URL (Node).
   A failed load is retried on the next call.
3. **L9 — the model is a cache:** each cell's input is read from the store
   (a change, else the file's formula, else its value); the model is rebuilt
   when the workbook object changes; only computed values are read back.
   Only reachable cells are loaded (formulas, the ranges they and defined names
   reference); `INDIRECT` or `OFFSET` loads everything; a new formula loads
   its ranges when typed. `_xlfn.`, `_xlws.`, `_xlpm.` prefixes are stripped
   for the engine.
4. **Derive:** on load, only cells whose computed value differs from the
   saved one; on a change, every formula whose value changed and every typed
   formula. A file formula back at its saved value, and a typed formula
   reverted away, return `clear: true` (SR-GRID 21b), so ⟳ and export mean
   "recalculated". Calls queue; calls behind a running recalculation share one
   evaluation. Numbers compare at a 1e-14 relative tolerance; `null` equals
   `''`. Values are read at 15 significant digits. On `restructure` (rows or
   columns inserted or deleted, W-52) the model is rebuilt from the moved
   workbook, as on a load — its formulas, and typed ones in the change map,
   already point where Excel would point them, `#REF!` for a deleted cell —
   and the whole derived set is returned.
5. **Errors:** `#DIV/0!`, `#REF!`, `#N/A` are values; a half-typed formula
   never throws (it shows IronCalc's `#ERROR!`). A cycle shows 0, as Excel
   does, is listed by `cycles()`, marked ↻ and named in the status line. A
   file formula IronCalc cannot calculate (`#NAME?`, `#SPILL!` or an engine
   error where Excel saved something else) keeps its saved value, is marked ≈
   and listed by `unsupported()` until it becomes computable.
6. **Export:** typed formulas become `<f>` + `<v>` (`t="e"`, `"str"`, `"b"`
   as needed); recalculated file formulas get a new `<v>` with their `<f>`
   (shared formulas included) kept; `fullCalcOnLoad="1"`. An untouched
   workbook's parts are byte-identical.
7. **UI:** `cellbar` — in View, `fx =…` as read-only text; in Edit the grid's
   own input holds the formula (SR-GRID 21b); `status` — Sum · Avg · Count of
   the selection, `⟳ N cells recalculated`, circular references; `cell`
   marks ⟳ (recalculated), ↻ (cycle), ≈ (unsupported); `overlay` — coloured,
   labelled outlines of the referenced ranges while a formula is edited
   (drawn as four edges, so cells stay clickable). A hidden formula on a
   protected sheet (W-62, SR-GRID 21e — `formulaHiddenIn`) shows no `fx` and
   no outlines; its value only.
8. **`evaluate(formula, { sheet, ref })`** returns one formula's value
   synchronously, through a scratch cell (the sheet's last cell) set,
   evaluated, read and cleared — the workbook is never touched. It serves
   `@sheetpane/validation`'s `custom` rules (SR-VALIDATION decision 3); a
   workbook with a `custom` validation rule, or a conditional-format
   expression, formula operand or formula threshold (W-19), builds the model
   even without a formula cell.
   `undefined` until the model is built or while a recalculation is queued.

### Consequences

- **Codes (W-40, SR-CODES):** a failed recalculation is logged as SP-5201, an engine that did not load as SP-5202.
- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg formulas` — 34 tests (derive on load
  and change, undo, revert, paste, cross-sheet and quoted names, defined
  names, CSV, cycles, errors, unsupported; export of typed and recalculated
  formulas and read-back; the cell bar, status and marks in a real
  `<sheetpane-excel>`; lazy load — no `.wasm` request before the first
  formula; preload; the parity and perf runs), plus SR-VALIDATION's
  `custom`-rule test through `evaluate()`.
- **Measured** (Arpit's MacBook, headless Chromium 156, 10 cores, under
  load from sibling agents): 250,000 rows with 10,000 formulas — the plugin
  adds about 0.4 s to a 6.1 s read (lightest run), one edit 40–48 ms; the
  `.wasm` loads in 34 ms. Parity: 3/3 formula cells of the W-13 fixtures,
  113/116 in a hand-written function probe (misses: `AGGREGATE`, `XLOOKUP`
  over array constants, `TEXTJOIN` with an empty literal — the test fails if
  the list changes).
- **Owed:** parity against **Excel-saved** fixtures (W-30, DoD 7's ≥ 99 %);
  perf on the reference machine against an `.xlsx` budget; reporting a cycle
  in `sheetpane-load`/`-change` detail (backlog B-032; today the status line
  and `cycles()`); 1904-date workbooks (IronCalc knows only 1900 — date
  functions over serials are off by 1,462 days); array and spilled formulas
  fall back to unsupported (the reader does not expose `t="array"`).
- The A1 and XML helpers duplicate `@sheetpane/export`'s small ones, to keep
  the grid the only peer.

### Alternatives considered

- Loading every non-empty cell — rejected: 2.6 s for 1.25 M cells and every
  evaluation slower.
- Reading values through IronCalc's General format — rejected: ~10
  significant digits.
- Returning every formula cell on load — rejected: ⟳ would mark every
  formula.
- An editable `fx` button in the cell bar — replaced by the grid's own input
  holding the formula (one place to edit a cell).

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/formulas/src/`](../packages/formulas/src/) · [`packages/formulas/test/`](../packages/formulas/test/)
- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md) — the `derive` hook

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** IronCalc's value differs from Excel's cached
value in more than 1 in 100 formula cells across the real-app fixtures
(W-30), or a workbook without formulas requests the `.wasm`.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg formulas`

- [`packages/formulas/src/index.ts`](../packages/formulas/src/index.ts) · [`model.ts`](../packages/formulas/src/model.ts) · [`cells.ts`](../packages/formulas/src/cells.ts) · [`export.ts`](../packages/formulas/src/export.ts) · [`ui.ts`](../packages/formulas/src/ui.ts)

<!-- source: records/0112_COMMENTS.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0112_COMMENTS.md) -->

# SR-COMMENTS — @sheetpane/comments

## §1 — For humans

**What colleagues wrote in Excel shows in the review.** A cell's note or
comment thread arrives in the error list as a *File comment* — read-only,
filterable, shown at its cell.

**And the review goes back into the file.** On export, every error becomes an
Excel comment thread at its cell — the message, then *Should be* as a reply,
marked done when resolved — so someone without sheetpane reads the review in
Excel. On by default; the host can switch it off (the decider, 2026-10-18).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    F["file: threadedComments · comments (notes) · persons"] -->|validate| E["errors author 'file' — read-only"]
    R["the review's errors"] -->|exportPatch| W["threadedCommentN · commentsN · vmlDrawingN · persons, rels, content types"]
    O["comments({ write:false }) / export({ comments:false })"] -.->|off| W
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   file: threaded comments, notes, persons --validate--> errors (author 'file', read-only)
   review's errors --exportPatch--> threadedCommentN, commentsN, vmlDrawingN, persons + rels, content types
   comments({ write: false }) or export({ comments: false }) --> nothing written
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-22 asked for comments both ways; the decider ruled writing on by default
with a host switch (2026-10-18). The error schema and the read-only rule for
`file` errors are SR-GRID's (decision 19b).

### Decision

1. **`comments({ write? })`** → `{ id: 'comments', provides: ['validate',
   'exportPatch'] }` and a read-only `lastExport: { written, skipped }`.
   Importing the package registers `comments`. No `./ui`; no runtime
   dependency; `@sheetpane/grid` is the only peer. String XML only — no
   `DOMParser`, no `document` — so it runs in Node.
2. **Read:** one draft per commented cell, `{ type: 'comment', severity:
   'note', author: 'file', found: <uploaded text or (blank)>, expected: '',
   message, status: 'open' }`. The message is the thread's first comment,
   its replies in file order, then the cell's note, each line led by
   `Name: ` (not twice). Excel's `tc=` placeholder notes are skipped; thread
   entries this review wrote are skipped.
3. **Write:** every error not authored `file` in the layers shown
   (`snapshot.visibleErrors`, W-51, SR-GRID 5d) but `@sheetpane/compare`'s
   `compare` layer — a comparison is not the review (W-63, SR-COMPARE 12) —
   or, with
   `export({ layers: [...] })` (`ctx.exportOptions.layers`), in the layers
   named, whatever is shown; `[]` writes nothing — at the top-left cell of its
   range — except results (`pass`, `skipped`; SR-GRID decision 23), which
   are written only when `ctx.exportOptions.includeResults === true`
   (`<sheetpane-excel>.export({ includeResults: true })`; W-50), so a
   downloaded review stays a list of problems; there is no Download-menu
   switch for it — the host asks. An error with no cell, about a whole sheet or the workbook (W-55,
   SR-GRID 5a), is not written, because a comment needs a cell and sheetpane
   never puts one on A1. It is reported in `lastExport.skipped` as `{ id,
   reason: 'no-cell', code: 'SP-5804' }`. `@sheetpane/review` (SR-REVIEW) is
   where these errors go into the file: listed on its Review sheet. First comment `<id> · <Severity> · <Type name> · Found: <found>` (`Passed`, `Not checked` for results),
   newline, the message; `expected` as a reply `Should be: <expected>`. All
   errors on one cell share one thread, `done="1"` only when every one is
   resolved or accepted. **An accepted error (W-69, SR-GRID 5c)** gets one
   more reply, `Accepted: <reason>`, written by who accepted it (`acceptedBy`,
   else the error's author) at `acceptedAt`; reopened, the next export drops
   it. On a cell with someone's thread the errors join it as replies; on
   a cell holding a legacy note nothing is written and the error is reported
   `note-at-cell` in `lastExport.skipped` (the file author's note is never
   rewritten).
4. **Parts:** `xl/threadedComments/threadedCommentN.xml`, `xl/commentsN.xml`
   (author `tc={root}`, the placeholder text), `xl/drawings/vmlDrawingN.vml`
   (one hidden Note shape per cell, a free `o:idmap` block),
   `<legacyDrawing>` in schema position, `xl/persons/person.xml` (one person
   per author, `providerId="None"`); every rel and content type. Existing
   parts are **extended, never replaced**; a sheet whose parts cannot be
   parsed is left as is (`unreadable-part`).
5. **Ids:** a thread entry's id is the version-5 UUID of
   `sheetpane:<id>:<createdAt>` (`…#expected` and `…#accepted` for the
   replies); a person's, of
   `sheetpane-person:<name>`. A second export of the same review replaces its
   own entries in place; replies added in Excel are kept and re-pointed.
6. **Switches:** `write: false` for good; `ctx.exportOptions.comments ===
   false` (`<sheetpane-excel>.export({ comments: false })`, SR-GRID decision
   6) for one export — then the parts are byte-identical to the input. The
   plugin declares `exportOptions: [{ key: 'comments', label: 'Write review
   as Excel comments', default: true }]`, so the Download menu shows the
   switch (W-34; none when `write: false`).
7. **No font** is written: the legacy `<t>` is plain and the VML names none.

### Consequences

- **Codes (W-40, SR-CODES):** SP-5801 (a comment part with no container), SP-5802 (not a worksheet), SP-5803 (comments not written for a sheet), SP-5804 (an error with no cell not written — W-55).
- **W-52 (2026-10-19):** notes and threads move with their cells in the
  workbook the plugin reads (SR-IMPORT decision 14), and their `file` errors
  keep their ids; a deleted row's note is resolved "row deleted". The file's
  parts are moved by `patchXlsx` before this plugin extends them.
  `structure.test.ts` checks it — no code here changed.
- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg comments` — 34 tests (results left out unless `includeResults`, W-50; the layers written, W-51; the `compare` layer only when named, W-63; notes and threads
  from the ExcelJS fixture and hand-written packages; read-only rows,
  author filter; the four parts, rels, content types and `legacyDrawing`
  order; extending existing parts; joining a thread; the note-at-cell and no-cell (W-55) skips;
  an error's `meta` (W-68, SR-GRID 5b) found in no written part;
  an accepted error's *Accepted* reply, its person and time, the thread
  done, the reply dropped once reopened and skipped when read back (W-69);
  both switches byte-identical; W-51: the layers shown by default, a named
  set by option, none for `[]`, and every layer's threads skipped when read
  back; export → reload → `setErrors` → export
  giving the same ids and counts; every written part well-formed; package
  shape and the Node-safe boundary).
- **Owed:** opening the exported fixture in Excel 365, Excel 2019 and
  LibreOffice (DoD 4; an accepted error's reply included — W-69) and fixtures saved by Excel with notes, threads and
  both — W-30, the decider's; validating the parts against the OOXML schema
  (backlog B-033). Unverified until then: whether Excel links the note to its
  thread by the `tc=` author alone (no `xr:uid` is written), the `dT` format
  (UTC, hundredths, no `Z`) and the computed VML anchors.
- Author names land in the file as personal data.
- The type name comes from `DEFAULT_ERROR_TYPES` and `BUILTIN_TYPE_NAMES`;
  a host's own `errorTypes` (on the element, not the store) are written by id.
- A plugin cannot report export warnings to the host's events; `lastExport`
  stands in (backlog B-032).

### Alternatives considered

- Reading `done` threads as `resolved` — kept `open`, as the DoD says; a
  ruling may change it.
- Converting a note to a thread, or appending to it, for an error on a note
  cell — rejected: it rewrites the file author's content.
- An id from `id` alone — rejected: ids restart at ERR-0001 each session.
- `crypto.subtle` for the UUID hash — rejected: `validate` is synchronous.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/comments/src/`](../packages/comments/src/) · [`packages/comments/test/`](../packages/comments/test/)
- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** Excel or LibreOffice reports a repair, or drops
a comment, on a file this plugin wrote (W-30).

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg comments`

is never listed here.*

**Records** — [SR-GRID](0105_GRID.md) · [SR-ERRORS](0106_ERRORS.md) · [SR-LAW-5](0007_LAW-5-host-font.md) · [SR-LAW-6](0008_LAW-6-edits-in-memory-export-with-changes.md)

**Code**

- [`packages/comments/src/index.ts`](../packages/comments/src/index.ts) · [`read.ts`](../packages/comments/src/read.ts) · [`write.ts`](../packages/comments/src/write.ts) · [`xml.ts`](../packages/comments/src/xml.ts) · [`guid.ts`](../packages/comments/src/guid.ts)

**Project docs**

- [`work/compare/plugins.compare.md`](../work/compare/plugins.compare.md)

<!-- source: records/0113_CHARTS.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0113_CHARTS.md) -->

# SR-CHARTS — @sheetpane/charts

## §1 — For humans

**A chart shows where Excel puts it.** Each chart in the workbook appears at
its cells: a frame naming its title, its type and its series, with **Show
source cells** to select the data it plots. The common types — bar, column,
line, pie, doughnut, scatter — are drawn; the rest stay a frame that says why.

**And it says when the review changed its data.** Edit a plotted cell and the
chart shows *data changed — Excel will redraw*. With the formulas plugin the
drawing follows the live cells; the file's chart part is never rewritten.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P["drawingN.xml → c:chart → chartN.xml (read once, lazily)"] --> M["model: groups, series, refs, caches, colours"]
    M --> F["stage 1 frame: title · type · series · Show source cells"]
    M --> S["stage 2 SVG: bar · column · line · pie · doughnut · scatter"]
    C["store: changes / derived"] -->|tag, live values| S
    S --> O["overlay item at the anchor (scales with zoom)"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   drawingN.xml -> c:chart -> chartN.xml (read once, lazily) -> model (groups, series, refs, caches, colours)
   model -> stage 1 frame (title, type, series, Show source cells)
   model -> stage 2 SVG (bar, column, line, pie, doughnut, scatter) <- store changes / derived (tag, live values)
   SVG -> overlay item at the anchor, scaled with zoom
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-21 asked for charts on the plugins verdict's `overlay` hook, in two
stages, with no chart library (L2 rules one out as a dependency the reviewer
does not need). Anchors are SR-IMAGES' arithmetic.

### Decision

1. **`charts({ draw? })`** → `{ id: 'charts', provides: ['overlay'] }`;
   `draw: false` keeps every chart a frame. `ui()` (`charts-ui`) adds a
   `status` line naming the source under the selection (or "N charts") and
   the Mod+Shift+U shortcut for Show source cells. Importing
   `@sheetpane/charts` registers `charts`; `/ui` registers `[charts(),
   ui()]`. Peers: `@sheetpane/grid` and `@sheetpane/images` (`anchorRect`,
   `cellAt`); no runtime dependency.
2. **Items:** one per `kind: 'chart'` drawing with a chart part; the id
   carries a workbook generation; the rectangle is SR-IMAGES' anchor
   arithmetic in the grid's geometry. The item is a `group` (it holds a
   button) named by the title once the part is read, else the drawing's
   description or name; the drawing inside is `role="img"` with a `<title>`.
3. **Reading:** on first render through `book.part()`, once per workbook,
   cached; DOMParser by local name. A missing or malformed part gives a
   labelled frame. Title: rich text, else the title reference's cache, else
   the only series' name, else "Chart". Type label from the plot-area
   element, `barDir` and `grouping` ("column + line" for a combination).
4. **Show source cells** selects the union of the plotted ranges when they
   tile one rectangle, else the first series' values (a selection is one
   rectangle — backlog B-034); across sheets; disabled when the data is
   literal.
5. **The tag** "data changed — Excel will redraw" shows while a `value` or
   `formula` change lies in a range the chart reads (names, categories,
   values), drawn in the SVG's title band so it scales with zoom.
6. **Stage 2** draws exactly one group of bar, column (clustered, stacked,
   100 %), line, pie, doughnut or scatter that is not a pivot chart; area,
   radar, 3-D, combination and pivot charts stay frames saying why. Values:
   the cached points, or the live cells (`store.value`) when a `derive`
   plugin is installed (`data-values` says which). Own SVG: a `viewBox` the
   anchor's size, no font named, every file string escaped, colours checked
   as `#RRGGBB`; nice ticks (1, 2, 2.5, 5 × 10ⁿ); pies from 12 o'clock plus
   `firstSliceAng`, clockwise.
7. **Colours:** explicit `solidFill` (srgb, scheme, sys with
   lumMod/lumOff/tint/shade), else the theme's accents by `c:idx`, else
   Office's. File colours are data: the same in both themes (SR-GRID 15a).
8. **Export:** nothing — patch mode copies the chart parts byte for byte;
   when rows or columns were inserted or deleted, the core moves their
   series references (SR-EXPORT decision 11). In the page, the moved
   workbook's `book.part()` serves the chart part moved (SR-IMPORT decision
   11), so the frame follows its anchor and the series read the moved
   ranges with no code here (W-52).
9. **Edit:** a click on the frame away from its button selects the cell
   under it.

### Consequences

- **Codes (W-40, SR-CODES):** a malformed chart part is logged as SP-5701, a part with no chart as SP-5702.
- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg charts` — 43 tests (the model of every
  type; frames at their anchors; Show source cells; the tag and undo; stage 2
  against the series' values — bar lengths proportional, line points linear,
  slice angles, scatter positions; colours; live values through a `derive`
  provider; zoom; the accessible names; the chart part byte-identical on
  export), and SR-GRID's geometry and overlay tests.
- **W-52:** `structure.test.ts` — an insert moves the anchor and the series
  ranges, a deleted values column leaves `#REF!` and no range, undo restores.
- **Owed:** fixtures with each type **saved by Excel** — W-30; a run with
  the real `@sheetpane/formulas` (the live path is the store's, tested with a
  generic `derive` provider).
- Not drawn: data labels, trendlines, axis titles, secondary, log and date
  axes. Placement uses the grid's 28 px rows (SR-IMAGES).
- Contract gaps — multi-area selection, `selbar` `appliesTo`, context for
  `text()`, a dispose signal — are backlog B-034.

### Alternatives considered

- A chart library — ruled out by L2 and the bundle a reviewer does not need.
- An HTML title band over a letterboxed SVG, or a CSS transform with a
  ResizeObserver — rejected: neither scales exactly with zoom.
- Selecting the bounding box of non-adjacent ranges — rejected: it selects
  cells the chart does not read.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/charts/src/`](../packages/charts/src/) · [`packages/charts/test/`](../packages/charts/test/)
- [SR-IMAGES](0107_IMAGES.md) — anchors

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a frame stops matching its anchor's cells, a
drawn mark disagrees with its series value, or a chart part changes on
export.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg charts`
