<!-- source: records/0114_CONDFMT.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0114_CONDFMT.md) -->

# SR-CONDFMT — @sheetpane/condfmt

## §1 — For humans

**Cells light up the way Excel lights them.** A workbook's conditional
formats — "over 1,000 in red", a colour scale, data bars, duplicates, top 10,
a formula rule — are drawn on the cells they cover, and change as the
reviewer edits. Nothing here writes a rule: it shows what the file says.

**Colour never speaks alone.** Hovering a coloured cell names the rule
("Conditional: greater than 1000 · F2:F5"); the status line counts the
file's rules and says how many are not shown.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    F["file: conditionalFormatting + dxfs"] --> R["rules, one priority order per sheet"]
    S["store: values, changes, derived"] --> E["evaluate (cached per snapshot, targeted drops)"]
    R --> E
    E -->|decorate, after styles| G["the grid: fill · colour · weight · bar"]
    X["formulas.evaluate()"] -.->|expression rules| E
    E --> U["ui(): hover legend · cell bar · status count"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   file: conditionalFormatting + dxfs --> rules (one priority order per sheet)
   store values, changes, derived ----> evaluate (cached per snapshot, targeted drops)
   formulas.evaluate() ...............> evaluate (expression rules)
   evaluate --decorate, after styles--> grid (fill, colour, weight, data bar)
   evaluate --> ui(): hover legend, cell bar, status count
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-19 asked for conditional formatting as a second `decorate` provider after
`@sheetpane/styles` (SR-STYLES), render only; expression rules through
`@sheetpane/formulas` (SR-FORMULAS decision 8).

### Decision

1. **`condfmt()`** → `{ id: 'condfmt', provides: ['decorate'], after:
   ['styles', 'tables'] }`: a rule's dxf overrides the static style and an
   Excel table's style (SR-TABLES) per property.
   `ui()` (`condfmt-ui`) adds the legend and the count. Importing
   `@sheetpane/condfmt` registers `condfmt`; `/ui` registers `[condfmt(),
   ui()]`. Peers: `@sheetpane/grid` and `@sheetpane/styles` (`dxfCss`,
   `allowListed`, colours); no runtime dependency.
2. **Rules drawn:** `cellIs` (all eight operators), `containsText`,
   `notContainsText`, `beginsWith`, `endsWith`, `containsBlanks`,
   `notContainsBlanks`, `containsErrors`, `notContainsErrors`,
   `duplicateValues`, `uniqueValues`, `top10` (top/bottom, percent, ties
   included; percent is floor(n·rank/100), at least 1), `aboveAverage`,
   `colorScale`, `dataBar`, `expression`. **Skipped and counted:** `iconSet`
   (needs glyphs), `timePeriod`, unknown or malformed rules.
3. **Comparison** follows Excel: numbers < text < logicals, text without
   case, a blank as 0 or empty text; duplicates count text without case and
   never blanks.
4. **Priority** is one order per sheet across every block (file order breaks
   ties); a higher rule wins each property it sets and a lower one fills the
   rest; a matching `stopIfTrue` rule stops the walk; multi-area `sqref` is
   one range.
5. **Drawing:** a dxf through styles' `dxfCss` + `allowListed` (never a font
   family); a colour scale as `background-color`, 2 or 3 colours interpolated
   in sRGB with `min`, `max`, `num`, `percent`, `percentile`, `formula`
   thresholds; a data bar as a `background-image` gradient from `minLength`
   (10) to `maxLength` (90) %. A rule fill with no text colour keeps the
   static style's colour, else `fonts[0]`'s, else black. These colours are
   the file's data: the same in both themes (SR-GRID 15a); state tints and
   error rings sit above them (SR-GRID 15b).
6. **Formulas** — `expression`, formula operands, formula thresholds — run
   through the `derive` provider's synchronous `evaluate()`, shifted from the
   first range's top-left (`shiftFormula`, re-exported by the grid); without
   one they are skipped with reason `formula`. `skippedRules(store)` →
   `{ rules, shown, skipped[] }`.
7. **Live, cached:** range statistics per sheet and `sqref`, results per
   cell, keyed on the snapshot's `book`, `changes` and `derived`; a change
   drops the changed cells, every cell of a range whose statistics hold one,
   and every result that read another cell; a `#style:` change drops only its
   cell; a new workbook resets all.
8. **UI:** hovering a rule-coloured cell shows `Conditional: <the rule in
   words>` and its range (an overlay with `passThrough`); the cell bar names
   the selected cell's rules; `status`: "n conditional rules from the file"
   (· k not shown).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `just test-pkg condfmt` — 44 tests (one hand-made
  fixture per rule type compared cell by cell through the plugin and a real
  `<sheetpane-excel>`; priority and `stopIfTrue`; scales and bar widths;
  expressions through the real `@sheetpane/formulas`, including a workbook
  without a formula cell; live re-evaluation counted; the order against
  styles, in both registration orders; the legend, the count and error rings
  over rule fills; L5; the package shape and the headless boundary).
  Mutation runs on the evaluator (stopIfTrue, statistics drop, volatile drop)
  each failed tests.
- **Owed:** a fixture per rule type **saved by Excel** — W-30.
- Not drawn: x14 data-bar extensions (negative colour, axis, solid fill,
  `showValue`), icon sets; a dxf's `<b val="0"/>` is lost at import.
- The hover legend reads the grid's cell elements (`data-r`, `data-c`): the
  plugin host has no per-cell hover text (backlog B-034); controls get no
  store, so the plugin keeps one per workbook from `decorate`.

### Alternatives considered

- Recomputing statistics per cell, or dropping the whole cache on any change
  — rejected for cost.
- A `title` through `decorate` — not on the allow-list; a `cell` control
  mark — its label is fixed and it would mark every coloured cell.
- Icon sets in v1 — they need glyphs.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/condfmt/src/`](../packages/condfmt/src/) · [`packages/condfmt/test/`](../packages/condfmt/test/)
- [SR-STYLES](0110_STYLES.md) decision 8 — the helpers

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a cell in a real-app fixture (W-30) is coloured
differently from Excel by a rule type listed as drawn, or a rule fill hides a
sheetpane mark.

**How to check it:** `just test-pkg condfmt`

**Code**

- [`packages/condfmt/src/index.ts`](../packages/condfmt/src/index.ts) · [`rules.ts`](../packages/condfmt/src/rules.ts) · [`evaluate.ts`](../packages/condfmt/src/evaluate.ts) · [`ui.ts`](../packages/condfmt/src/ui.ts)

**Project docs**

<!-- source: records/0115_FIXTURES.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0115_FIXTURES.md) -->

# SR-FIXTURES — @sheetpane/fixtures

## §1 — For humans

**Test files you don't have to make.** A host, a demo or a test loads a known
workbook and knows what is in it: its sheets, its titles, the features it
exercises, the errors the rules sample produces on it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M["scripts/make.mjs (writeZip)"] --> F["files/: showcase · rules · edge · csv"]
    M --> J["fixtures.json + src/manifest.ts + src/urls.ts"]
    F --> A["url() · path() · bytes() · info()"]
    J --> A
    A --> T["tests · demos · @sheetpane/testing"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   scripts/make.mjs (writeZip) --> files/ (showcase, rules sample, edge cases, csv dialects)
                               --> fixtures.json, src/manifest.ts, src/urls.ts
   files + manifest --> url(), path(), bytes(), info() --> tests, demos, @sheetpane/testing
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

W-42 asked for the samples scattered across `examples/` and the plugins' test
helpers to become one package any runner can load (W-32 made the showcase).

### Decision

1. **The package** has no dependencies (`@sheetpane/export` is a
   devDependency of the generator only) and ships `dist/` and `files/` —
   the one exception to SR-BUILD decision 7's `dist`-only rule, so that
   `url()` reaches the files from `src/` and `dist/` alike. `./files/*` is
   exported.
2. **The files** — `showcase.xlsx` (one sheet per plugin; its `Tables`
   sheet, W-61, holds two Excel tables — Units, and Readings with a totals
   row — and a list rule over `Units[Unit]` through the defined name
   `UnitList`), `showcase.rules.json`, `dependent-lists.xlsx` (W-60:
   Readings' Unit list is `=INDIRECT($A2)` over one defined name per
   parameter on Lists; one stale unit, `Readings!C6`), `protected.xlsx`
   (W-62: Spec and Lists protected with the password `sheetpane`, stored as
   Excel's legacy hash `CC7D`; Spec's Value, Unit and Description columns
   unlocked — their cells and their `<col style>`, so empty rows below stay
   open — Parameter and the header locked, Limit a hidden formula; Notes not
   protected; the structure locked, Archive hidden), `edge/` (empty,
   hidden sheet, non-ASCII names, merged, 1904, formula errors, a legacy
   `.xls`, not a ZIP), `csv/` (comma, semicolon, tab, BOM, quoted, formula
   guard), `compare/` (W-63: `base.xlsx` and `now.xlsx`, two versions of one
   spec workbook — a price changed, a row removed, added and moved, a sheet
   renamed, removed and added) — are written by `scripts/make.mjs`, never hand-zipped, and are the
   same byte for byte on every run (`writeZip`'s fixed timestamps). The
   250,000-row case is `hugeCsv(rows)`, not a file.
3. **The manifest** `files/fixtures.json` (and `src/manifest.ts`, generated
   beside it) lists per file its kind, `appSaved` (null for hand-built), its
   sheets with titles, its features, and for the rules sample the cells it
   fails; refused files are `kind: "refused"`.
4. **The API:** `url(name)` (one literal `new URL('../files/…',
   import.meta.url)` per file in the generated `src/urls.ts`, so every
   bundler copies each — a template string reaches no subfolder),
   `path(name)` (Node), `bytes(name)` (disk in Node, `fetch` elsewhere, typed
   without Node's types), `info(name)`, `MANIFEST`, `hugeCsv(rows)`.
5. **Used by** both demos (the gallery and the Rules file tab) and the grid's
   rules-file test; `@sheetpane/testing` (W-41) loads from here;
   `@sheetpane/validation`'s tests read `dependent-lists.xlsx` (W-60);
   the grid's, the formulas plugin's and `@sheetpane/visibility`'s
   protection tests read `protected.xlsx` (W-62). `book()` in `make.mjs`
   takes its own `styles`, a `workbookProtection` element and per-column
   formats (`colStyle`); every other file is unchanged byte for byte.
6. **The parity pair (W-54):** `test/parity.ts` names the cases — every
   manifest file (the refused two by their code) and `hugeCsv(20000)` — and
   the pane's settings for each (the rules sample, element `columns`, an
   async `validate`; plugins numfmt, validation, comments, formulas).
   `parity.test.ts` opens each in `<sheetpane-excel>` in the browser,
   `parity.node.test.ts` runs `check()` from `@sheetpane/grid/check` in Node;
   both must equal `test/golden/parity.json` (errors without `id` and
   `createdAt`, in one order), so the browser and Node agree.
   `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` rewrites it from Node. Those four plugins and
   `@sheetpane/validation` are this package's devDependencies for it.
6a. **The static pair (W-67):** `test/static.ts` names the cases — the
   showcase, `merged`, `hidden-sheet`, `unicode-names`, `date1904` and
   `comma.csv`, with the rules sample, plugins numfmt, styles, condfmt,
   validation and comments, and one edit on the showcase (a changed and a
   stale cell) plus its Numbers sheet's later marks — results at `marks`
   (one under a rule's error), an accepted deviation, an error about the
   sheet and one about the workbook, and one in a hidden layer. `static.test.ts` opens each in `<sheetpane-excel>` (Edit,
   Chromium) and, for every sheet in both themes, compares each cell and
   header of `renderStatic()`'s table with the grid's — computed text,
   colours, weight, style, size, alignment, borders, padding, the mark's ring
   and tint, a result's glyph, colour, size and label, the changed corner,
   width and height; `static.node.test.ts`
   renders the same in Node; both equal `test/golden/static.json`.
   `@sheetpane/styles` and `@sheetpane/condfmt` are devDependencies for it.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project fixtures --project
  node` — every listed file read in Chromium matches its sheets and titles;
  refused files are refused; the hidden sheet and 1904 read as listed; the
  rules sample on the showcase fails exactly the listed cells; `path()` and
  `bytes()` in Node; `hugeCsv()`; the parity pair (decision 6); the static
  pair (decision 6a). `pack-check` checks the `./files/*` folder.
- **Owed:** files saved by Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice and Numbers,
  with `appSaved` naming the app and version — W-30 (DoD 5). The import
  package's ExcelJS fixtures stay with their generator (ExcelJS is that
  package's devDependency).

### Alternatives considered

- Fixtures inside `dist/` only — rejected: `url()` from `src/` (the
  workspace's `source` condition) would point at nothing.
- One template `new URL(\`../files/${name}\`, import.meta.url)` — rejected:
  Vite rewrites it into a one-level glob and subfolders resolve to nothing.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/fixtures/`](../packages/fixtures/) · [`packages/fixtures/scripts/make.mjs`](../packages/fixtures/scripts/make.mjs)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a listed file stops matching its manifest, or the
generator writes different bytes from the same source.

**How to check it:** `just fixtures && git diff --exit-code packages/fixtures/files`

*Every source this record cites, gathered in one place. An archived document
is never listed here.*

**Records** — [SR-BUILD](0102_BUILD.md) · [SR-GRID](0105_GRID.md) · [SR-LAW-3](0005_LAW-3-xlsx-and-csv-only.md)

**Code**

- [`packages/fixtures/src/index.ts`](../packages/fixtures/src/index.ts) · [`packages/fixtures/scripts/make.mjs`](../packages/fixtures/scripts/make.mjs)

<!-- source: records/0116_SKILLS.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0116_SKILLS.md) -->

# SR-SKILLS — @sheetpane/skills

## §1 — For humans

**A host's agent knows sheetpane.** One command copies sheetpane's skills into
a repository, so Claude Code, Kiro and Codex embed, load, export, review, rule,
theme, test and extend sheetpane from the same text — each skill pointing back
to the record it summarises.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P["@sheetpane/skills: skills/ · entry/ · bin/"] --> I["npx sheetpane-skills install"]
    I --> C[".claude/skills · CLAUDE.md block · .claude/agents"]
    I --> K[".kiro/skills · steering · .kiro/agents"]
    I --> X[".agents/skills · AGENTS.md block"]
    T["test/skills.test.ts"] -.drift check.-> P
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   @sheetpane/skills (skills/, entry/, bin/) --npx sheetpane-skills install--> .claude/, .kiro/, .agents/ (+ marked blocks)
   test/skills.test.ts checks every skill against the elements' source
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Decision

1. **The package** ships `skills/`, `entry/`, `bin/` only, has no
   dependencies and no build, and is a `dependency` of export, import, grid
   and every plugin package at the lockstep version (`sheetpane-plugins`
   lists each, `@sheetpane/tables` since W-61, visibility and compare included) — SR-BUILD decision 7's
   second exception. `@sheetpane/grid` exposes the same `sheetpane-skills`
   bin (`src/skills-bin.ts` forwards to `@sheetpane/skills/bin`), because
   package managers link only direct dependencies' bins.
2. **The skills:** 25 folders `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — 23 for hosts, two
   for contributors (`sheetpane-file-work-item`, `sheetpane-records`), and the
   router `sheetpane`. Frontmatter is the subset all three tools read: `name`
   (= folder), `description` (≤ 250 characters, saying when to use it **and
   when not**; unquoted, it never holds `: ` or ` #`, which break YAML and make
   Claude Code drop every key), optional `license` and `metadata`
   (`audience`). No `argument-hint`: claude.ai and the Skills API refuse it. A `SKILL.md`
   is ≤ 200 lines. A skill links to its records on GitHub (so the links work
   once installed elsewhere) and never restates a rule as its own
   (SR-LAW-0). Where a host's step runs outside the page — checking a file
   on a server or in a worker — `sheetpane-setup` and `sheetpane-backend`
   point at `@sheetpane/grid/check` (W-54, SR-GRID decision 22f), and
   `sheetpane-backend` at `@sheetpane/grid/static` for a report or an email
   showing the sheet (W-67, SR-GRID decision 22g).
2a. **Commands (W-45):** every skill is a command in all three tools (`/name`
    in Claude Code and Kiro, `$name` in Codex), the typed text reaching it
    (`$ARGUMENTS` where filled). Three are written as commands:
    `sheetpane-embed [framework]`, and two thin routers — `sheetpane-rules
    [path]` → `sheetpane-rules-file`, `sheetpane-test [runner]` →
    `sheetpane-testing`. Nothing was renamed.
3. **Entry files:** `entry/claude.md` and `entry/agents.md` — a ≤ 30-line
   block between `<!-- sheetpane:start -->` / `<!-- sheetpane:end -->`;
   `entry/kiro-steering.md` (`inclusion: fileMatch`); `entry/claude-agent.md`
   and `entry/kiro-agent.json` (a `sheetpane-integrator`, the Kiro one listing
   the skills as `skill://` resources).
4. **The installer** `bin/sheetpane-skills.mjs` (Node ≥ 20, no dependencies,
   no `postinstall`): `install` / `uninstall`, `--claude --kiro --codex
   --all`, `--skip` / `--only` (groups or skills), `--skills-only`,
   `--no-mcp`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--cwd`. With no tool flag it installs
   for the tools whose folders exist. It edits only the marked blocks of
   `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`, refuses to overwrite a file changed since it
   wrote it unless `--force`, and records every path in
   `.sheetpane-skills.json` so `uninstall` removes exactly those.
4a. **The MCP server entry (W-39, SR-MCP decision 8):** unless `--no-mcp` or
   `--skills-only`, install also registers `@sheetpane/mcp` (`npx -y
   @sheetpane/mcp`) — the `sheetpane` key of `mcpServers` in `.mcp.json`
   (Claude Code) and `.kiro/settings/mcp.json` (Kiro), every other key kept;
   a `# sheetpane:start` … `# sheetpane:end` block holding
   `[mcp_servers.sheetpane]` in `.codex/config.toml` (Codex). A config that is
   not a JSON object, an entry edited since install, or a
   `[mcp_servers.sheetpane]` outside the block is refused without `--force`;
   `uninstall` removes the entry, and the file only when install created it
   and nothing else is left.
4b. **`sheetpane-skills check-rules <file…>` (W-45):** the rules file's
    document checks of the grid's `checkDocument` (SP-6010…SP-6021, the same
    codes and messages, re-implemented in the dependency-free bin; a test keeps
    the two equal on 19 documents), one line per problem; exit 0 clean, 1 a
    problem, 2 usage or an unreadable file. `--hook claude | codex | kiro`
    reads the edited path (Claude's `tool_input.file_path`, Codex's
    `apply_patch` text, Kiro's `{{filePath}}`), ignores all but
    `*.rules.json`, and on a problem writes stderr and exits 2 so the agent
    sees it.
4c. **Hooks (W-45):** `install` writes, unless `--no-hooks` or
    `--skills-only`: a `PostToolUse` group (`Edit|Write|MultiEdit`) in
    `.claude/settings.json`; `.codex/hooks.json` (`PostToolUse` on
    `apply_patch` — Codex runs it once the user trusts it in `/hooks`, so the
    `AGENTS.md` block also says to run the check); `.kiro/hooks/sheetpane-rules.json`
    (`PostFileSave`, `\.rules\.json$`). A JSON group is ours by its exact
    command, recorded like decision 4a's MCP entry (refused if hand-edited
    without `--force`; every other key kept; the file removed only when install
    made it and nothing else is left).
4d. **The Claude Code plugin (W-45):** `scripts/build-plugin.mjs` (`just
    plugin`) generates `plugins/sheetpane/` — the host skills, the integrator
    subagent, `.mcp.json` (`@sheetpane/mcp`), `hooks/hooks.json` running a
    bundled copy of the bin — and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`; a
    freshness test fails on any stale or extra file. `claude plugin validate
    --strict` passes on both. Install: `/plugin marketplace add
    arpitarya/sheetpane`, then `/plugin install sheetpane@sheetpane`. Formats
    as documented on 2026-10-18 (Claude Code skills, hooks, plugins; Kiro
    hooks 2026-10-10; Codex hooks).
5. **The drift check** (`test/skills.test.ts`) reads every skill and fails on
   a frontmatter key outside the subset, a `name` ≠ folder, a description over
   250 characters or without its "not for", a `SKILL.md` over 200 lines, a
   link that does not resolve, or an event, element attribute or member that
   the elements' source does not have (derived from `observedAttributes`, the
   classes' members and the events the packages fire).
6. **Dogfood:** this repository installs its two contributor skills for all
   three tools (`--only contributor --skills-only`); its own `CLAUDE.md` is
   governed by SR-WORK-DOCS and is not written by the installer.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `test/skills.test.ts` — the drift check per skill and
  the installer in temp repositories (each tool and all, re-run no-op,
  hand-edit refused without `--force`, the block replaced with the text
  outside kept, uninstall restoring the repo, `--dry-run`, `--skip
  contributor`, Windows paths); `test/packages.test.ts` (the package shape
  and its font scan of `skills/`, `entry/`, `bin/`); `pack-check`.
- **Owed:** one real prompt per tool from the packed tarballs — W-48, the
  decider's (split from W-35 DoD 8; it did not block W-35). Skill 18 (`sheetpane-frameworks`) was written with
  W-37's typings; `sheetpane-react` points at `@sheetpane/grid/jsx`.
  `sheetpane-plugins` and `sheetpane-plugin-author` name rich text with W-53
  (a sheet's `runs`, `decorateRuns`, `richText` on `sheetpane-editstart`), so the
  drift check covers them. `sheetpane-rules-file` names W-58's *Write rules as
  Excel dropdowns* (`rulesAsValidation`, `lastRulesWrite`, SP-5401 – SP-5406)
  and `sheetpane-plugin-author` the export switch's `applies` (W-58).
- **Taught since W-56 (2026-10-19):** `sheetpane-events` and `sheetpane-react`
  cover `sheetpane-hover`, `highlight()` and `clearHighlight()`; the drift
  check (decision 5) reads them against the element's source.
- **Taught since W-62 (2026-10-19):** `sheetpane-security` covers protected
  sheets — locked cells refused with SP-3026, hidden formulas, the structure
  lock (sheets, and since the merge inserts and deletes, with a sheet's
  insert/delete switches), `protection="ignore"` as the host's decision, and that a password is
  never read or removed; `sheetpane-events` lists `reason: 'locked'` on
  `sheetpane-editcancel`.
- **Taught since W-66 (2026-10-19):** `sheetpane-embed` covers `ref`,
  `link="hash"` and *Copy link*, and that React, Vue and Solid set `ref`
  with `setAttribute` (their own `ref` is the framework's).
- **Taught since W-52 (2026-10-19):** `sheetpane-events` covers inserting and
  deleting rows and columns — the menus, the keys, the store methods,
  `kind: 'structure'` with `op`, `at` and `count`, the SP-3022…3020 refusals;
  `sheetpane-plugin-author` covers `DeriveInput` `restructure`, the moved
  `ctx.book` and `restructureFormula`.

### Alternatives considered

- A `postinstall` that writes skills — rejected: pnpm blocks lifecycle
  scripts by default, and writing into a repository unasked is wrong.
- Reading skills from `node_modules` — none of the three tools does.
- Relative record links — rejected: they break once the skills sit in
  another repository.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/skills/`](../packages/skills/) · [`test/skills.test.ts`](../test/skills.test.ts)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a skill names an API the elements do not have, or
`uninstall` leaves a file `install` wrote.

**How to check it:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project repo test/skills.test.ts`

<!-- source: records/0117_CODES.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0117_CODES.md) -->

# SR-CODES — stable error codes

## §1 — For humans

**An error you can look up.** `SP-3012: header row 2 not found — …/ERRORS.md#sp-3012`
tells a host — or an agent — what happened and where the fix is. Codes are
permanent: a code is never reused or renumbered.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["CODES (packages/export/src/codes.ts)"] --> H["spError · spMessage · codeOf"]
    H --> T["throws · console · notes · load refusals · blocked edits"]
    R --> D["docs/ERRORS.md (index generated)"]
    C["test/error-codes.test.ts + lock"] -.checks.-> T & D & R
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   CODES (export/src/codes.ts) --> spError, spMessage, codeOf --> throws, console, notes, load refusals, blocked edits
   CODES --> docs/ERRORS.md (index generated)
   test/error-codes.test.ts + error-codes.lock.json check all three
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Decision

1. **Every message sheetpane shows a host carries `SP-` and four digits:**
   thrown errors, `console.warn` / `console.error`, rules-engine `note`
   errors, refused loads, event details that carry a reason.
2. **Ranges:** 1xxx import · 2xxx export (21xx `download()`) · 3xxx grid
   (SP-3020, W-54: `check()` given something other than bytes; SP-3027 and
   SP-3028, W-67: `renderStatic()` given no loaded workbook, or a sheet or
   range it cannot draw) ·
   4xxx `<sheetpane-errors>` · 5xxx plugins (5100 numfmt, 5200 formulas,
   5300 styles, 5400 validation, 5500 condfmt, 5600 images, 5700 charts,
   5800 comments, 5900 compare — W-63: SP-5901, a per-sheet key that is
   not a column; 5000 review — W-59: SP-5001 – SP-5005, its own hundred, the
   5100 – 5900 hundreds being taken) · 6xxx column rules and the rules file · 7xxx mcp
   (W-39: SP-7001…7007, the MCP server's tool errors — SR-MCP decision 7;
   `@sheetpane/mcp` also reports the 60xx rules notes `check_rules` finds).
3. **Never reuse:** a code is never renumbered or removed; a dead one stays in
   `CODES` with `retired: true`; `test/error-codes.lock.json` is append-only.
4. **The registry** is `CODES` in `packages/export/src/codes.ts` (the leaf
   every package depends on): titles and severity only — the long text lives
   in the docs. Plugins read it through `@sheetpane/grid`'s re-export.
5. **One helper:** `spMessage(code, detail)` →
   `SP-xxxx: <title> — <detail> (<docs>#sp-xxxx)`; `spError` builds an Error
   carrying `code`, `spCode`, `spDetail`; `codeOf(x)`, `detailOf(x)`,
   `codeUrl(code)`.
6. **Where the code lives:** `spCode` on every thrown error; where `code` was
   free it is the SP code (plain errors, `SheetpaneError.code`, the
   `sheetpane-editcancel` detail); where `code` is already a typed reason
   (`ExportError`, `ImportError`, `LoadState`) it stays and `spCode` sits
   beside it. Messages keep their old text after the code.
7. **`docs/ERRORS.md`:** one entry per code (`### SP-xxxx`): meaning, likely
   cause, fix, the record it comes from; its index is generated from `CODES`
   and compared by the test (`SP_WRITE_ERRORS_DOC=1` rewrites it).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `test/error-codes.test.ts` (87) scans `packages/*/src`
  for a throw (outside a three-line, reasoned allow-list), a console line not
  built by `spMessage`, or a rules note without a code; checks ranges, the
  lock, a docs entry per code and none without one, and the index. 73 codes at
  W-40. Later codes are appended to the lock in the order they were issued,
  not by number. Example: SP-5804, from W-55, comes after SP-7007, and
  SP-3016 and SP-3017, from W-68 (a dropped error `meta`, a throwing
  `renderDetail`), come after SP-5804, and SP-3018, from W-69 (an acceptance
  refused), after them; SP-3021, from W-51 (an unusable review-layer name),
  after SP-5901.
- **W-65** added SP-1009 (warning): no SHA-256 where Web Crypto is missing —
  the file's fingerprint is `undefined`, never a substitute (SR-IMPORT
  decision 11).
- **W-57** added SP-2015 (error, `bad-rule`): a data-validation rule,
  conditional format or differential format `toXlsx` / `patchXlsx` cannot
  write as Excel reads it (SR-EXPORT decision 6).
- **W-66** added SP-3019 (warning): the `ref` attribute or a `#sheetpane=`
  link names no cell (SR-GRID decision 11d).
- **W-58** added SP-5401 – SP-5407 (warnings), the first 5400 codes: the
  host's rules written into the download as Excel's own — a check Excel
  cannot hold, two checks in one rule, a list it cannot type out, a bound it
  cannot read, a missing column or sheet, cells that keep their own rule,
  and a sheet whose rules could not be rewritten (SR-VALIDATION decision 10).
- **W-54** added SP-3020 (error, `TypeError`): `check()` from
  `@sheetpane/grid/check` given something other than a file's bytes (SR-GRID
  decision 22f). Issued as SP-3016 in its lane; renumbered at the merge, as
  W-68 had taken SP-3016.
- **W-51** added SP-3021 (warning): a review-layer name that is not one
  (SR-GRID decision 5d). Issued as SP-3019 in its lane; renumbered at the
  merge, as W-66 had taken SP-3019.
- **W-59** added SP-5001 – SP-5005, the 5000 hundred (`@sheetpane/review`:
  the Review sheet not written, a sheet's cells not coloured, a range too
  large to colour whole, no styles part, a fill that is not a colour — SR-REVIEW
  decisions 8–9). Issued as SP-5901 – SP-5905 in its lane; renumbered at the
  merge, as the 5900 hundred is @sheetpane/compare's (W-63, SP-5901);
  appended to the lock after SP-3021.
- **W-52** added SP-2016 (`bad-structure`, an error) and SP-3022 – SP-3025
  (warnings: a merge cut, a pivot moved, cells pushed off the sheet, a table
  cut) (SR-EXPORT decision 11, SR-GRID decision 21d). Issued as SP-2015 and
  SP-3017 – SP-3020 in its lane; renumbered at the merge, as W-57, W-68,
  W-69, W-66 and W-54 had taken them; appended to the lock after SP-5005.
- **W-62** added SP-3026 (warning, *Locked in the file*): an edit refused on a
  locked cell of a protected sheet, carried by `sheetpane-editcancel`
  `{ reason: 'locked', code: 'SP-3026' }` (SR-GRID decision 21e); since the
  merge, also W-52's insert or delete refused by the structure lock or a
  sheet's insert/delete switch (decision 21d). Issued as
  SP-3020 in its lane; renumbered at the merge, as W-54 had taken it;
  appended to the lock after SP-3025.
- **W-67** added SP-3027 (error, `TypeError`: `renderStatic()` given no
  loaded workbook) and SP-3028 (error, `RangeError`: a sheet it does not
  hold, a range that is not A1, or more than 200,000 cells) (SR-GRID
  decision 22g). Issued as SP-3017 and SP-3018 in its lane; renumbered at
  the merge, as W-68 and W-69 had taken them; appended to the lock after
  SP-3026.
- Hosts that matched message text keep working; they should move to `spCode`
  / `codeOf()`.
- Consumers: the troubleshoot skill (W-35) and the MCP `explain_code` tool
  (W-39) read `CODES`.

### Alternatives considered

- Replacing `.code` with the SP code — rejected: it breaks the typed reasons
  the grid, hosts and tests read.
- A generator script under `scripts/` — rejected: the test renders and
  compares the index.
- A code per throw site for `ExportError` / `ImportError` — not yet: one code
  per typed reason, the docs list each reason's causes; finer codes can be
  added without reusing any.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/export/src/codes.ts`](../packages/export/src/codes.ts) · [`docs/ERRORS.md`](../docs/ERRORS.md) · [`test/error-codes.test.ts`](../test/error-codes.test.ts)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a code is reused or renumbered, or a message
reaches a host without one.

**How to check it:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project repo test/error-codes.test.ts`

<!-- source: records/0118_TESTING.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0118_TESTING.md) -->

# SR-TESTING — @sheetpane/testing

## §1 — For humans

**A host's tests read like what a reviewer does:** `await sp.edit('B2', '42');
expect(await sp.readDownload()).toHaveCell('Sheet1!B2', 42)` — in Playwright and
in Vitest browser mode, through the hooks the grid promises to keep.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    T["the host's test"] --> P["@sheetpane/testing/playwright — sheetpane(page)"]
    T --> D["@sheetpane/testing/dom — sheetpane(element)"]
    P & D --> H["roles · labels · data-sp-* (SR-GRID 9a)"]
    P & D --> R["readFile · changesBetween · matchers"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   host test --> sheetpane(page) [Playwright] | sheetpane(element) [Vitest browser]
             --> only roles, labels and data-sp-* hooks (SR-GRID 9a)
             --> readFile, changesBetween, valueAt, matchers (toHaveCell, toHaveError)
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Decision

1. **The package** has three entries: `.` (`readFile`, `changesBetween`,
   `valueAt`, `matchers`, the driver types), `./playwright` (`sheetpane(page,
   { excel?, errors? })`) and `./dom` (`sheetpane(element, { errors? })`).
   Dependencies `@sheetpane/import` and `@sheetpane/skills`;
   `@playwright/test` and `vitest` are optional peers — Playwright's Page and
   Locator are typed structurally, never imported.
2. **One API** for both drivers: `waitForLoad`, `ref`, `select`, `edit`,
   `paste`, `flag`, `resolve`, `undo`, `switchSheet`, `download`,
   `readDownload`, `errors`, `value`, `text`. A cell is `B3`, `Sheet1!B3` or
   `{ column, row, sheet? }` (the title read from the element's
   `header-row`).
3. **Only committed hooks:** roles, labels and SR-GRID decision 9a's
   `data-sp-*` attributes — never CSS classes. A hook the helpers need is
   added to that list first.
4. **Acting as a person:** clicks, the cell bar, a paste event, the Download
   button (Playwright's download event; in the DOM driver `sheetpane-export`
   is captured and the browser's save prevented); `flag` fills the form where
   it opens (SR-GRID decision 13) and waits for it to close.
5. **Reading back:** `readFile` reads through `@sheetpane/import` in a page
   and in Node alike — the import package reads `.xlsx` without `DOMParser`
   since W-39 (SR-IMPORT decision 8), so the values-only Node reader this
   package carried at first is gone: one reader.
6. **Dogfood:** `scripts/demo-check.mjs` drives the review steps (load, flag,
   resolve, edit, Download read back) with these helpers.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `--project testing` (the DOM driver, every helper, in
  Chromium; Firefox and WebKit nightly) and `--project node` (the Playwright
  driver against the HTML demo; the Node reader on `@sheetpane/fixtures`'
  showcase, every sheet by name — its Tables sheet since W-61); `demo-check`.
- **Owed:** each starter template ships one test using these (W-43).

### Alternatives considered

- Requiring a DOM shim in Node to read `.xlsx` — rejected. A values-only
  reader of its own served until the import package read `.xlsx` in Node
  (W-39); two readers of one format was the cost, now paid off.
- Locating by CSS classes — rejected: restyling would break every host's tests.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/testing/`](../packages/testing/)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a helper needs a CSS class, or a hook in SR-GRID 9a
changes name without a major version.

**How to check it:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project testing --project node`

**Code**

- [`packages/testing/src/playwright.ts`](../packages/testing/src/playwright.ts) · [`dom.ts`](../packages/testing/src/dom.ts) · [`read.ts`](../packages/testing/src/read.ts)

<!-- source: records/0119_MCP.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0119_MCP.md) -->

# SR-MCP — @sheetpane/mcp

## §1 — For humans

**An agent asks; sheetpane answers from what ships.** `npx @sheetpane/mcp`
starts a server any MCP client can use. Every answer is computed — from the
custom-elements manifest, the import package, the grid's own checks, the
error docs and the skills — never generated, so the same question always gets
the same answer.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["agent (Claude Code, Kiro, Codex)"] -- "stdio, JSON-RPC" --> S["sheetpane-mcp"]
    S --> D["describe_api — custom-elements.json"]
    S --> I["inspect_workbook · draft_rules — @sheetpane/import"]
    S --> C["check_rules — the grid's checkDocument and check()"]
    S --> E["explain_code — docs/ERRORS.md"]
    S --> F["find_skill — @sheetpane/skills"]
    S --> W["diff_workbooks — @sheetpane/compare"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   agent --(stdio, JSON-RPC, MCP 2026-07-28)--> sheetpane-mcp
       describe_api      <- custom-elements.json (W-37)
       inspect_workbook  <- @sheetpane/import (reads .xlsx in Node)
       draft_rules       <- @sheetpane/import
       check_rules       <- @sheetpane/grid/check: checkDocument, check()
       explain_code      <- docs/ERRORS.md
       find_skill        <- @sheetpane/skills descriptions
       diff_workbooks    <- @sheetpane/compare diffWorkbooks (W-63)
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

Agents writing host code guessed attribute and event names, and could not
see inside a workbook or a rules file before wiring them. W-39 gives them a
server to ask.

### Decision

1. **The package** `@sheetpane/mcp`, bin `sheetpane-mcp`, Node ≥ 20. Runtime
   dependencies `@sheetpane/import`, `@sheetpane/grid` (its DOM-free
   `@sheetpane/grid/check` entry: the rules checker, the pane's `check()` and
   the code registry — SR-GRID decision 22f), `@sheetpane/compare` (its
   headless root) and `@sheetpane/skills`; nothing else. Its build copies `docs/ERRORS.md`, the grid's `custom-elements.json`
   and a plugin table (from each plugin's `package.json`) into `dist/`.
2. **Hand-written protocol, no SDK** (`work/compare/mcp-server.compare.md`):
   JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, one message per line; stdout carries protocol
   messages only. **Tools only** — no resources, prompts, sampling, roots or
   logging.
3. **Revision 2026-07-28, stateless:** no handshake is needed; a request's
   `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]` names the revision;
   `server/discover` returns `supportedVersions` and `capabilities`; every
   result carries `resultType: "complete"` and
   `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]`; `tools/list` is cacheable
   (`ttlMs`, `cacheScope: "public"`) and lists the tools in one fixed order.
   A version the server does not support → error −32022 with
   `{ supported, requested }`.
4. **Older clients:** `initialize` (2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18) is answered
   with that revision, and a request without the version `_meta` is answered
   the 2025 way (no `resultType`, no cache fields). JSON-RPC batches (removed
   in 2025-06-18) are an invalid request; a notification gets no reply.
5. **The tools**, each input schema JSON Schema 2020-12, `additionalProperties:
   false`:
   - `describe_api(name)` — an element, attribute, member, event (with or
     without `on`), `--sp-*` property, slot, part or plugin → its manifest
     entry (which carries the TSDoc) and its record link — an element before
     a same-named event (`sheetpane-errors` is both), a member's own `kind`
     kept as `memberKind`; near names when nothing matches (a name holding
     the ask, or a name of four letters or more the ask holds).
   - `inspect_workbook(path)` — sheets, rows × columns, dimension, the
     header-row guess (the first of the top ten rows whose two or more filled
     cells are all text), titles, each column's type (text, number, integer,
     date — by its number format — boolean, mixed, empty), blanks, up to 12
     distinct values, merges, freeze, counts of formulas, validations,
     conditional formats, pictures, charts and notes, and the plugins the file
     would use (`@sheetpane/tables` when a sheet holds an Excel table, W-61).
   - `draft_rules(path, sheet?)` — a W-33 rules file: per titled column
     `required` when it has no blanks, its type, `oneOf` for a text column of
     2–12 distinct values; `draft: true` and a note to review it; problems
     (no title, duplicate title, mixed types) listed.
   - `check_rules(rules, path?)` — the grid's `checkDocument` (the same 60xx
     notes the grid gives), each rule in words (`describeRule`); with a
     workbook, the pane's own `check()` over it (W-54 — no third copy): its
     workbook notes as problems (SP-6022 a sheet it lacks, SP-6023 a title no
     header row has, SP-6024 a duplicated title a rule names — each on the
     sheet and cell the grid puts it) and the cells that fail as `findings`
     (`sheet`, `range`, `type`, `severity`, `found`, `expected`, `message`;
     the first 50, in `check()`'s order) with `findingCount`; `ok` speaks of
     the rules file only.
   - `explain_code(code)` — title and severity from the registry; meaning,
     cause and fix from `docs/ERRORS.md`; the link.
   - `find_skill(task)` — words of the task against each skill's name (×3)
     and description, the "Not for …" clause left out; the top three.
   - `diff_workbooks(base, path, key?, headerRow?, limit?)` — SR-COMPARE's
     `diffWorkbooks` on two files: the summary and its line, then per sheet
     that is not the same its status, names, rename likeness, key, counts,
     columns, rows (1-based: added, removed, changed, moved from → to),
     cells (`was` / `now`), merges, hidden and rule counts — at most `limit`
     (default 200) rows of each kind and cells per sheet, with a `truncated`
     note; the key is for every sheet, so a sheet without it is aligned
     unkeyed and says so in a `note`. Listed last. A coded error a package
     throws reaches the agent with its code first, as a ToolError does.
6. **Read-only and bounded:** paths come from the agent and are only read;
   `.xlsx` and `.csv` only (SR-LAW-3, the import package refuses the rest);
   256 MB at most; no network, no writes.
7. **Errors:** a bad input is a tool result with `isError: true`, its text an
   SP code first — the reader's own (SP-10xx) or the server's SP-7001…7007 —
   never a crash; an unknown tool is −32602, an unknown method −32601.
8. **Registration:** `sheetpane-skills install` (SR-SKILLS) adds the server
   — `{ "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@sheetpane/mcp"] }` — under the
   `sheetpane` key of `.mcp.json` (Claude Code) and
   `.kiro/settings/mcp.json` (Kiro), and as a marked
   `[mcp_servers.sheetpane]` block in `.codex/config.toml` (Codex, trusted
   projects); `--no-mcp` leaves it out.

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `packages/mcp/test/mcp.node.test.ts` (`--project
  node`) — the protocol over a spawned server (discover, legacy initialize,
  list, call, every error), the schemas, golden outputs per tool on the
  showcase and the rules sample (`UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` rewrites them), bad input
  as tool errors; `test/skills.test.ts` for the registration; the error-code
  registry for 7xxx.
- **Goldens follow the manifest:** `describe-onchange.json` was rewritten
  (2026-10-19, W-52) when `sheetpane-change` gained `op`, `at` and `count`
  for an insert or delete — `describe_api` reads the element manifest, so a
  changed event contract changes its answer; no code here changed.
- **Not done:** a run against the MCP Inspector — it is an interactive tool;
  the spawned-server test stands in for it.

### Alternatives considered

- The official TypeScript SDK — rejected for now: several runtime
  dependencies for a server with six read-only tools; see the compare doc.
- Resources for the docs and records — rejected: tools answer a question;
  a resource dump is what `llms-full.txt` already is.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/mcp/`](../packages/mcp/) · [MCP 2026-07-28 schema](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a second transport (HTTP) or resources/prompts
are wanted, or the 2026-07-28 revision changes what a stateless request must
carry.

**How to check it:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project node packages/mcp`

<!-- source: records/0121_VISIBILITY.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0121_VISIBILITY.md) -->

# SR-VISIBILITY — @sheetpane/visibility

## §1 — For humans

**Seeing is core; changing is the plugin.** Without this plugin the grid
still hides what the file hides, marks every place, and lets a reviewer show
it for viewing. With it, in Edit, an editor can hide and unhide rows,
columns and sheets and group outlines — counted, undoable, and in the
download.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U["Hide rows 4–6 (bar, menu, Ctrl+Alt+9)"] --> S["store.setHidden — a change"]
    M["◂▸ marker click (Edit)"] --> S
    S --> G["the grid redraws: 0 px, a marker"]
    S --> D["Download: patchXlsx hidden"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   Hide / Unhide / Group (selection bar, cell + header + tab menus, keys, marker click)
       -> store.setHidden / setSheetState / setOutline (changes, undoable)
       -> the grid redraws (SR-GRID 21c)  -> the download carries it (SR-EXPORT hidden)
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Decision

1. **The package:** `@sheetpane/visibility` — `visibility()` (headless, `id:
   'visibility'`, no hook: its presence lets a marker click unhide in Edit)
   and the actions `setSpanHidden`, `setSheetHidden`, `hiddenIn`,
   `canHideSheet`, `spanOf`, `blockedReason`, `sheetBlockedReason` (W-62); `@sheetpane/visibility/ui`
   adds the controls (`id: 'visibility-ui'`) and registers `visibility` for
   the `plugins` attribute. `@sheetpane/grid` is a peer; `@sheetpane/export`
   a dependency. No seventh hook: the core API (SR-GRID 21c) does the work.
2. **Controls** (all `selbar`, Edit, labels that follow the selection — "Hide
   rows 4–6", "Unhide columns C–E"): Hide rows (Ctrl/⌘+Alt+9), Hide columns
   (Ctrl/⌘+Alt+0), Unhide rows (Ctrl/⌘+Shift+9), Unhide columns
   (Ctrl/⌘+Shift+0) — in the cell and header menus (`menus`, SR-GRID 19);
   Group / Ungroup (Alt+Shift+→ / ←; whole columns selected → columns, else
   rows) — in the header menu; Hide sheet — in the tab menu. Keys are Google
   Sheets' (Excel's Ctrl+9 / Ctrl+0 are the browser's), digits matched on
   `e.code`.
3. **Rules:** Unhide needs a selection across the hidden span (as in Excel);
   the last visible sheet cannot be hidden ("A workbook needs one visible
   sheet"); Hide sheet writes `hidden`, never `veryHidden`, and moves to the
   next visible sheet; a CSV stores no hidden state, so every control is
   disabled there with the reason ("CSV can't store hidden rows"). **A
   protected structure (W-62):** while the file's `<workbookProtection
   lockStructure="1">` is honoured (SR-GRID 21e, `structureLockedIn`),
   Hide sheet is disabled with "Locked in the file — the workbook's
   structure is protected" (`sheetBlockedReason`) and `setSheetHidden`
   returns `false`; the store refuses `setSheetState` itself, and the core
   banner's *Unhide* is disabled with the same reason. `protection="ignore"`
   opens them. Rows and columns are not covered by the structure lock.
4. **Changes:** hiding is one change per sheet and axis (`hidden`), a sheet's
   state one (`sheetState`), outline levels one per axis (`outline`) —
   counted, undoable, exported (SR-GRID 21c, SR-EXPORT `hidden`).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `packages/visibility/test/visibility.test.ts` (Chromium):
  the bar's label and its run, ⌘⌥9 matched on `e.code`, one change and undo;
  Unhide disabled until a range crosses the gap; a marker click unhides in
  Edit; the header menu's Hide and Group; the tab menu's Hide sheet and the
  last-sheet rule; CSV disabled; a protected structure (W-62, on
  `protected.xlsx`) — Hide sheet and the banner's Unhide disabled with the
  reason, `setSheetHidden` refused, both open again under
  `protection="ignore"`. The demos' gallery tab "Hide and show" and
  its `demo-check` step.
- **Not done:** opening a download in Excel and LibreOffice (W-30's real-app
  files).

### Alternatives considered

- A seventh plugin hook to change geometry — rejected: hiding changes which
  cells exist on screen; core owns geometry, as for merges and freeze panes.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/visibility/`](../packages/visibility/)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** editors expect a collapse of an outline group to
be saved, or a host needs hiding without the plugin's controls.

**How to check it:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project visibility`

**Code**

- [`packages/visibility/src/index.ts`](../packages/visibility/src/index.ts) · [`ui.ts`](../packages/visibility/src/ui.ts)

<!-- source: records/0122_TABLES.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0122_TABLES.md) -->

# SR-TABLES — @sheetpane/tables

## §1 — For humans

**A table looks like a table.** Excel's tables (*Insert › Table*) carry a
style: a coloured header row, banded rows, a totals row. The reader already
knows every table by name (SR-IMPORT decision 13) and a dropdown over a table
column already follows it (SR-VALIDATION decision 3); this plugin draws them.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    F["xl/tables/tableN.xml"] --> I["@sheetpane/import: sheet.tables"]
    I --> X["@sheetpane/export: resolveStructuredRef('Units[Unit]')"]
    X --> V["@sheetpane/validation: the list follows the table"]
    I --> T["@sheetpane/tables: decorate — header, bands, totals"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   xl/tables/tableN.xml -> import: sheet.tables
        -> export: resolveStructuredRef('Units[Unit]') -> validation: list sources
        -> tables: decorate (header row, bands, first/last column, totals row)
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Decision

1. **The package:** `@sheetpane/tables` — `tables()` (`id: 'tables'`,
   `provides: ['decorate']`), registered as `tables` on import; the helpers
   `tableAt(sheet, row, col)`, `findTable(book, name)` (case-insensitive),
   `tableCss(table, row, col, theme)`, `paletteOf(style, theme)`, `tint`,
   `TABLE_STYLES`. Draw-only: no control, no change kind, no `exportPatch` —
   a download keeps the file's table parts untouched (`patchXlsx` copies
   every part it does not rewrite, SR-EXPORT). `@sheetpane/grid` is a peer;
   `@sheetpane/export` (`parseRange`) a dependency. No third-party
   dependency (SR-LAW-2).
2. **What is drawn**, per cell inside a table's `ref`: the header row bold;
   the totals row bold under a 3 px double line in the style's colour; with
   `showRowStripes`, every other data row from the first filled with the
   stripe tint; with `showColumnStripes`, every other column from the first;
   `showFirstColumn` / `showLastColumn` bold. **Light** styles: a 1 px line
   in the style's colour over and under the table and under the header.
   **Medium** styles: the header filled in the style's colour with the
   theme's light colour as text, and a 1 px line (tint 0.4) under every row.
   A filled cell takes the theme's dark text colour, so it reads in a dark
   host (SR-GRID 15a: the file's colours are data). No `font-family`
   (SR-LAW-5).
3. **The subset:** `TableStyleLight1`–`7` and `TableStyleMedium1`–`7`,
   approximated from the workbook's theme (`themeColors`, Office's default
   when the file has none): style 1 in `dk1`, styles 2–7 in accents 1–6;
   stripes tint 0.8 (0.85 for `dk1`). **Every other style** — Light 8–21,
   Medium 8–28, Dark 1–11, a custom `<tableStyle>` — draws a bold header row
   only. A table that names no style draws nothing (Excel's *None*).
4. **Order:** a cell's own format and its conditional formats draw over the
   table's style, as in Excel, whatever order `plugins` lists them in:
   `styles` declares `after: ['tables']`, `condfmt` `after: ['styles',
   'tables']` (SR-GRID decision 17's `after`).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project tables` (Chromium): the
  subset and its palette from the theme; Excel's HSL tint; each region's CSS
  (Medium header, bands, totals, banded and bold columns, Light lines, no
  header row, the fallback, no style, outside); through a store and a real
  `<sheetpane-excel>`; a cell's own fill over the table's in both plugin
  orders; registration. The demos' gallery tab "Tables" and its `demo-check`
  step (both tables in their colours; C9's list is `Units[Unit]`).
- **Rows and columns inserted or deleted (W-52):** each table's `ref`, its
  `autoFilter` and, on a column delete, its `columns` move in memory as in
  the download, and a cut a table cannot follow is refused (SR-IMPORT
  decision 14, SR-GRID 21d's SP-3025) — so this plugin draws the moved table.
- **Not done:** a table's own `<autoFilter>` buttons, `[#This Row]`, totals-row
  formulas recalculated by the table and custom table styles are not drawn
  or evaluated. Opening a sheetpane download with tables in Excel is W-30's.

### Alternatives considered

- Reading each built-in style's dxfs from Excel's `presetTableStyles.xml` —
  rejected: the file is Microsoft's, not in the package, and 60 styles of
  exact borders are decoration; the subset covers the defaults
  (`TableStyleMedium2` is Excel's) and the rest stays readable.
- Drawing tables in core — rejected: a style is optional decoration, which
  is what `decorate` plugins are for; the reading and the resolver are core
  because validation needs them without this plugin.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/tables/`](../packages/tables/)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** hosts' files use table styles outside the
subset often enough that a bold header reads as broken, or a custom table
style must match Excel exactly.

**How to check it:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project tables`

---

**Code**

- [`packages/tables/src/index.ts`](../packages/tables/src/index.ts) · [`styles.ts`](../packages/tables/src/styles.ts)

<!-- source: records/0123_REVIEW.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0123_REVIEW.md) -->

# SR-REVIEW — @sheetpane/review

## §1 — For humans

**The review travels inside the file.** On download, the plugin adds a
*Review* sheet: one row per error, each with a link to its cell. A reviewer
works the list in Excel, fixes the file and uploads it again. Optionally,
every flagged cell is filled by its severity.

**The user's own cells and formatting stay.** A flagged cell keeps its
format: only its fill changes. Every other cell keeps its exact bytes, and a
sheet the user already called *Review* is never overwritten.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    E["the review (store errors)"] --> X["exportPatch"]
    X --> S["Review sheet: id · sheet · cell link · severity · … · status · Accepted"]
    X --> F["flagged cells: cloned xf + solid fill"]
    X --> N["defined name _sheetpane_review"]
    N --> H["re-upload: reviewSheetOf(book) → skip it"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   the review (store errors) -> exportPatch
       -> Review sheet (one row per error, Cell = internal hyperlink)
       -> flagged cells: their own xf cloned with a solid fill (optional)
       -> defined name _sheetpane_review  -> re-upload: reviewSheetOf(book) -> skip
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

pdfsuite's spec intake (SR-SPEC-INTAKE decision 14) needs an *annotated
workbook*: every error cell filled red and a sheet listing the errors, to fix
in Excel and re-upload. `@sheetpane/comments` (SR-COMMENTS) already writes the
review as comments. This plugin writes the same review as a table. W-59.

### Decision

1. **The package:** `@sheetpane/review` — `review(options)` (`id: 'review'`,
   `provides: ['exportPatch']`, `lastExport`), registered as `review` on
   import. Also exported: `reviewSheetOf`, `REVIEW_NAME`, `COLUMNS`,
   `PROBLEM_SEVERITIES`, `DEFAULT_FILLS`, `MAX_FILL_CELLS` and the
   `ReviewOptions`, `ReviewReport`, `SkipReason` and `ReviewPlugin` types.
   `@sheetpane/grid` is a peer; `@sheetpane/export` (its OOXML helpers) is
   the one runtime dependency. String XML only, so it runs in Node. **No new
   core hook:** the existing `exportPatch` context writes a part, adds a
   relationship and sets a content type, which is all this needs (SR-EXPORT
   is unchanged). There are no controls. `exportOptions` adds two items to
   the Download menu (W-34): *Add a Review sheet* (`review`, default
   `options.sheet !== false`) and *Colour flagged cells* (`reviewFills`,
   default `options.fill === true`).
2. **What is listed:** every error in the store except the file's own
   comments (`author: 'file'`). Only the severities in `severities` are
   listed: the default is `error`, `warning` and `note`, and results such as
   `pass` and `skipped` (W-50) appear only when named. Only the layers in
   `layers` are listed (W-51): the default is every layer, and an error with
   no `layer` is `review`. `export({ reviewSeverities, reviewLayers })`
   overrides both for one export. **An empty selection writes nothing.**
   The types are the grid's: `severities` is `Severity[]` (a
   `reviewSeverities` naming anything else is ignored) and an error's layer
   is the grid's `layerOf`.
3. **The sheet:** a new worksheet part (`xl/worksheets/sheetN.xml`, the first
   free N), a worksheet relationship from the workbook, an `<Override>`
   content type, and a `<sheet>` added last (`sheetId` = max + 1). The
   relationships namespace is bound on the root if it is missing. Cells are
   **inline strings**, so `sharedStrings` is never touched, at most 32,767
   characters each and cleaned of characters XML forbids. Columns, left to
   right: ID, Sheet, Cell, Severity, Type, Found, Expected, Message, Author,
   Status, Accepted, Accepted by, Accepted at. The header row is frozen.
   Rows come in this order: workbook errors, then each sheet in the file's
   order, with its whole-sheet errors first and then its cells from top to
   bottom and left to right.
4. **Links:** the Cell column holds an internal `<hyperlink location>`
   (`'Q3 ''final'''!B2`), which needs no relationship. A whole-sheet error
   (W-55) reads *Whole sheet* and links to its A1. A workbook error reads
   *Whole workbook* and has no link. An error whose sheet the file lacks has
   no link.
5. **Names:** the name is `sheetName` (default `Review`), with `[ ] : * ? / \`
   and apostrophes at either end removed, cut to 31 characters. If a sheet
   already has that name (compared ignoring case, as Excel does), the plugin
   adds `Review (2)`, `(3)`… within 31 characters. **A user's sheet is never
   overwritten.**
6. **The marker:** a workbook-scoped, hidden defined name `_sheetpane_review`
   over the table (`'Review'!$A$1:$M$n`), placed in schema position.
   `reviewSheetOf(book)` reads it from what `@sheetpane/import` returns, so a
   host can skip the sheet on re-upload. **Exported again**, a file whose
   marker names an existing sheet with no relationships of its own has that
   sheet rewritten in place, keeping its name and position. If someone gave
   the sheet comments or a drawing in Excel, it is left alone and a new sheet
   is added.
7. **Accepted errors (W-69, SR-ERRORS 14, SR-GRID 5c):** listed with Status
   *Accepted* and *Accepted: \<reason\>*, with who (`acceptedBy`, else the
   author) and when (`acceptedAt`, UTC). They are **never filled** and are
   counted apart from open errors in `lastExport.counts` (`{ open, accepted,
   resolved }`). Resolved errors are listed and never filled.
8. **Fills (optional):** each **open** error at a cell, whose severity has a
   colour, fills the cells of its range. The defaults are `error` FFFFC7CE,
   `warning` FFFFEB9C and `note` FFDDEBF7, and `fills` overrides them (`null`
   turns one off; a value that is not a colour throws SP-5005). The cell's
   own `xf` is **cloned** with a solid fill (`fillId`, `applyFill="1"`), once
   per format and colour. Fills and formats are only ever **appended** to
   `styles.xml`, and its counts are updated. Only a flagged cell's `s` is
   written. **Every other row and cell is byte-identical.** A flagged cell
   the file lacks is added empty, styled from its row (`customFormat`) or
   column, in column order. A missing row is created in row order, and
   `spans` and `<dimension>` are widened. When a cell has two severities, the
   worse one wins. The header row takes a grey fill, not bold: **no font is
   written** (SR-LAW-5).
9. **Not coloured, reported in `lastExport.skipped`:** `no-cell` (a
   whole-sheet or workbook error, W-55 — listed only), `no-sheet`,
   `bad-range`, `range-capped` (a range over `MAX_FILL_CELLS` = 10,000 colours
   only the cells the file has, SP-5003), `no-styles` (no readable styles
   part, SP-5004; the sheet is still written) and `unreadable-part` (the
   sheet could not be read, so it is left as it was, SP-5002). If the
   workbook part cannot be read, no sheet is written (SP-5001, logged).
10. **Scope:** an `.xlsx` download of an `.xlsx` only. Core never runs
    `exportPatch` for a CSV, or for a CSV converted to `.xlsx` (SR-LAW-3).
    The parts go into the bytes the browser saves, and nothing is sent
    anywhere (SR-LAW-11).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `packages/review/test/` (Chromium):
  - `sheet.test.ts` covers the part, relationship, content type, `<sheet>`
    and marker (all well-formed), the order, the text, the links, every
    other part byte-identical to a plain export, the `Review (2)` collision,
    name cleaning, an apostrophe in a link, export twice → one sheet, the
    switches, the severity and layer filters, accepted rows and counts, and
    the read-back through `@sheetpane/import` (`reviewSheetOf`) and
    `@sheetpane/testing` (`readFile`, `valueAt`).
  - `fills.test.ts` covers the cloned formats (number format, font, border
    and alignment kept), untouched cells byte-identical, added cells and
    rows, spans and dimension, the worse fill winning, accepted and resolved
    never filled, `no-cell`, dedup, custom fills, SP-5005, SP-5003 and
    SP-5004.
  - `roundtrip.test.ts` runs the showcase and the exceljs fixture with
    `@sheetpane/comments` on the same export.
  - `package.test.ts` checks for no font, no DOM, no network call (L11) and
    the dependencies.
  - The demos' gallery tab *Review sheet* and its `demo-check` step (L10).
- **Not done:** opening a download in real Excel, with every link going to
  its cell and no repair prompt, is part of W-30 DoD 3. An autoFilter on the
  header is not written.

### Alternatives considered

- **Shared strings:** rejected. Extending `sharedStrings.xml` touches a part
  every sheet reads; inline strings are local to the new sheet.
- **A new core hook to add a sheet:** rejected. The `exportPatch` context
  already writes parts, relationships and content types.
- **Bold header:** rejected. It writes a `<font>`, and the header is marked
  with a fill instead (SR-LAW-5's spirit: sheetpane adds no font).
- **Always adding a new sheet on re-export:** rejected. Review sheets would
  pile up. The marker lets the plugin replace its own sheet, and a sheet
  someone extended in Excel is still kept.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/review/`](../packages/review/)

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** Excel or LibreOffice repairs a downloaded file,
does not follow a link (W-30), or hosts need the Review sheet kept beside an
earlier one rather than replacing it.

**How to check it:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project review`

---

is never listed here.*

**Code**

- [`packages/review/src/index.ts`](../packages/review/src/index.ts) · [`write.ts`](../packages/review/src/write.ts) · [`sheet.ts`](../packages/review/src/sheet.ts) · [`fills.ts`](../packages/review/src/fills.ts) · [`rows.ts`](../packages/review/src/rows.ts)

<!-- source: records/0124_COMPARE.md (https://github.com/arpitarya/sheetpane/blob/v0.3.0/records/0124_COMPARE.md) -->

# SR-COMPARE — @sheetpane/compare

## §1 — For humans

**What changed since the version that was approved?** A reviewer picks the base file (or the host
hands it over); the pane marks every added, removed, moved and changed row and cell, the status
line says how much changed, and Alt+F5 walks through the changes. The same diff runs in Node and
answers an agent through the MCP server.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    B["base file (picked, or from the host)"] -- "read in the page" --> D["diffWorkbooks(base, the pane's file)"]
    P["the pane's file, as loaded"] --> D
    D --> T["decorate: tints"]
    D --> S["status: n sheets · n rows · n cells changed"]
    D --> E["publishChanges → the errors list (type compare)"]
    D --> K["Alt+F5 / Alt+Shift+F5: next / previous change"]
    D --> M["@sheetpane/mcp diff_workbooks"]
```

<details>
<summary><b>ASCII twin</b> — the same diagram, for terminals and diffs</summary>

```text
   base file (picked / from the host) --read in the page--+
   the pane's file, as loaded --------------------------> diffWorkbooks
        -> decorate (tints) -> status line (summary) -> errors list (publishChanges, type compare)
        -> Alt+F5 / Alt+Shift+F5 (next / previous change)   -> @sheetpane/mcp diff_workbooks
```

</details>

---

## §2 — For agents

### Context

pdfsuite's reviewers change a PDF template from a spec workbook; *what changed since the last
approved spec* tells them which pages to re-test (W-63, Group 3). Excel's own Spreadsheet Compare
runs only on Windows with some enterprise Office editions; `daff` (MIT) aligns table rows but knows
no sheets or merges — a reference for row alignment, not a dependency (SR-LAW-2: none is added).

### Decision

1. **The package:** `@sheetpane/compare`. The root is headless and side-effect free —
   `diffWorkbooks`, `applyDiff`, `summaryText`, `relativeFormula` and their types — and runs in
   Node and the browser. `@sheetpane/compare/ui` is the plugin (`id: 'compare'`, registered for the
   `plugins` attribute) with `compareWith`, `clearCompare`, `comparison`, `stepChange` and
   `publishChanges`. Dependencies `@sheetpane/export` and `@sheetpane/import`; `@sheetpane/grid` an
   optional peer (the `/ui` entry only). No third-party code.
2. **Sheets** match by name. An unmatched sheet of the newer workbook whose distinct rows are mostly
   an unmatched older sheet's (rows in common over rows in either ≥ `renameThreshold`, default 0.5;
   the most alike pairs first) is *renamed*; the rest are added or removed. The result lists the
   newer workbook's sheets in its order, removed sheets last.
3. **Columns** match by header-row title (trimmed, ignoring case; `headerRow`, default 1) when both
   header rows hold two or more titles and no title twice; columns left over pair in order when
   both sides have the same number left (a renamed title). Otherwise by position. Columns whose
   order changed are reported as moved (the longest in-order run stays).
4. **Rows.** With `key` columns (titles or letters; for every sheet, or per sheet with `'*'` as the
   default) rows at or above the header row pair by position and data rows by key — the n-th row
   of a key with the n-th; a pair outside the longest in-order run is **moved**; a row whose key
   cells are blank matches only a row with the same content and is never called moved. Without a
   key, rows align on their content (patience anchors — rows unique on both sides, kept in order —
   and Myers' diff inside each gap, capped at 1,000 edits a gap), and inside each gap rows alike
   enough (half or more of the filled cells equal) pair as **changed**; a row that changed place
   is removed and added, never moved (W-63's hazard: *moved* only when certain). Of two in-order
   runs of the same length, the one whose rows sit nearer their old places wins. Trailing blank
   rows do not count.
5. **Cells** of rows both versions hold differ by value, display text or formula; formulas are
   compared with each relative reference written as an offset from its cell, so a formula that
   only moved with its row is not a change. A new column's filled cells are changes with `was:
   null`. Also reported per sheet: merges added and removed (mapped through the alignment), rows
   and columns newly hidden or shown, the sheet's state, and data-validation and
   conditional-format rule counts when they differ.
6. **The result** is plain data (L9): per sheet a status, the row operations (`added` with its
   values, `removed` after the newer row it followed, `changed`, `moved`), the cell changes (`was`
   and `now`: value, text, formula; `what` differs), counts, and a summary — sheets, rows and cells
   changed (a removed or added sheet's rows count). `applyDiff(a, diff)` rebuilds the newer
   version's values; a key named for one sheet that both versions lack is SP-5901, a key named for
   every sheet is used only where it exists (the sheet carries a `note`).
7. **Speed:** two versions of a 50,000-row, 8-column sheet (500 cells edited, 100 rows inserted,
   100 deleted, 50 moved), and the same sheet with every row changed, each diff in under **500 ms**
   in Node. Recorded 2026-10-19 on an Apple M4 (10 cores, 16 GB, macOS) under a load average of
   14–17 from six other build lanes: unkeyed 120 ms, keyed 119 ms, every row changed 138 ms.
   With `CI` set the time is reported, not asserted.
8. **The comparison in a pane** is the file as loaded (`store.book`) against the base, never the
   pane's edits since; another file loaded into the pane is compared with the same base. The base
   comes from Compare… (a file picker; `.xlsx` or `.csv`) or from the host (`compareWith(store,
   bytes | File | workbook, { name, key, headerRow })`); either way it is read in the page and
   nothing is sent (SR-LAW-11 decision 2). A base that cannot be read is said in the status line.
9. **Tints** (`decorate`, after `styles` and `condfmt`): changed cell amber, added row or column
   and every cell of an added sheet green, moved row blue, a red top border on the row below
   removed rows (bottom border on the last row when they were at the end) — each a
   `--sp-compare-*` custom property with a default that reads on light and dark.
10. **The status line** (`status` slot, View and Edit): *Compared with ‹name›: n sheets · n rows ·
    n cells changed*, and the removed sheets by name.
11. **Keys and buttons** (cell bar, View and Edit): Compare…, Previous change (Alt+Shift+F5), Next
    change (Alt+F5) — VS Code's keys for the same act; F-keys keep ⌥ from changing the key on a Mac
    — and Stop comparing. Stops are sheet-level notes, new columns, added, moved and removed rows
    (the row selected) and changed cells, in sheet, row, column order, wrapping.
12. **The errors list** (L7: every surface shows the same comparison): each change is an error
    of type `compare`, severity `note`, author `compare` — a sheet added or renamed and a sheet's
    structural changes at A1, a column added, a row added or moved (the row), removed rows (the
    row below them), a changed cell (`was … → now …`, formulas named) — at most 2,000 and one note
    for the rest. `found` is the file's text (as for every error) and `expected` what the base
    holds there — the base's text, its formula when only the formula changed, a moved row's old
    row — so the list reads *now → base*. They are written by one function, `publishChanges`, as the `compare` review layer
    (W-51, SR-GRID 5d; `COMPARE_LAYER`): `setErrors(list, { layer: 'compare' })` replaces the
    previous comparison's and leaves every other layer — a person's review included — and undo
    as they are; ids are the pane's next `ERR-n`. With two layers the errors panel's switch
    shows the review and the comparison apart. `@sheetpane/comments` leaves the layer out of a
    download unless `export({ layers })` names it (SR-COMMENTS 3). A removed sheet has no place in the workbook: the status
    line names it.
13. **MCP:** `@sheetpane/mcp`'s `diff_workbooks(base, path, key?, headerRow?, limit?)` runs
    `diffWorkbooks` on two local files, the key for every sheet (SR-MCP).

### Consequences

- **Enforced today:** `packages/compare/test/diff.node.test.ts` — fast-check: a workbook diffed
  with itself is empty; the diff applied to `a` gives `b`'s values for any two workbooks, keyed or
  not; a keyed shuffle is only moves — and the alignment, column, formula, sheet and structure
  cases; `perf.node.test.ts` the budget (decision 7); `fixtures.node.test.ts` the fixtures pair
  (SR-FIXTURES `compare/`); `compare.test.ts` (Chromium) the tints, the status line, the errors
  list, the keys and buttons, Stop comparing and a second file; `packages/mcp/test` the tool's
  golden; the demos' gallery tab *Compare* and its `demo-check` step (SR-BUILD 11a).
- **The layer (W-51, closed with W-63):** `compare.test.ts` checks the changes are the
  `compare` layer, the review its own, undo kept, and the visible layers filtering them;
  comments' `write.test.ts` that the layer is left out unless named.
- **Not done:** a
  removed sheet's changes have no place to be listed (W-55's sheet-level errors would give them
  one); comparing the pane's edits, not the file, is W-64's edits view.

### Alternatives considered

- `daff` as a dependency — rejected: rows only, no sheets, merges or formulas, and SR-LAW-2 asks for
  none where the code is this small.
- Report a reordered row as moved without a key — rejected: equal rows make it a guess (W-63's
  hazard).
- Compare the pane's live values (edits included) — rejected for now: every edit would rewrite the
  errors list; the file against the file is the question asked.

### Reference (required)

- [`packages/compare/`](../packages/compare/) · W-63 · Myers, *An O(ND) Difference Algorithm and
  Its Variations* (1986) · Bram Cohen's patience diff.

### Veto condition

**Reopen this decision if:** a host needs moved rows without a key, the 50,000-row budget fails on
an idle machine, or W-51's layers change how a plugin writes errors.

**How to check it:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project node packages/compare && pnpm exec vitest run --project compare`
